The upper-corner grinder brings two vertical heads down on the two top corners of a box at once and presses the belt on the weld with pads; time and pressure are set on the touch screen by how much weld there is to remove. families.summary: The torch is driven along one axis at a set speed and welds the straight corner seam of bent boxes, cabinets, trays and enclosures in mild steel, stainless steel and aluminum — with a TIG or a plasma source, instead of by hand. The operator places the part on the table with its corner against the external copper squaring guide and presses the lock button: a pneumatic cylinder presses it from inside against the copper guides, which hold the corner square and keep the heat of the part down. Start, and the machine welds the corner with the parameters of the recipe; release, and the next part goes in. The CWS 200 and CWS 300 take parts from 3-15/16 × 3-15/16″ to 59-1/16 × 59-1/16″ with corners 7-7/8″ or 11-13/16″ high; the WELCOR 400 X welds corners up to 15-3/4″ high on parts to 39-3/8 × 39-3/8″.

families.headline: Two axes, X and Y · CWS 300 XY parts to 59″ square · WELCOR 400 XY corners 15-3/4″ on X, 4-5/16″ on Y
families.summary: Here the torch is driven on two axes, X and Y. The CWS 300 XY takes parts from 3-15/16 × 3-15/16″ to 59-1/16 × 59-1/16″ with corners 7-7/8″ to 11-13/16″ high; its touch panel shows the X and Y positions, counts the parts and calls up the recipe. The WELCOR 400 XY welds corners up to 15-3/4″ on X and 4-5/16″ on Y — a seam that runs in two directions, in one cycle — on parts to 39-3/8 × 39-3/8″. The rest works as on the one-axis machines: the part is clamped pneumatically from inside against copper squaring guides, the torch welds at 0 to 47 in/min with a TIG or a plasma source, and the parameters of each part are stored.

families.page_title: Corner welding machines — TIG and plasma corner welders, 1 to 4 axes
families.headline: Four axes, X, Y, Z and torch rotation · laser seam reading · parts to 39-3/8″ square · 0 – 47 in/min
families.summary: The three axes of the WELCOR 400 XYZ and a fourth: the torch is mounted on a rotary actuator that sets its angle in each phase of the weld, from vertical to about 120° as the job needs. Before it welds, the torch runs along the weld line while a laser sensor beside it checks that the edges are straight and how long they are; the machine memorizes the path and then welds it — a self-learning system that finds the corners by itself. Programs are saved for repeat work, the automatic welding program makes the machine easy to run even for operators who are not welders, and the color touch screen draws the welding process to help pick the right parameters. Pneumatic clamping positions the flaps; modular copper pads, matched to the size of the box, carry off the heat and limit burning of the part. Parts from 3-15/16 × 3-15/16″ to 39-3/8 × 39-3/8″, the smallest box 1-15/16″ high; torch path up to 15-3/4 × 1-7/8 × 4-7/16″.

families.summary: The value-line CNC press brake: a welded, stress-relieved mono-block frame, electro-hydraulic servo synchronisation with servo valves and linear scales, a servo-driven pump that only runs while the ram moves, a Delem DA-53Tx control and a servo back gauge on ball screws — the same architecture as the European machines, built to a price that lets a small shop own a real CNC brake. Twenty-five models on one design, from 55 US tons (50 t) × 4 ft to 331 US tons (300 t) × 20 ft: the 110 and 135 t (121 and 149 US tons) × 10 ft machines are the ones most Canadian shops ask for; from 170 t (187 US tons) up the machines have 17.7 – 19.7″ throats, 7.9 – 9.8″ strokes and 18.9 – 22.4″ daylight for deep boxes, with 25 – 40 cc pumps and 13 – 21 kW servo main motors, and the 220 and 250 t (243 and 276 US tons) × 13 ft bend 3/8″ plate the full length. families.summary: Plasma and oxy-fuel cutting leave dross welded to the bottom edge of thick parts, and grinding it off by hand is slow, noisy work. pages.h1: 3D laser cutting machines — five-axis SF3015TD, 5 × 10 ft, 3 to 20 kW
pages.desc: Five-axis 3D fiber laser for formed, stamped, drawn and bent parts and pipe fittings: the SF3015TD with endless C and ±135° A rotation, 5 × 10 ft, 3 to 20 kW.
pages.intro: A 3D laser cuts formed parts — stamped, drawn, hot-stamped or bent — with a five-axis head that follows the surface: it trims edges and cuts holes and slots after forming, where a flat-bed laser cannot reach and a trimming die would cost more than the run. NovoTech sells Senfeng's five-axis SF3015TD in Canada, from the value line: a 3 to 20 kW head with endless C rotation and ±135° A swing over a 5 × 10 ft envelope, on a marble base, with a 180° dual-station rotary table and a fully enclosed cabin. The family below has its full specification table, photos and brochure. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, chiller and offline programming software, installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: SF3015TD five-axis laser: 5 × 10 ft envelope, 27.6″ Z, endless C and ±135° A, 328 ft/min, 3 – 20 kW
Marble base and marble guide rails for accuracy; 180° dual-station rotary table or a servo shuttle table
Offline programming from the 3D model; fully enclosed cabin with interlocked doors and a light curtain
faq: What parts suit a five-axis 3D laser?

Formed parts that a flat-bed laser cannot reach: hot-stamped and cold-pressed automotive parts such as pillars, door rings and bumper beams, drawn covers and housings, pipe fittings and exhaust parts, and stainless metalwork such as pots and trays. The SF3015TD trims edges and cuts holes and slots after forming in place of trimming and piercing dies; it is programmed offline from the 3D model, and its 180° dual-station table loads one part while the other is cut.
What laser power do I need?

Power sets the thickness and the speed. As a guide for mild steel: 3 kW cuts 1/2″, 6 kW 3/4″ (and 1/4″ at over 300 in/min), 12 kW 1″, 20 kW 1-1/4″ and 30 – 40 kW 1-1/2″ and beyond; stainless and aluminum run about 20 – 30 % thinner at the same power, with nitrogen or air assist. Most Canadian job shops buying today choose 6 or 12 kW: thick enough for structural work, fast enough to pay for the machine on thin sheet. Tell us your material mix and we run the cutting chart for you.
What about assist gas and fume extraction?

Oxygen gives the fastest cut and an oxide edge on mild steel; nitrogen a clean, paint-ready edge on all metals; compressed air at 16 bar replaces nitrogen on sheet to about 1/4″ and cuts the gas bill to near zero — the intelligent air-cutting package is an option on both lines. The machines have pneumatic extraction compartments under the table and connect to a dust collector, which we can supply.
What does the machine need on site?

A level floor, 600 V 3-phase (with the transformer we supply) or 480 V, a chiller (included), assist gas, a dust collector and a compressed-air supply for air cutting. A 6 kW 3015 draws about 46 kW in total (Dener's figure for the GFL) and needs roughly 33 × 20 ft with its shuttle table. Delivery, installation and operator training are done by NovoTech from Mississauga, ON, Canada, and the Ontario pre-start health and safety review is prepared by us.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: NovoTech semi-automatic band saws
pages.desc: Value-line hydraulic semi-automatic band saws: BS-315GF full-hydraulic double-miter, BS-460G dual-miter, BS-5030 single-column and the 18″ BS-650GA.
pages.intro: Hydraulic saws for the production floor at value-line prices, led by our best seller — the BS-315GF, a 10-inch double-miter (mitre) saw with hydraulic vise, hydraulic down-feed and hydraulic bow up-lift. A hydraulic cylinder lowers the bow at a dialled-in rate, the bow lifts and the machine stops at the end of the cut. From the 10-inch saws to the 18-inch BS-650GA swivel-head saw, with a single-column touch-screen model (BS-5030) in between. If you are looking for a semi-automatic metal bandsaw, a hydraulic horizontal band saw for metal or an industrial band saw machine with a hydraulic vise, this is the page.
points: BS-315GF: full-hydraulic 10″ double-miter saw — our most popular model
Hydraulic descent, automatic bow return and shut-off on every model
Round capacities from Ø10″ (250 mm) to Ø18″ (460 mm)
faq: What is the difference between a semi-automatic and a fully automatic band saw?

A semi-automatic saw makes one cut per start: it clamps, cuts and lifts the bow, then waits for the operator to feed the next piece. A fully automatic saw also feeds the material to length and repeats the cycle for the programmed quantity — see the value line automatic band saws.
Which value-line saws cut miters on both sides?
The BS-315GF, BS-460G / 460G-JC and BS-650GA swivel to both sides (45° left and right, 60° right); the BS-2114TH cuts angles up to 60° on one side.
What does "full-hydraulic" mean on the BS-315GF?

Hydraulic vise, hydraulic down-feed and hydraulic bow up-lift on one 10-inch machine: the operator loads the bar, presses start and the saw clamps, cuts, lifts the bow and switches off. The gear drive and a bow that swivels to both sides with fast stops at 30°, 45° and 60° complete it.
What does SC mean?

Single column: the BS-5030 guides the bow vertically on a column instead of a pivot, for square straight cuts up to Ø11-3/4″ / 19-3/4″ × 11-3/4″ with a PLC touch screen. Its automatic sister is the BS-5040.
What voltage do these saws run on?
Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V with a CSA-approved electrical panel; 208 V, 240 V or 480 V 3-phase are available on request.

pages.h1: Upcut saws for aluminum extrusions and PVC window profiles
pages.desc: Rising-blade saws for aluminum extrusions and vinyl window profiles, Ø17-11/16″ to Ø25-9/16″ blades, with double-head, glazing bead and miter saws.
pages.intro: An upcut saw (rising-blade saw) raises its blade from under the table through a profile that is already clamped, so the cut is guarded, square and nearly burr-free — the standard saw for aluminum extrusions and PVC (vinyl) window profiles. NovoTech supplies the saws of Plastmak, built in Bursa, Turkey: the SC 401, whose Ø17-11/16″ blade turns from 0° to 180°; the fully automatic SC 402 and SC 403 with Ø21-5/8″ to Ø25-9/16″ blades and hydro-pneumatic feed, for profiles up to 9-3/16 × 12-3/8″; the SC 450 for roller-shutter boxes and lamella packs; the SC 400S and SC 4000S double-head saws, which cut both ends of a frame profile at once, up to 171-5/8″ long; the SC 301 and SC 301S glazing bead saws; and the SC 431, SC 441 and SC 451 miter saws. Supplied with a CSA-approved panel, installed and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. For the shop that cuts aluminum profiles now and then, the NovoTech value-line QCS-400 is a 16″ saw with pneumatic clamping and feed, and the QCS-500A a 20″ saw whose head swivels from 0 to 180° for profiles up to 10-1/4 × 5-1/8″.
points: Upcut saws Ø17-11/16″ – Ø25-9/16″ (450 – 650 mm), automatic from the SC 402, profiles to 9-3/16 × 12-3/8″
Glazing bead, shutter box and miter saws — the whole cutting side of a window shop
faq: What is an upcut saw?

A saw whose blade sits under the table and rises through the profile, which is clamped from above and from the side before the cut. The blade stays covered until it cuts, the profile cannot move, and the cut comes out square and nearly burr-free — which is why aluminum and PVC window shops use upcut saws rather than chop saws. The SC 401, SC 402 and SC 403 are upcut saws; the SC 431, 441 and 451 cut from above.
Which blade size do I need?

The blade decides the largest profile. At 90° the Ø17-11/16″ (450 mm) SC 401 cuts profiles up to 5-5/16″ high and 8-9/16″ wide, the Ø21-5/8″ (550 mm) SC 402 7-1/16 × 10-7/16″, and the SC 403 8-3/16 × 11-5/16″ with its Ø23-5/8″ (600 mm) blade or 9-3/16 × 12-3/8″ with the Ø25-9/16″ (650 mm) one. Most window and door profiles fit the SC 401 or 402; curtain-wall and large door profiles need the SC 403. Send us your largest profile and we will check it against the cutting chart.
Upcut saw or double-head saw?

An upcut saw cuts one end at a time — flexible and inexpensive, enough for a few dozen windows a shift. A double-head saw cuts both ends at once, to a length typed in or read from a barcode, with both heads tilting to 45°: the SC 400S and SC 4000S roughly double a shop's output and take measuring errors out of the job. Many shops run a double-head saw for frames and an upcut saw for mullions and odd cuts.
Do they cut aluminum as well as PVC?

Yes. The SC 402, 403, 400S and 4000S cut both, with hydro-pneumatic or hydro-check feeds that keep aluminum cuts clean and spray or oil cooling for the blade; the SC 401 slows its feed in aluminum and takes an optional cooling device and hydro-check. Fit a blade made for the material you cut.
What do the model names mean?

SC — often written SC — is Plastmak's model prefix. Across the range, 1xx are welders, 2xx end mills and notchers, 3xx bead saws, 4xx saws, 5xx routers and CNCs, 6xx corner cleaners, 9xx crimpers and 1000s conveyors; an S marks the servo or upgraded version, as on the SC 400S and SC 4000S.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.desc: American-style punches and dies with the .500″ tang — 88° straight and gooseneck, 28° – 30° acute punches, 1V dies V .375 – .875″, 36″ and 18″.
pages.intro: EUROSTAMP punches and dies with the American tang — .500″ (12.7 mm) wide with the safety lip — for the American-style clamping found on most press brakes built in North America. Punches stand 3.779″ (96 mm) high: 88° straight and 88° / 85° gooseneck punches for 90° air bending, 30° and 28° acute punches for hemming and acute angles, and a 5.125″ acute gooseneck. The dies all share a 1.937″ (49.2 mm) working height: 88° dies V .375 to .750″ and 30° – 34° acute dies V .375 to .875″. Every tool comes in 36″ and 18″ lengths and a 35.75″ sectioned set, each with its own part number. For press brakes with European-style (Amada-Promecam) clamping there is a Z1 intermediate that takes these punches.
points: Punches 88°, 85°, 30° and 28°, 3.779″ (96 mm) high — tang .500″ with safety lip
36″ (914.4 mm), 18″ (457.2 mm) and 35.75″ (908 mm) sectioned lengths

faq: Will American-style tooling fit my press brake?

It fits press brakes with American-style clamping — a .500″ tang in a clamp bar, used on most press brakes built in North America. Measure the tang slot of your upper clamp and lower die holder, or send us a photo of a tool you use now, and we confirm. If your brake has European-style clamping, see the European punches and dies pages — or, to use American-style punches on it, the Z1 intermediate on this page, for brakes built for Z1 intermediates.
Why do the drawings say the dimensions are in inches?

American-style tooling is designed in inches. The tables give each dimension in decimal inches with the exact metric value, and the part numbers carry the length in millimetres: 0914 for 36″, 0457 for 18″ and 0908 for the 35.75″ sectioned set.

pages.h1: Tube rollers, pipe rollers and angle rolls — roll benders for profiles
pages.desc: Tube rollers, pipe rollers and angle rolls sold, installed and supported in Canada: hydraulic roll benders from a 2 HP bench bender to HEB 600 beam benders.
pages.intro: An angle roll (also called a roll bender, section bender, profile bender, ring roller or tube roller) pushes a bar, angle, pipe, tube or beam between three rolls to bend it into an arc, a ring or a spiral — the machine behind curved handrails, tank stiffener rings, rolled flanges, arched trusses and coiled heating pipe. The NovoTech premium line covers the complete range: the motorized PK 30 and PK 35 for small flat bar, angle and tube, the hydraulic HPK 40 to HPK 120 section and pipe benders with digital readouts, hydraulic guides and optional NC control, the HPK DP heavy-duty beam benders for channel, I-beam and H-beam up to HEB 600, and the TC-42 NC coiling machine for variable-pitch tube coils. Every machine rolls horizontally or vertically, comes with a standard roll set and takes pipe, tube, angle and special profile rolls; capacity charts for each model are on this page. Sold with a CSA-approved panel, parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada. NovoTech's value-line ring rollers, built in China, add motorized RBM and HRBM profile benders with Ø13/16 to 2-1/2″ shafts — the H models with a hydraulic top roll — the ETR-50 electric tube roller and the CRB-76 decorative ring roller.
points: PK 30 / PK 35 motorized and HPK 40 – 120 hydraulic angle rolls — pipe to NPS 5, angle to L 4-3/4 × 4-3/4 × 1/2″
HPK 160 – 360 DP heavy-duty beam benders — IPN 600, UPN 600, HEB 600, pipe to NPS 16
Digital readouts standard; NC control, hydraulic lateral guides and spiral crane optional; capacity chart per model
NovoTech value line: RBM / HRBM motorized profile benders Ø13/16 – 2-1/2″ shafts, ETR-50 tube roller, CRB-76 decorative roller
faq: Angle roll, roll bender, section bender, ring roller, tube roller — are these the same machine?

Yes. All describe the three-roll machine on this page: two driven rolls hold the section and the third roll pushes it into a curve, and a ring is finished by running the piece round again. Each profile — flat bar, angle, square bar, pipe, tube, channel, beam — has its own roll set; the capacity chart under each model lists the largest section it rolls and the smallest diameter it rolls it to.
How do I read the capacity chart?

Find your profile in the left column and read the largest section the machine can roll and, after the arrow, the minimum outside diameter it can roll that section to. A second entry gives a smaller section with its tighter minimum diameter. 'Standard rolls' profiles are rolled with the roll set supplied with the machine; 'optional rolls' need the matching roll set. The chart is for mild steel of 37,700 psi yield; stainless, aluminum and high-strength sections need the next model up.
Which angle roll do I need for 2″ pipe or 2 × 2 × 1/4″ angle?

The HPK 50 rolls NPS 2 pipe to a Ø39″ ring and L 2 × 2 × 1/4″ angle leg-out to Ø24″; the HPK 60 does the same with more margin and takes NPS 3 pipe and L 2-3/4 × 2-3/4 × 1/4″. For a smaller ring in the same section, or for daily production, step up one size — the minimum diameter shrinks and the rolls last longer.
Horizontal or vertical — what is the difference?

The HPK 40 to HPK 120 and the PK 35 work in both positions. Vertical takes less floor space and suits short pieces and rings; horizontal lets long bars, pipe and beams run out over the floor on supports and is the only position on the HPK DP machines. Lateral guide rolls (manual or hydraulic) keep the section square to the rolls and stop twist on angle and channel.
Can these machines roll spirals and coils?

Yes. Every HPK with the optional spiral bending crane rolls spiral staircases, stringers and heating coils; the TC-42 NC is the dedicated coiling machine that rolls variable-pitch coils with a straight elbow at each end in one automatic pass.
Do you supply the rolls for my profile?

A standard roll set comes with every machine and rolls flat bar, square bar and tee. Pipe, tube, angle, channel and special profile rolls are quoted to your section drawing and shipped with the machine or added later; Delrin rolls are available for polished stainless and aluminum.
Premium-line angle roll or value-line ring roller?

The premium-line PK and HPK angle rolls are built in Turkey for daily structural work — heavier frames, larger shafts, NC options and capacities to 6″ angle. The value-line RBM and HRBM ring rollers are lighter and lower in price for the fabrication, railing and ornamental shop: flat bar, angle, channel, tee and tube to 4-3/4 × 1″ flat on the HRBM65, with one combination roll set for every profile.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Bekamak automatic band saws
pages.desc: Bekamak BMSO automatic feed band saws: roller-feed, encoder and servo shuttle-vise saws to Ø17-3/8″ (440 mm), the BMSO 320S with touch screen, and miter saws.
pages.intro: Set the length and the quantity, load the bar and walk away. Bekamak's BMSO saws feed the material — with driven rollers, an encoder-measured feed or a servo shuttle vise — clamp, cut and count until the job is done. From Ø9″ to Ø17-3/8″ (230–440 mm), including automatic single- and double-miter models with NC job lists. For buyers searching for an automatic metal cutting bandsaw, a CNC band saw machine or an industrial horizontal band saw for metal with automatic feeding, these are the models NovoTech sells and supports in Canada.
points: Roller feed, encoder feed or servo shuttle-vise feed
NC job lists: length × quantity
Automatic single- and double-miter models
faq: Roller feed or shuttle vise — which is better?

Roller feed (BMSO 230–440, BMSO E) is simple and fast for bar and tube in straight cuts; the encoder versions measure the fed length for better accuracy. A shuttle vise — servo-driven on the BMSO 320S, the BMSO GS/GLS and all CS/CGS double-column saws, motorized on the compact 270DGS — grips the bar and moves it to the programmed length, giving ±0.1 mm repeatability on the servo models and reliable feeding of bundles and short remnants.
How many lengths can I program?
The NC control on the servo-feed models stores a job list of several length-and-quantity pairs, so one bar can be cut into different parts without re-programming.
What happens at the end of the bar?

The saw stops when the remaining length is shorter than the next part or the feed vise reaches its limit, and the counter shows how many pieces were cut. Remnant length depends on the model — typically 3–6 in (80–150 mm).
Do automatic saws need a roller table?
A short infeed roller table is included on the BMSO E models; a 10 ft (3 m) manual or motorized roller table is optional on the others and is strongly recommended for bars longer than about 6 ft.

pages.h1: Automatic cold saws — carbide and HSS production saws to Ø11-3/4″
pages.desc: Automatic circular cold saws sold in Canada: the CSM CT325 servo-feed saw for tube and bundles to Ø4″, Bekamak BMDO XS carbide saws and HSS production saws.
pages.intro: An automatic cold saw feeds the bar, clamps it, cuts and counts by itself: the operator loads the bars, programs the lengths and quantities and the saw runs the batch. NovoTech sells two lines in Canada, all on this page: CSM's CT325 hydraulic circular saw with a servo carriage, cutting tube and bundles to Ø4″ in three spindle-speed ranges; and Bekamak's automatic production saws — the BMDO XS high-speed carbide (TCT) cold saws that cut solid bar to Ø6-1/4″ from a 20 ft magazine loader with servo feeding, the OPUS 300 with a Ø35-7/16″ (900 mm) carbide blade and a 50 HP spindle for solid bar to Ø11-3/4″, and the BMDO CS HSS saws for tube and bar to Ø4″ with a servo gripper feed and touch-screen control. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. For manual and semi-automatic saws, see the cold saws. CSA-approved panels and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: CSM CT325: hydraulic down-feed, servo carriage to ±.004″, tube and bundles to Ø4″ in three spindle-speed ranges
Bekamak BMDO XS carbide saws: solid bar Ø3/8″ – 6-1/4″ at up to 920 ft/min, servo feed, 20 ft magazine loader — and the OPUS 300 for bar to Ø11-3/4″
Bekamak BMDO CS HSS saws: tube and bar to Ø4″, servo gripper feed to ±.004″, several lengths per bar
faq: What does an automatic cold saw do by itself?

You load bars in the magazine (BMDO XS) or on the roller table (BMDO CS), program the lengths and quantities, and the saw feeds each bar with a servo gripper, clamps it hydraulically, cuts, counts and moves on to the next length — to ±.004″ on the CS and with a 60 mm remnant on the XS.
TCT carbide or HSS cold saw?

A carbide (TCT) blade runs at 130–920 ft/min and is the fastest way to cut solid steel bar in production — the Bekamak BMDO XS saws and the Ø11-3/4″ OPUS 300 are built around it, with servo feeding and a magazine loader for unattended runs. HSS blades run slower (22–130 ft/min on the BMDO CS) and are the choice for tube, thin walls and mixed work; the XS saws accept HSS blades for tube as well.
What is the CSM CT325 for?

Cutting tube to length in production, single or in bundles: the CT325 clamps hydraulically, feeds with a servo carriage to ±.004″ at 39 in/s and feeds the blade down hydraulically through planetary gears, with a PLC touch-screen and a pedestal with emergency stop. The L, M and H types differ only in spindle speed — steel, stainless and alloy, aluminum and non-ferrous. It is the saw CSM builds into its bending cells, and stands just as well on its own.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.desc: Automatic rebar processing lines in Canada: the SLS 12 CNC stirrup bender from coil, MATRIX 55 shear lines and the SYNCLONE 45S double bender, with videos.
pages.intro: PLC and servo-controlled lines for rebar shops and precast plants: the SLS 12 CNC stirrup bender that straightens, bends and cuts from coil, the MATRIX 55 and 55S shear lines that cut bundles to programmed lengths, and the SYNCLONE 45S double bender that bends both ends of a 40 ft bar in one cycle. Installed, commissioned and supported in Canada by NovoTech.
points: Stirrups from 1/4″–1/2″ coil at 1250°/s with 50+ shapes pre-loaded
Shear lines cutting up to 35 bars at once, ± 1/8″ accuracy
Servo double bender for bars up to Ø1-5/8″ (42 mm) and 40 ft long
faq: What does a shear line replace in a rebar shop?

A MATRIX 55 line cuts whole bundles to programmed lengths — up to 35 × Ø5/16″ or 11 × Ø1″ bars at once — and discharges them to bins, so one operator does the work of a cutting crew measuring and cutting bar by bar. The 55S version adds automatic bins and discharge to both sides, which GMS rates as eliminating 2–3 operators.
What coil sizes does the SLS 12 run?
1/4″, 5/16″, 3/8″ and 1/2″ (6, 8, 10 and 12 mm) wire, processed two strands at a time, with length tolerance of ± 0.039–0.079 in and bending tolerance of ± 1°.
What power, air and floor space do the lines need?

The SLS 12 needs about 67 × 197 in plus two decoilers of 83 × 85 in each, a compressor at 120–150 psi and 24 HP of servo and AC motors. The MATRIX 55 draws 21–25 HP total and the SYNCLONE 45S 34 HP; both are supplied for 600 V 3-phase, with 208, 240 or 480 V on request. Send us your floor plan and we will lay the line out for you.
Can the SYNCLONE 45S work as two separate benders?

Yes. The stationary and the moving bender can each be used on its own for small shapes, or together as a double bender for bars up to 40 ft (12 m) long. The minimum distance between the two heads is 3.3 ft (1 m), less with bending tools.
Who installs and commissions the line in Canada?

NovoTech installs, commissions and trains your operators on site, and keeps spare parts and technical support available in Canada. Remote connection for diagnostics is available on the MATRIX and SYNCLONE lines.

pages.h1: Band saw blades for metal — bimetal M42 and carbide, welded to length
pages.desc: WIKUS band saw blades welded to length in Canada: the MARATHON M42 bimetal blade for every shop saw and the FUTURA carbide-tipped blade for production sawing.
pages.intro: A band saw blade is the one consumable that decides what a band saw machine can do: the right cutting material, tooth form and tooth pitch cut faster, straighter and longer than the wrong one on any saw. NovoTech supplies the two WIKUS blades that Canadian shops run most — made in Germany by the world's largest band saw blade maker and welded to the length of your machine in Mississauga, ON, Canada. The MARATHON® M42 bimetal blade is the everyday blade for profiles, tube, bundles and solid bar on any horizontal or vertical band saw; the FUTURA® carbide-tipped blade is the production blade for solid steel, stainless and aluminum on the Bekamak saws and any machine with a carbide package. Both come in every width from 1/2″ to 3-1/8″ and in every tooth pitch; the rest of the WIKUS program — coated PREMIUM blades, X3000® blades for difficult alloys, the NE blades for aluminum and copper, CBN-coated blades for hardened steel — is available to order.
points: MARATHON® M42 bimetal blade, 1/2″ to 3-1/8″ wide — profiles, bundles and solid material to 145,000 psi on any saw
FUTURA® carbide-tipped blade, 1-1/16″ to 3-1/8″ wide — two to three times the cutting rate on solid steel, stainless and aluminum
Every blade welded and annealed to your machine's length in Canada; the complete WIKUS program available to order
faq: Bimetal or carbide — which band saw blade do I need?

The MARATHON M42 bimetal blade (M42 high-speed-steel teeth on a spring-steel back) is the right blade for a fabrication shop: structural profiles, tube, bundles and solid bar up to about 145,000 psi, mixed materials, on any band saw. The FUTURA carbide-tipped blade cuts solid material two to three times faster and lasts several times longer, but it wants a rigid saw with enough motor power and band tension — the Bekamak production saws and most saws with a carbide package. If most of your cutting is solid bar, plate strips or stainless on such a saw, the FUTURA pays for itself; for everything else, the MARATHON.
How do I choose the tooth pitch?

By the contact length — the width of material the blade is in at any moment: 4 to 12 teeth should be in the cut. Thin-wall tube and small profiles need a fine pitch (10–14 TPI), bar of 2 to 4 inches a 3–4 or 2–3 TPI blade, and large solid material 1.4–2 TPI and coarser. A variable pitch (for example 3–4 TPI) runs quieter and resists vibration on profiles and bundles; a constant pitch is used on uniform solid material. Each blade's table on this page lists the pitches available in every width and the contact length each pitch is meant for.
Which blade width and length fits my saw?

The width and thickness are set by the saw's wheels and guides — 1″ × 0.035″ on most 10″ to 13″ shop saws, 1-1/4″ × 0.042″ and 1-1/2″ × 0.050″ on the mid-size automatic saws, 2″ to 3-1/8″ on the double-column production saws. The length is the loop length of your machine; we weld the blade to it from coil. Send the saw make and model and we look it up.
Can the FUTURA carbide blade run on my saw?

On the Bekamak BMSO and BMSY automatic saws, the double-column saws and any saw with a carbide package (high band tension, rigid guides, enough motor power) — yes. On a lighter saw, stay with the MARATHON M42, or ask us about the TAURUS, a carbide blade set and ground to run without the carbide package.
Do you supply other WIKUS blades?

Yes — the complete WIKUS metal-cutting program is available to order: the economical PRIMAR and the high-performance SKALAR and SELEKTA GS bimetal blades, the coated PREMIUM versions, the X3000® blades for stainless, nickel and titanium alloys, the DUROSET and TAURUS carbide blades, the FUTURA VA, 718, NE and SN specialists for stainless, superalloys, aluminum and hardened parts, and the CUBOGRIT® CBN blades for hardened steel above 55 HRC. Tell us the material and the saw and we propose the blade; data sheets on request.
Do you stock blades and weld them in Canada?

Yes — the common widths of the MARATHON M42 are stocked as coil in Mississauga, ON, Canada and welded and annealed to your length; the FUTURA and the rest of the program are welded to order. Tell us the saw, the materials you cut and the sizes, and we propose the blade and the pitch — and we are happy to run a test blade on a difficult job.

pages.h1: Metal cutting band saws — horizontal, vertical and automatic, to 87″
pages.desc: Metal cutting band saws sold, installed and supported in Canada: horizontal manual, semi-automatic and automatic, double column and vertical saws, Ø9″ to 87″.
pages.intro: Horizontal metal cutting band saws — metal bandsaws for steel, stainless, aluminum and other metals — for fabricators, machine shops and steel service centres across Canada, in two clearly separated lines: the premium Bekamak range built in Turkey, and NovoTech's own value line. Whether you are searching for a manual band saw for metal, a semi-automatic hydraulic bandsaw, an automatic CNC band saw machine or an industrial double column saw for heavy bar and bundles or a vertical band saw for contour cuts, blocks and plate, every machine is here with specifications in inches and millimetres, a CSA-approved panel, spare parts and technical support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Premium line: Bekamak, Ø9″ to 87″ (230–2200 mm)
Value line: NovoTech, Ø10″ to 23-5/8″ (250–600 mm) — semi-automatic, automatic, double-column and vertical
Manual (Bekamak), semi-automatic, automatic, double-column and vertical saws
Band saw buying guide, blade selection and troubleshooting chart on this page
faq: What is the difference between the Premium and Value lines?

Premium-line saws are built by Bekamak in Turkey with European components and the heaviest construction in their class. Value-line saws carry the NovoTech name: proven designs built to our specification at a lower price. Each line has its own pages on this site so you can compare like with like. Both lines come with a CSA-approved electrical panel, a 1-year warranty and spare parts and technical support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
Band saw or bandsaw — is there a difference?

No. Bandsaw (one word) and band saw (two words) are the same machine: a continuous toothed steel band running over two wheels. Horizontal metal cutting band saws — most of the machines on this page — cut bar, tube, profile and plate to length; vertical band saws run the blade upright to slice plates and blocks. Google treats both spellings alike, and so do we.
How do I choose the size of a band saw?

Start with the largest round or rectangular stock you cut regularly and add about 1–2 in (25–50 mm) of clearance. Bekamak model numbers give the round capacity in millimetres (BMSY 440 = 440 mm) and NovoTech value-line model numbers give it in inches (BS-650GA = 18″). Then decide how much automation you need — manual, semi-automatic or automatic — and whether you cut miters. The buying guide on this page walks through each choice.
Which saws can cut bundles of tube or bar?

Semi-automatic and automatic saws with a hydraulic top clamp can cut bundles; the double-column CS and CGS NC models and the Bekamak XS line are designed for bundle cutting with servo feeding. Ask us for the bundle size of the model you are considering.
Do the saws come with a blade and coolant system?
Yes — every band saw ships with a bi-metal blade, an electric coolant pump and a blade brush. We stock replacement blades for all sizes in Mississauga, ON, Canada.
Can I get a saw for 208 V, 240 V or 480 V?
Three-phase saws are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request. Some small manual saws are available in single-phase.
Do you install and train?
Yes. Installation and operator training are available across Canada, and spare parts, blades and technical support are handled from our Mississauga, ON, Canada location.

pages.h1: Bead rollers — motorized and hydraulic beading machines, sheet to 8 ga
pages.desc: Hydraulic and motorized bead roller machines for sheet to 8 ga, sold in Canada: HIBKS, IBKS, IKM and IKMP with beading, swaging and flanging roll sets.
pages.intro: Bead rollers — also called beading machines, rotary machines or swagers — form stiffening beads, wired edges, flanges, crimps and seams in sheet metal for HVAC ducts, drums, tanks, buckets and architectural work. ISITAN builds them motorized and hydraulic — from the IKM and IKMP cast-iron bead rollers with foot-pedal control to the HIBKS 4.0, whose hydraulic top roll beads 8 ga steel under constant pressure. Every machine comes with its sets of standard rolls, a CSA-approved panel and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada. NovoTech's value-line bead rollers, built in China, add ETB beading machines to 8 ga, RM24 – RM42 deep-throat bead rollers with variable-speed drive for auto body panels, and for round duct the RM18E power beading machine and the LQ15 slitting and bending machine.
points: Hydraulic HIBKS and motorized IBKS for sheet to 8 ga (4 mm)
Motorized IKM / IKMP with 4 speeds or pneumatic top shaft
Standard roll sets (4 to 8 per machine) and the roll spanner key included; extra sets made to order
NovoTech value line: ETB beading machines 18 – 8 ga, RM24 / 36 / 42 motorized deep-throat bead rollers
Round duct: RM18E power beading machine, 15 ga; LQ15 slitting and bending machine, 16 ga × 47″
faq: Bead roller, beading machine, rotary machine or swager — what is the difference?

They are the same machine under different names: two shaft-mounted rolls that form a profile in sheet metal as it is turned through them. "Bead roller" is the common North American term, "swager" the older sheet-metal trade word, "rotary machine" the HVAC term. The roll sets decide what it does — beading, wiring, crimping, flanging, burring or trimming.
Which rolls are included?

Every ISITAN bead roller ships with its standard roll sets — 4 sets (S1–S4) on the HIBKS / IBKS 4.0 and 2.5, 3 on the IBKS 1.8, 8 sets on the IKM 1.2 and IKMP 1.2 — plus the roll spanner key. Extra sets (E1–E8) and rolls for special jobs are made to order; tell us the profile you need.
Hydraulic or motorized top roll?

On the IBKS the operator sets the gap between the rolls by hand and the motor turns them. On the HIBKS the top roll is moved hydraulically, so the pressure stays constant through the bead and deep beads in 8 ga steel are formed in one pass with the foot pedal — the choice for production work and heavier sheet.
What is throat depth?
The distance from the rolls to the frame: it sets how far from the sheet edge a bead can be formed. The IBKS 1.8 has an 11″ throat for beads deep into a panel; the HIBKS / IBKS 4.0 7.9″.
Which throat depth for auto body panels?

The throat is how far from the edge of the panel the bead can go: 24″ reaches the centre of a 48″ panel, 36″ and 42″ reach into floor pans, hoods and truck beds. The RM-H models also have a 4″ high throat so formed panels clear the frame. For duct, ends of tanks and edge beads, the 8 – 12″ throat of the ETB beading machines is enough.
What voltage do bead rollers run on?
Motorized models are supplied for 600 V 3-phase with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request and 240 V single-phase on the 1–2 HP models.

pages.h1: Metal belt grinders, disc sanders and bench grinders
pages.desc: Belt grinders for metal with 2 – 8″ belts: pedestal, floor and wide-belt grinders, 2 × 72 knife grinders, combination grinders, 12 – 20″ disc sanders.
pages.intro: Belt grinders are the finishing machines of the fabrication shop: they take the burr off a cut, blend a weld, square an end and put a chamfer on an edge faster than a hand grinder and with a flatter result. NovoTech's value-line grinders are built in China to our specification: pedestal belt grinders with 3″ and 6″ belts up to 5.5 HP, a mobile floor grinder for weld seams, wide-belt grinders with 4″ and 8″ belts, knife and tool grinders, combination machines with a belt, a disc and a wheel on one motor, disc sanders to 20″, bench grinders and wire-wheel machines, end-surface grinders and the dust collectors that keep metal dust out of the shop. Parts and belts from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Pedestal belt grinders 3 × 79″ and 6 × 79″, 4 – 5.5 HP, to 6,693 ft/min; dust collector built in on the HB models
Wide-belt grinders 4″ and 8″, mobile floor grinder, knife grinders, combination belt / disc / wheel machines
Disc sanders 12″ and 20″, bench grinders 8 – 10″, MD-380 end-surface grinders, metal dust collectors 494 – 650 CFM
faq: Which belt width — 2″, 3″, 4″, 6″ or 8″?

2″ belts (2 × 72″, 2 × 79″) are for knives, tools and detail work; 3″ is the all-round width for deburring and blending in the fabrication shop; 4″ and 6″ belts grind wider parts flat and last longer; 8″ belts are for flat sanding of wide parts and for radius grinding. Most shops start with a 3″ or 6″ pedestal grinder and add a disc sander for flat faces.
What belt speed for steel, stainless and aluminum?

Around 5,000 – 6,500 ft/min for steel and stainless with zirconia or ceramic belts; slower — 2,500 – 4,000 ft/min — for aluminum, for heat-sensitive parts and for fine finishing. The two-speed and variable-speed grinders (S-150, SDD75, BGM-50, SP-2) cover both.
Belt grinder or disc sander?

A belt grinder removes metal faster, grinds radii on the contact wheel and runs cooler because the belt is long; a disc sander gives a flat face and an accurate angle against its table — chamfers for welding, squaring ends, deburring flat parts. The combination machines (SP-6, BTM250) put both on one stand.
Do I need a dust collector for metal grinding?

Grinding dust settles everywhere and is a health and housekeeping problem; a collector at the machine keeps it out of the air. Use a collector made for metal — sparks reach the filter — and never connect the same collector to a woodworking machine: wood dust and hot metal sparks are a fire hazard. The DVS14 and DC650 are metal-only collectors; for heavy production the WD-1800 wet collector is on the deburring machines page.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Box and pan brakes — finger brakes from 12″ to 13 ft, 22 to 12 gauge
pages.desc: Box and pan brakes (finger brakes) sold in Canada: hand-operated brakes from 12″ to 157″ in 22 – 12 ga and heavy brakes that fold 14 ga boxes, with fingers.
pages.intro: A box and pan brake (finger brake) is a sheet metal brake whose upper clamping blade is made of removable fingers: take the fingers out where the sides of a box come up and the leaf folds all four sides of a box or a pan; with every finger in place it works as a straight brake. NovoTech sells four kinds in Canada, all on this page: hand-operated box and pan brakes from a 12″ bench model to 157″, in 22 to 12 ga; heavy box and pan brakes from 52 to 100″ with 2, 3 and 4″ fingers that fold 14 ga boxes 9″ deep; box and pan folding machines with segmented blades — the PBB A and 3SH foot-clamp folders and the TSBS and MFS heavy folders — in 20 to 14 ga over 40 to 119″; and hydraulic box and pan brakes that clamp and fold 14 ga over 52 and 100″ from a foot pedal. Each family below has its full specification table, photos and the finger sets supplied. NovoTech's value-line brakes are built in China to our specification, with parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Hand-operated box and pan brakes 12 – 157″, 22 to 12 ga mild steel, removable fingers in 1 – 6″ widths
Hydraulic box and pan brakes 52″ and 100″: 14 ga, foot-pedal clamping and folding
Heavy brakes 52 – 100″ with 2, 3 and 4″ finger sets — boxes to 9″ deep in 14 ga; counterweighted leaf
Box and pan folding machines 40 – 119″, 20 – 14 ga: segmented blades, foot or lever clamping
faq: Box and pan brake or straight hand brake?

A straight (hand) brake has a one-piece clamping blade: the best choice for long straight bends such as flashing, trim and duct panels, and a little stiffer for its length. A box and pan brake has a blade of removable fingers, so it also folds the four sides of a box or a pan; with all the fingers in place it does everything the straight brake does. Most shops that make boxes, pans, enclosures and ducts buy the box and pan brake; the straight brakes are on the hand brake page.
How deep a box can I fold?

The box depth is limited by the height of the fingers and the clearance behind the clamping beam: the standard box and pan brakes fold boxes up to about the finger height (2 – 3″), the heavy brakes with 4″ fingers fold 14 ga boxes 9″ deep, and for boxes of any depth a magnetic brake — which has no beam frame at the ends — is the machine. The maximum depth per model is in the specification table.
How are the capacities rated, and what about stainless and aluminum?

Capacities are given in gauge of mild steel over the full bending length. Stainless steel bends at about two gauges lighter (a 16 ga brake takes 20 ga stainless), aluminum at about two gauges heavier. Bending at less than full length lets a brake take somewhat heavier sheet; folding heavier material than rated bends the beams permanently.
Which finger sets come with the machine?

A full set of fingers that adds up to the bending length is in the crate, in widths from 1″ to 6″ (2, 3 and 4″ on the heavy brakes), so any combination of box sides can be made; extra fingers and narrow 1/2″ fingers are available. Fingers are hardened and ground on the bending edge and can be reversed for a second edge.
Can a brake fold painted or coated sheet without marking it?

Yes — that is one of the reasons to fold instead of press-brake bending. The sheet is clamped and the leaf swings around the clamp edge without sliding over a die; a strip of protective film on the sheet keeps pre-painted and stainless finishes perfect.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Bystronic and LVD-style press brake tooling — punches and dies
pages.desc: Bystronic / Beyeler type R and RF-A punches, flattening blades and dies; LVD-style punches and dies V6 – V120 to 340 t/m — made in Italy, DXF profiles.
pages.intro: EUROSTAMP tooling for two clamping systems with their own tangs. Bystronic and Beyeler press brakes with type R, RF and RF-A clamping take the punches here — straight and acute, gooseneck, sash and 24° flattening blades, 155 to 250 mm (6.10 – 9.84″) high — and the 55 – 65 mm dies from V6 to V60. LVD press brakes take the LVD-style punches 196 mm high and dies 90 or 130 mm high from V6 to V120, rated up to 340 t/m (114 US t/ft). Tell us the clamping of your brake and we confirm the tang; the DXF profiles are on the page.
points: Bystronic type R and RF-A punches 6.10 – 9.84″ (155 – 250 mm), flattening blades, dies V .24 – 2.36″
LVD-style punches 7.72″ (196 mm) and dies V .24 – 4.72″, 90 and 130 mm high, rated to 114 US t/ft
500 / 1,000 mm and 510 mm lengths, sectioned sets for Bystronic; DXF profiles
faq: Type R or RF-A — which do I need?

They are two Bystronic / Beyeler clamping systems with different tangs and punch heights — type R punches here are 155 mm high, RF-A punches 175 mm, and the 250 mm punches fit both. Look at the clamp or at the marking on a punch you already use, or send us a photo, and we match it.
Can I use European-style tooling on my Bystronic or LVD brake?

Yes, with adapters: the upper adapters 4192 (type R), 4193 (type S) and 4214 (RF-A) take European-style punches on a Beyeler ram, 4143 – 4146 on an LVD ram, and the lower adapters 4301, 4302 and 4304 / 4305 do the same for dies. They are on the holders and adapters page.
Can we get the tools as DXF files for our CNC?

Yes — every tool in these tables that has a DXF link can be downloaded straight from the page: the profile drawn in millimetres, ready to import into the tool library of a Delem, ESA or Cybelec control or into offline bending software. For the few tools without one, ask us and we get the drawing from EUROSTAMP.

pages.h1: C-frame hydraulic presses — open-gap presses, 22 to 276 US tons
pages.desc: C-frame hydraulic presses sold in Canada: premium-line CFS, enclosed CFSS and CFDD deep drawing C-frame presses from 33 to 276 US tons, value line from 22.
pages.intro: A C-frame (gap-frame) hydraulic press is open on three sides: small dies go in and out quickly, the operator reaches the part from the front and both sides, and the press takes less floor space than an H-frame of the same force — the press for punching, blanking and forming with small dies, press-fitting and assembly. NovoTech sells two lines in Canada, all on this page: the premium line, built in Turkey on a welded monoblock frame with a chrome-plated cylinder and a T-slotted table, 33 to 276 US tons — the CFS with a pressure transmitter, light barrier and two-hand control, the CFSS with the work area enclosed by guards and a light barrier, and the CFDD for deep drawing, with a die cushion of 11 to 110 US tons and an ejector that lifts the drawn part out; and the value line, built in China — the HP-C presses from 22 to 110 US tons, open on three sides for assembling and dismantling large parts. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. For larger tables and tonnages, see the H-frame presses. Parts, installation and service from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Premium line: CFS single action, CFSS enclosed and CFDD deep drawing C-frame presses, 33 – 276 US tons, 15.7″ stroke
T-slotted tables to 43.3 × 23.6″; two-hand control and light barriers; die cushion 11 – 110 US tons with ejector on the CFDD
NovoTech value line: HP-C C-frame presses 22 – 110 US tons, tables 15.7 × 11.8″ to 31.5 × 23.6″
faq: C-frame or H-frame?

A C-frame press is open on three sides, so small dies go in and out quickly, the part is easy to reach and the press takes less floor space. The open throat deflects slightly under load, which limits the table size and the force — the premium-line C-frame range stops at 276 US tons. For deep drawing large parts, long dies or more force, an H-frame press is stiffer and takes larger tables.
CFS, CFSS or CFDD?

All three share the welded monoblock frame, chrome-plated cylinder and T-slotted table, from 33 to 276 US tons with a 15.7″ stroke. The CFS is the simpler press with a pressure transmitter, light barrier and two-hand control. The CFSS encloses the work area with guards and a light barrier for production with smaller dies. The CFDD adds a die cushion of 11 to 110 US tons in the lower table and an ejector, for deep drawing on a C-frame.
Single action or double action — what is a die cushion?

A single action press has one ram. A double action (deep drawing) press adds a die cushion in the lower table — a second cylinder that holds the blank holder with its own programmed force — so a flat blank can be drawn into a deep cup, pan or housing without wrinkling. The HDD H-frame and CFDD C-frame presses have the cushion built in; it is an option on the HCFP column press.
Can the press be built to my die?

Yes — every series of the premium line is built to order in the table size, stroke, daylight and tonnage the die needs, from a 33 US ton C-frame to a 3,307 US ton H-frame, with quick die change, die loading arms, ejector, heated platens or a die cushion as required. Send us the die drawing and the cycle you need and we quote the press around it.
Premium-line or value-line press?

The premium-line shop and production presses are built in Turkey with European hydraulics and Siemens controls, for daily production work, straightening lines and custom sizes. The value-line presses are built in China for the repair shop, the maintenance department and lighter production — the same tonnages at a lower price, with built-on or separate power units.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Circle shears — sheet metal circle cutting and flanging machines
pages.desc: Circle shears cutting discs and rings to Ø78.7″ in 3/16″ plate, and tank-head cutting and flanging machines for dished and elliptical heads to Ø15 ft.
pages.intro: Circle cutting machines (circle shears, circle cutters) cut round blanks and rings from sheet for tank heads, fan housings, flanges, lids and gaskets; a flanging machine then turns the edge of the disc up for a dished or flat tank head. ISITAN's IDK series runs from the motorized IDK-1.8 to the hydraulic IDK-5 cutting 78.7″ discs in 3/16″ steel. The SDK 6 and SDK 8 cut and flange dished heads up to Ø15 ft in 5/16″ plate on the same head, and the EFM 6 does the same for elliptical heads. Sold with CSA-approved panels and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. NovoTech's value-line circle shears, built in China, add the MCS-1250E motorized circle shear for discs to Ø49″ in 10 ga and the ECS10/10 motorized circle shear with flanging rolls.
points: IDK-5: discs to Ø78.7″ (2000 mm) in 3/16″ steel, hydraulic clamp, flanging option
SDK 6 / SDK 8: cut and flange tank heads Ø21.7″ to Ø15 ft in 5/16″ plate; EFM 6 for elliptical heads
NovoTech value line: MCS-1250E motorized circle shear Ø8 – 49″, ECS10/10 circle shear with flanging
faq: How does a circle cutting machine work?

The sheet is clamped at its centre on a spindle and turned by hand or motor while two rotary blades shear a circle at the radius set on the arm. On the IDK-5, 3.5 and 2 a second pass at a smaller radius cuts the inside diameter, leaving a ring; the blank can then be flanged on the IDK-5's optional attachment.
What size and thickness can be cut?

From Ø4.3″ up to Ø78.7″ (2 m) depending on the model, in mild steel from 14 ga on the IDK-1.8 and IDK-2 to 3/16″ on the hydraulic IDK-5. Stainless steel reduces the capacity by roughly one gauge; ask us for the model that suits your material.
Hydraulic, pneumatic or manual clamp?

The centre clamp holds the sheet on the spindle while it rotates. The IDK-5 clamps hydraulically and the IDK-3.5 pneumatically (116 psi shop air) — fast and consistent for production; the IDK-2 and IDK-1.8 clamp by hand screw, which is fine for a few parts at a time.
How does a tank-head flanging machine work?

The plate disc is clamped on the part carrier and rotated while a top and bottom flanging roll, driven through planetary gearboxes, turn its edge up to the radius of the roll set — R1″ as supplied, other radii optional. On the SDK 6 and SDK 8 the same head first cuts the disc from the square plate with rotary blades, so a dished or flat head is cut and flanged without moving it; hydraulic lateral supports hold large heads and the LCD touchscreen runs the cycle.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Circular cold saws — manual, semi-automatic and automatic
pages.desc: Cold saws for metal sold in Canada, by kind: manual and semi-automatic circular saws with 9 – 16″ HSS blades, automatic carbide and HSS saws for tube and bar.
pages.intro: A cold saw cuts metal with a slow-turning, coolant-flooded circular blade instead of a hot abrasive disc, leaving a square, burr-free end that is cool to the touch and ready to weld. NovoTech sells two kinds in Canada, each on its own page: cold saws — the manual and semi-automatic circular saws of the fabrication shop: ISITAN SFC pull-down and semi-automatic saws with 10-3/4 to 13-3/4″ blades and NovoTech's value-line CS, PDS-315H and PDS-400 saws with 9 to 16″ blades, with abrasive cut-off saws and roller stands; and automatic cold saws — production saws that feed, cut and count by themselves: the CSM CT325 with servo feed for tube and bundles to Ø4″, the Bekamak BMDO XS carbide saws for solid bar to Ø6-1/4″, the BMDO CS HSS saws and the OPUS 300 for solid bar to Ø11-3/4″. Below, the two kinds compared, every model in one table, the buying guide and the questions we get asked; every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Cold saws: ISITAN SFC pull-down and semi-automatic saws, 10-3/4 – 13-3/4″; value-line CS, PDS-315H and PDS-400, 9 – 16″
Automatic cold saws: CSM CT325 with servo feed, Bekamak BMDO XS carbide, BMDO CS HSS and the OPUS 300 for bar to Ø11-3/4″
faq: Manual, semi-automatic or automatic — which do I need?

By the number of cuts. For a few cuts a day in a fabrication or maintenance shop, a manual cold saw — the operator pulls the head down — is the simplest machine; a semi-automatic saw runs the cut from a foot switch with a regulated head descent, for batches of the same part. When the same lengths are cut by the hundred, an automatic cold saw feeds the bar with a servo gripper, clamps, cuts and counts by itself. The manual and semi-automatic saws are on the cold saw page, the production saws on the automatic cold saw page.
TCT carbide or HSS cold saw?

A carbide (TCT) blade runs at 130–920 ft/min and is the fastest way to cut solid steel bar in production — the Bekamak BMDO XS saws and the Ø11-3/4″ OPUS 300 are built around it, with servo feeding and a magazine loader for unattended runs. HSS blades run slower (22–130 ft/min on the BMDO CS) and are the choice for tube, thin walls and mixed work; the XS saws accept HSS blades for tube as well.

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: CNC lathes — TTC and TTH slant-bed lathes, 6″ to 12″ chucks
pages.desc: CNC lathes for sale in Canada: Dener TTC and TTH slant-bed lathes with Fanuc control, 12-station servo turret, 6″ to 12″ chucks, Ø27.6″ swing, live tooling.
pages.intro: A CNC lathe turns, faces, bores, grooves and threads round parts from bar stock or chucked blanks, with its tools on a turret that brings the next one into position in a fraction of a second. NovoTech sells Dener's CNC lathes in Canada, built in Kayseri, Turkey, in the machine-tool plant Dener took over from Taksan in 2016. Both families share one design: a one-piece cast bed inclined at 45°, roller linear guides with C1 and C3 ballscrews coupled straight to the servo motors, a 12-station servo turret that indexes in 0.2 s, a hydraulic chuck and a hydraulic tailstock, under a Fanuc 0i-TF Plus control (Mitsubishi M80 to order). The compact TTC-6 and TTC-8 swing Ø22″ (560 mm) with 6″ and 8″ chucks; the TTH-8, TTH-10 and TTH-12 swing Ø27.6″ (700 mm), turn parts to Ø20.8″ × 26.8″ and go up to a 12″ chuck, 3.74″ (95 mm) bar and 602 lb·ft of spindle torque. A BMT55 C-axis turret with 12 live tools turns any of them into a turn-mill centre. Installed, programmed with you and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: TTC-6 / TTC-8: Ø22″ swing, turning Ø12″ × 17″, 6″ or 8″ chuck, 6,000 / 4,500 rpm
TTH-8 / 10 / 12: Ø27.6″ swing, turning Ø20.8″ × 26.8″, 8″ to 12″ chucks, bar to Ø3.74″ (95 mm)
Fanuc 0i-TF Plus, 12-station servo turret, hydraulic tailstock; C-axis live tooling, bar feeder and probes to order
faq: TTC or TTH — which lathe do I need?

Choose by the largest part and the bar you feed. The TTC turns parts up to Ø12″ × 17″ (305 × 433 mm) from a 6″ or 8″ chuck and takes bar to 1.77″ (TTC-6) or 2.05″ (TTC-8): the machine for shafts, pins, flanges and bushings in series. The TTH swings Ø27.6″, turns to Ø20.8″ × 26.8″ (528 × 680 mm) and has 8″, 10″ and 12″ chucks with bar to 2.05″, 2.95″ and 3.74″; the TTH-12's A2-11 spindle, 4.65″ bore and 602 lb·ft of torque are for large diameters, pipe and heavy roughing. Send us a drawing of your largest part and we check it against the working range.
Why a 45° slant bed?

On a slant bed the chips fall away from the tools and the guideways straight into the chip conveyor, the turret sits behind the spindle where the cutting force pushes into the casting, and the operator reaches the chuck easily over the low front. Dener casts the bed in one piece, stress-relieves it and lays it out by finite-element analysis, so it damps vibration in interrupted and heavy cuts.
Fanuc or Mitsubishi?

Dener lathes for North America come with the Fanuc 0i-TF Plus as standard, the control most Canadian programmers and service technicians already know; the Mitsubishi M80 is available instead. Both run ISO G-code with canned turning, grooving and threading cycles and take programs from any CAM system. The spindle motor differs slightly between the two (see the table).
What does the C-axis option add?

A BMT55 turret with 12 live (driven) tools at up to 6,000 rpm and a spindle that indexes and holds position: cross holes, tapped holes, flats, slots, hex and keyways are machined in the same setup instead of on a mill. The largest turning diameter and length are a little smaller with the live-tool turret — both are in the table.
Can it run unattended?

With the automatic bar feeder and a parts catcher a lathe runs through a bar without the operator; the tool-setting arm and workpiece probe measure offsets and parts in the cycle, and the automatic door opens and closes for a robot. All are options on both families.
Do you deliver, install and train in Canada?

Yes. Machines ship from Kayseri to Mississauga, ON, Canada; NovoTech unloads, levels and commissions the machine, checks the geometry, trains your operators and programmers on the control and helps with the first parts. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, a 1-year warranty and parts and service from Mississauga. Ask for the foundation drawing and the power and air requirements before the machine ships.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: CNC tube benders — electric, hybrid and hydraulic mandrel benders
pages.desc: CNC tube benders sold, installed and supported in Canada: CSM all-electric, hybrid and hydraulic CNC mandrel benders from Ø15/32″ to Ø8-5/8″, and ISITAN.
pages.intro: A CNC tube bender feeds, rotates and bends the tube from a program, so a part with ten bends in different planes comes off the machine the same every time; a mandrel inside the tube and a wiper die keep thin walls round at tight radii. NovoTech sells two makers' CNC mandrel benders in Canada, all on this page, small to large: CSM of Tainan, Taiwan — the EMB / EMR all-electric benders that switch between left- and right-hand bending within one part, from Ø19/32″ brake and fuel line to Ø3″, and the all-electric MRE2-RBE to Ø4″; the TBRE / TMRE / TSRE / TDRE and MBE / MRE electric hybrids from Ø15/32″ to Ø6″ with one to three stacked tools and roll-bending heads; and the TSR / TDR hydraulic CNC pipe benders to Ø8-5/8″ — then ISITAN of Bursa, Turkey: the five-axis SFB CNC/A5 with servo roll-bending for large sweeps, Ø1-1/2″ to Ø2-1/2″, and the SFB CNC/A3 in five sizes from Ø1-1/2″ tube to Ø3-1/2″ × 8 ga pipe, both with a 21″ touchscreen CNC, 3D simulation and spring-back compensation. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, tooling, installation and training, supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. NC mandrel benders, which program the bend angles while the tube is fed by hand or by a carrier, are on the NC page.
points: CSM all-electric EMB / EMR and MRE2-RBE Ø19/32″ – Ø4″ · electric hybrid TBRE / TDRE and MBE / MRE Ø15/32″ – Ø6″, 1 – 3 stacked tools
CSM TSR / TDR hydraulic CNC pipe benders to Ø8-5/8″ pipe on 20 ft mandrels
ISITAN SFB CNC/A5 and CNC/A3: Ø1-1/2″ × 11 ga to Ø3-1/2″ × 8 ga, 3 or 5 servo axes, 21″ touchscreen CNC with 3D simulation
faq: All-electric, electric-hybrid or hydraulic?

All-electric (EMB / EMR, MRE2-RBE): every axis is a servo motor — no oil, no warm-up, lower energy use, quiet and the most repeatable; the choice for small tube in high volume — fuel and brake lines, HVAC, head-rest bars, furniture. Electric hybrid (MBE / MRE and the T series): servo bend arm, carriage and collet for accuracy, hydraulic clamp, pressure die and mandrel for force — the usual production bender from Ø1/2″ to Ø6″. Hydraulic CNC (TSR / TDR): a hydraulic bend arm for heavy wall and large pipe to Ø8-5/8″ — boiler, shipyard, construction and water-supply pipe. NC (TSRJ / TDRJ, TNCPB, TNCB): PLC control and a lower price where the parts are simpler or the batches smaller.
How many stacked tools do I need, and what is roll bending?

Each stacked tool is another bend die (radius) on the same head; the head shifts up / down and left / right between them, so a part with two or three radii is bent in one cycle without a die change. One tool (TSRE, TSR, TNCB) suits single-radius parts; two (TDRE, TDR, TBRE) or three (MBE / MRE, TMRE) furniture, automotive and exhaust parts with several radii; the EMB / EMR carry 3 + 3, for left- and right-hand bends. A roll-bending head (EMR, MRE, TBRE / TMRE, MRE2-RBE) rolls large and variable radii — arcs, coils and frames — without a die for every radius.
What does a rear booster do?

It pushes the tube from behind while the bend arm draws it around the die, so the outside wall thins less and the inside wall does not wrinkle — the way to bend thin-wall tube and pipe to radii down to about 1 × D (boiler pipe on the 120 TNCB-RBF, for example). -RBE is a servo booster on the electric and hybrid benders; -RBF, -RBH and -CBF are hydraulic boosters on the hydraulic machines.
Can the bender be automated?

Yes: bundle loaders that feed the tube to the carriage, punching units on the head for holes in furniture tube (the P versions), an integrated circular saw that cuts each part off the bar, end-forming stations, robot transfer and checking fixtures. The videos under each series show most of them in production, and we lay out the cell for your parts.
How do I read a CSM model name?

The number is the largest round tube in millimetres: a 38 TDRE bends Ø1-1/2″ (38.1 mm), an 80 MBE Ø3-1/8″ (80 mm), a 220 TNCB Ø8-5/8″ pipe. The letters name the series — EMB / EMR all-electric, MBE / MRE and the TBRE / TMRE / TSRE / TDRE electric hybrids, TSR / TDR hydraulic CNC, TSRJ / TDRJ, TNCPB and TNCB NC — and in the T series S, D and M stand for one, two and three stacked tools. The suffix names the booster: -RBE a servo rear booster, -RBF, -RBH and -CBF hydraulic boosters.
3-axis or 5-axis?

Both ISITAN CNC benders have servo feed (Y), rotation (B) and bend (C). The A5 adds two servo roll-bending axes, so one machine can draw-bend tight radii around the mandrel and roll-bend large-radius sweeps — handrail returns, roll cages, furniture arcs — without changing machines or tooling. If every bend in your parts is a tight radius, the A3 does the job.
Does it bend without a mandrel too?

Yes — every SFB CNC bends with or without the mandrel, selected in the program. Thick-wall tube and generous radii bend without; thin-wall tube and tight radii need the mandrel (and often a wiper die) to stop wrinkling and collapse.
Can I program from a drawing?

The CNC takes X-Y-Z coordinates from the part drawing and converts them to Y-B-C bender data (feed, rotation, bend), simulates the sequence in 3D with collision warning, and estimates the tube length and cycle time before you bend the first part.
CSM or ISITAN?

Both are mandrel benders sold, installed and supported by NovoTech. The ISITAN SFB benders (Turkey) cover Ø1-1/4″ to Ø3-1/2″ with NC and CNC models for the job shop and fabricator. CSM covers a far wider range — from Ø15/32″ brake line to Ø8-5/8″ pipe — with all-electric and hybrid machines, stacked tools, boosters and automation for series production. Send us the part drawing and the tube and we quote the right machine from either range.
What do you need from me to quote tooling?

Six things: material type, tube or profile size, wall thickness, the smallest centreline radius (CLR) you bend, the maximum bend angle and the maximum tube length. Every bender comes with one die set in the size you request; extra sets, ball mandrels and wiper dies are quoted from the same list.
What voltage do the benders run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on the BK-42 and other models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase.

pages.h1: Coil-fed laser cutting lines — uncoil, level and cut, 1.5 to 80 kW
pages.desc: Five Senfeng coil-fed fiber laser lines sold in Canada: the SF1503CH for thin coil, the open SF15015C, the TOP line from coil to sorted parts, 9/16″ coil.
pages.intro: A coil-fed laser line uncoils, levels and feeds strip straight into the laser, so blanks are cut without a sheet ever being handled, stacked or scrapped at the edges and with no limit on part length — and coil costs less than cut-to-length sheet. NovoTech sells five Senfeng lines in Canada, all on this page and from the value line: the SF1503CH for thin coil to 0.118″ on a 5 × 10 ft laser with 3 to 6 kW; the open-style SF15015C, the affordable line for 0.031 to 0.047″ coil; the TOP line that takes coil to cut, bent, welded and stacked parts; the SF1503CLH with a straightener made for aluminum coil; and the SF2012CH that levels and cuts 0.314 to 0.551″ coil from 22-ton coils with 12 to 80 kW. Each line below has its full specification table and photos. Every line comes with a CSA-approved panel, chiller and software, installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: SF1503CH: thin coil 0.031 – 0.118″ to 16.5 US tons, 5 × 10 ft laser, 3 – 6 kW
SF15015C: open-style line for 0.031 – 0.047″ coil in half the floor space, 1.5 – 3 kW
TOP line: coil, laser, robot sorting, panel bending and welding in one unmanned line
SF1503CLH: aluminum coil 0.023 – 0.118″ with a straightener built for aluminum, 6 kW
SF2012CH: 5/16 – 9/16″ coil to 22 US tons on a 13 × 6.6 ft laser, 12 – 80 kW
faq: When does a coil-fed line pay off?

When the same material runs all day: enclosures, HVAC, appliance and automotive parts. The decoiler, leveller and laser work on one control, there is no sheet handling, no offcuts and no limit on part length, and coil costs less than cut-to-length sheet. The SF15015C runs 0.031 – 0.047″ coil through an open-style laser in half the floor space; the SF1503CH takes coil to 0.118″ and 16.5 tons; the SF1503CLH has a straightener made for aluminum coil; the SF2012CH levels and cuts 5/16″ to 9/16″ coil from 22-ton coils with 12 to 80 kW; and the TOP line carries on to robot sorting, panel bending, welding and stacking.
What laser power do I need?

Power sets the thickness and the speed. As a guide for mild steel: 3 kW cuts 1/2″, 6 kW 3/4″ (and 1/4″ at over 300 in/min), 12 kW 1″, 20 kW 1-1/4″ and 30 – 40 kW 1-1/2″ and beyond; stainless and aluminum run about 20 – 30 % thinner at the same power, with nitrogen or air assist. Most Canadian job shops buying today choose 6 or 12 kW: thick enough for structural work, fast enough to pay for the machine on thin sheet. Tell us your material mix and we run the cutting chart for you.
What about assist gas and fume extraction?

Oxygen gives the fastest cut and an oxide edge on mild steel; nitrogen a clean, paint-ready edge on all metals; compressed air at 16 bar replaces nitrogen on sheet to about 1/4″ and cuts the gas bill to near zero — the intelligent air-cutting package is an option on both lines. The machines have pneumatic extraction compartments under the table and connect to a dust collector, which we can supply.
What does the machine need on site?

A level floor, 600 V 3-phase (with the transformer we supply) or 480 V, a chiller (included), assist gas, a dust collector and a compressed-air supply for air cutting. A 6 kW 3015 draws about 46 kW in total (Dener's figure for the GFL) and needs roughly 33 × 20 ft with its shuttle table. Delivery, installation and operator training are done by NovoTech from Mississauga, ON, Canada, and the Ontario pre-start health and safety review is prepared by us.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Cold saws — manual and semi-automatic circular saws, 9″ to 16″ blades
pages.desc: Manual and semi-automatic circular cold saws sold in Canada: ISITAN SFC saws with 10-3/4 – 13-3/4″ blades and mitre 45° both ways, value-line saws 9 to 16″.
pages.intro: A cold saw cuts metal with a slow-turning, coolant-flooded circular blade instead of a hot abrasive disc, leaving a square, burr-free end that is cool to the touch and ready to weld. This page has the manual and semi-automatic cold saws for the fabrication shop: ISITAN's wet-type SFC 275 and 315 pull-down saws with a manual or pneumatic vise and the semi-automatic SFC 350-VX with a hydro-pneumatic head, all mitring 45° both ways; NovoTech's value-line saws, built in China — gear-driven manual CS saws with 9 – 14″ blades, the PDS-315H semi-automatic hydraulic saw and the PDS-400 heavy-duty saw with a 16″ blade; abrasive cut-off saws with 12 – 16″ wheels; and roller stands, a roller conveyor with a digital length stop and a measuring roller table. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. For production saws that feed, cut and count by themselves, see the automatic cold saws. CSA-approved panels and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: ISITAN SFC 275 / 315 pull-down saws and the SFC 350-VX semi-automatic: 10-3/4 – 13-3/4″ HSS blades, round to Ø4-1/2″, mitre 45° both ways
NovoTech value line: CS cold saws 9 – 14″, PDS-315H semi-automatic hydraulic, PDS-400 heavy-duty 16″, TV abrasive saws 12 – 16″
Roller stands, a roller conveyor with a digital length stop and a measuring roller table
faq: Manual, pneumatic or semi-automatic?

The SFC V clamps with a hand vise — the simplest saw for occasional cuts. The SFC VP clamps with air at the pull of a lever, which saves time on every cut and holds short pieces better. The SFC 350-VX runs a semi-automatic cycle from a foot switch with a regulated head descent, for batches of the same part without an operator on the handle.
Cold saw or abrasive chop saw?

An abrasive chop saw grinds through the steel at high speed, leaving a hot, burred, slightly bevelled end and sparks. A cold saw cuts with a slow HSS blade (45–90 rpm) under coolant, so the cut is square, cool to the touch, burr-free and ready to weld or fit — and the blade is resharpened dozens of times instead of thrown away.
Which blade do I need?

A standard HSS blade cuts mild steel and aluminum. For medium-hard steel we fit TiN-coated blades, TiCN for high-strength steel and TiAlN for stainless. The blade bore is 32 mm with two Ø11 mm pin holes on all SFC models, so blades are readily available in Canada.

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
