pages.h1: Column and boom welding manipulators — 31.5 to 275.6″ lift and boom
pages.desc: Column and boom welding manipulators for tank and vessel seams — 31.5 to 275.6″ lift, 39.4 to 315″ boom, fixed, rotating or travelling, sold in Canada.
pages.intro: A column and boom (welding manipulator) holds the welding head — submerged arc, MIG or TIG — on a horizontal boom that travels up and down a column and in and out over the part, and feeds it along the seam at the welding speed: longitudinal seams of tanks and pipe, and, with turning rolls or a positioner turning the part beneath it, circumferential seams inside and outside. NovoTech's value-line manipulators, built in China, come in three sizes, all on this page, small to large: small manipulators with 31.5 to 78.7″ of lift and 39.4 to 78.7″ of boom travel, the column turned by hand; medium ones with 78.7 to 157.5″ of lift and 118.1 to 196.9″ of boom; and heavy ones with 196.9 to 275.6″ of lift and 236.2 to 315″ of boom, with motorized column rotation and carriage travel. Every model is available fixed, fixed with rotation or travelling with rotation, with arc auto-tracking, a TV monitor and flux recovery as options. Parts, installation and service from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Small DLH0810 – DLH2020: 31.5 – 78.7″ lift, 39.4 – 78.7″ boom, column turned by hand
Medium DLH2030 – DLH4050 and heavy DLH5060 – DLH7080: to 275.6″ lift and 315″ boom, motorized rotation and carriage
Boom feed 4.7 – 47.2 in/min · fixed, rotating or travelling · arc tracking, TV monitor, flux recovery
faq: What is a column and boom used for?

Welding long and circumferential seams by machine: the boom puts the welding head over the seam and feeds it at the welding speed while the operator watches the arc. With the vessel on turning rolls the head stays still and the vessel turns for circumferential seams; with the boom feeding, it welds longitudinal seams — inside and outside of small tanks, longitudinal and transverse seams of large ones.
Fixed, rotating or travelling?

A fixed column suits a cell where the part comes to the machine. A fixed column with rotation swings the boom up to ±180° between two stations — weld one part while the next is loaded. A travelling column runs on rails along the work, for long vessels and several stations.
Which size do I need?

By the largest part: the lift has to put the head at the top of the largest vessel on its rolls, and the boom has to reach the far end of the longest seam — or inside the vessel for internal seams. Send us the diameters and lengths of your vessels and the welding process and we size the manipulator and the rolls under it.
What options are there?

Arc auto-tracking that keeps the head on the seam, a TV monitor for watching the arc from the control station, and a flux recovery and conveying system for submerged-arc welding. The welding power source and head are chosen for the process.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Compact and small hydraulic press brakes — 16 to 66 US tons (15 to 60 t), 2 to 8 ft
pages.desc: Small hydraulic press brakes sold in Canada: the Dener XL 1560 compact CNC brake, 66 US tons × 5 ft with ESA S840 control, and value-line NC brakes from 16.
pages.intro: A compact hydraulic press brake bends sheet between a punch and a V-die like its big brothers, at the size that fits a sheet-metal shop rather than a steel-fabrication plant: 2 to 8 ft of bending length and 16 to 66 US tons (15 to 60 t), on a footprint that goes through a door and runs on a 600 V or 208 V supply. NovoTech sells three on this page: the Dener XL 1560 — the smallest machine of the premium line, 66 US tons (60 t) over 5 ft with the 15.6″ ESA S840 2D control, Y1-Y2 ram on linear scales, a ball-screw X back gauge and EUROSTAMP tooling in the crate, built in Turkey; NovoTech's own value-line compacts, built to our specification — the WAD-50T CNC brakes, 55 US tons (50 t) over 4.3 and 5.2 ft with servo valves and a Delem DA-53Tx, and the WC67K-30T torsion-bar NC brake, 33 US tons (30 t) over 5.2 ft with an Estun E21PS; and the value-line HBV bending brakes, 16 to 35 tons (15 to 32 t), with a four-way V-block (HBV24 / 48) or two cylinders (HBV-1250 / 2540) for brackets, clips and short parts in plate to 3/16″. For HVAC fittings, enclosures, signage, brackets and job-shop work where a 100-ton (91 t) machine is more than you need. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel and a 1-year warranty, installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. For 10 ft and longer, or 1/4″ plate and up, see the hydraulic press brakes; for a brake with no hydraulic oil the electric press brakes.
points: Dener XL 1560: 66 US tons (60 t) × 5 ft, 15.7″ throat, ESA S840 2D control, Y1-Y2-X axes on linear scales, EUROSTAMP 1281 punch and 2067 4-way die included — premium line, made in Turkey
Value line: WAD-50T/1300 and 1600 CNC brakes, 55 US tons (50 t) × 4.3 – 5.2 ft, 4 axes with Delem DA-53Tx; WC67K-30T/1600 NC torsion-bar brake, 33 US tons (30 t) × 5.2 ft with Estun E21PS
Value-line HBV bending brakes: 16.5 – 35 US tons (15 – 32 t), 5/32″ × 24 – 48″, 3/16″ × 49″ and 1/8″ × 100″, four-way V-block or two cylinders
faq: What tonnage do I need?

Bending force depends on the sheet thickness, the bend length and the V-die opening: F = S² × 2 × R ÷ (1.4 × V) tonnes per metre with S and V in millimetres and R = 47 kg/mm² for mild steel — in inches and US tons per foot about 575 × t² ÷ V. In a V of 8 × the thickness, a 4 ft bend takes about 16 US tons (15 t) in 16 ga, 39 tons (35 t) in 10 ga and 47 tons (43 t) in 8 ga (0.16″); a wider die lowers the force — 8 ga in a 2″ V takes about 31 tons (28 t) over 4 ft — at the cost of a larger inside radius. The control calculates the exact force for the tool and material you enter; send us your thickest and longest bend and we size the machine.
Dener XL 1560 or a value-line compact?

The XL 1560 is the premium machine: the heaviest frame, servo-valve hydraulics, an ESA 2D control with collision control, the DSP-AP laser finger guard as standard, every Dener option open to it — 3D controls, 4- to 6-axis back gauges, CNC crowning, Wila clamping, robot cells — and parts stocked in Canada; it bends 3/16″ over the full 5 ft and 1/4″ over 4 ft. The value-line WAD-50T is the same electro-hydraulic servo architecture (servo valves, linear scales, Delem control) built to our specification at a lower price, for 1/8″ over 5.2 ft; the WC67K-30T is the simple torsion-bar NC brake for one material and repeat parts. If the brake runs all day or you program from CAD, the XL; if it bends brackets and enclosures a few hours a day, the value line.
NC or CNC?

An NC brake (the WC67K-30T) sets the ram depth and the back gauge from a stored program, with the two cylinders kept in step by a torsion bar — enough for the same parts in one material. A CNC brake (the XL 1560 and the WAD-50T) measures the ram on linear scales and corrects it through servo valves, calculates tonnage, bend sequence and gauge positions from the drawing, and changes material and tool in the program — the machine for mixed work, tight angles and multi-bend parts. The buying guide on the press brake page compares every control these machines are sold with.
Press brake or HBV bending brake?

The XL 1560, WAD-50T and WC67K-30T are press brakes: a programmable ram, a motorised back gauge, segmented tooling and a guard, for sheet work all day. The HBV is a hydraulic bending brake for short parts in plate — brackets, clips, tabs — bent on a four-way V-block (HBV24 / 48) or between two cylinders (HBV-1250 / 2540) with a hand-wheel back gauge, at a fraction of the price. If you bend panels and enclosures, a press brake; if you bend 3/16″ plate brackets a few at a time, the HBV.
What tooling fits, and do you stock it?

European-style (Promecam / Amada) segmented tooling fits every line: the premium Dener brakes carry European-style top-tool holders, the value-line brakes their own clamping, and a sectioned punch set with a 2-V or 4-V die ships with every machine (a 4-V die with the Dener brakes, a 2-V die with the value line) — tell us which tooling standard your shop already has and we fit the holders to match. NovoTech stocks Eurostamp press brake tooling in Canada — punches, dies, radius, hemming and joggle tools, gooseneck and special profiles — and sizes it to your machine; quick-release, pneumatic and Wila hydraulic clamping and American-style adapters are options, not standard equipment.
Are they safe to run without a separate guarding system?

Every compact press brake carries side guards, an enclosed rear guard with interlocked doors and a foot pedal with emergency stop; the Dener XL 1560 comes with the DSP-AP laser finger guard and an MCS safety PLC as standard, and on the value-line machines a laser guard — DSP, Fiessler AKAS or a light curtain — is an option we recommend. In Ontario a new press brake needs a pre-start health and safety review (PSR) under Regulation 851 before it runs.
Do you deliver, install and service in Canada?

Yes — NovoTech sells, installs and supports press brakes across Canada and the United States. Installation, commissioning and operator training are free of charge in the Greater Toronto Area; outside the GTA our technicians do the same work at an additional charge. Parts are stocked in Canada. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, 600 V standard (208 / 240 / 480 V on request), a 1-year warranty and remote diagnostics through the control.
What does delivery cost, and who unloads the machine?

A press brake ordered from the factory (back-ordered) travels in its container straight from the port, customs and the rail yard to your plant door: in the Greater Toronto Area that delivery is free; outside the GTA the freight is quoted and charged. A machine from NovoTech's stock is loaded, shipped and unloaded at the buyer's cost. In every case unloading is the buyer's responsibility and expense — the crane or forklift, the rigging and moving the machine onto its foundation — so book a rigger for the delivery day; we are glad to recommend riggers who know press brakes and to tell you the weight and lifting points.
Is the hydraulic oil included?

No — the hydraulic oil is bought by the customer. Before commissioning, fill the tank with ISO VG 46 anti-wear hydraulic oil (AW 46) in the quantity shown in the specification table for your model; our technician checks the level and bleeds the system during installation. Electric press brakes have no hydraulic oil at all.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Corner grinding machines and corner sanders — for weld seams of boxes, doors and frames
pages.desc: Corner grinders (corner sanders) that grind the welds on box, cabinet and door corners flush or to a radius: hand-fed, automatic and PLC GECAM machines, to 59″.
pages.intro: A corner grinder (corner grinding machine, also called a corner sander or weld seam sander) grinds the weld on the corner of a welded box, cabinet, door or tray flush with the sheet, or to a neat radius, ready for paint or polishing — work that takes long minutes with a hand grinder and never looks the same twice. NovoTech sells GECAM corner grinders, built in Parma, Italy: the hand-fed GECAM 131 and GECAM 136, where an abrasive belt on an oscillating fork grinds corners up to 5-7/8″ and 11-13/16″ high to a radius of 3/64″ to 3/8″; the GECAM 135, whose head travels the full length of the edge by itself on boxes with edges up to 59″; and PLC-controlled machines for series work — an upper-corner grinder, a six-head grinder and a grinder for the welds of 90° tube frames. Supplied with a CSA-approved panel, installed and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. NovoTech's value line, built in China, adds the YQ corner grinding machines: horizontal machines for box edges up to 35.4, 47.2 or 59.1″ long and the YQ-450 vertical machine for corners up to 17.7″ high.
points: GECAM 131 · GECAM 136: hand-fed, corners to 5-7/8″ and 11-13/16″ high, radius 3/64″ – 3/8″ or sharp
GECAM 135: automatic head travel along edges up to 31-1/2″ or 59″, one or two heads
Special PLC grinders for upper corners, two corners at once and 90° tube frames
NovoTech value line: YQ horizontal corner grinders for edges to 59.1″ and the YQ-450 vertical corner grinder
faq: What does a corner grinder do?

It grinds the weld bead on an outside corner of a welded box, cabinet, door or tray flush with the sheet — or to a radius — so the corner can be painted, powder-coated or polished without visible weld. The belt runs over rollers or a pad shaped for the corner, so the result is the same on every part, unlike hand grinding.
Is a corner sander the same as a corner grinder?

Yes. Corner grinder, corner grinding machine, corner sander and weld seam sander are names for the same machine: an abrasive belt that grinds the weld on an inside or outside corner flush with the sheet or to a radius.
Hand-fed or automatic?

The GECAM 131 and GECAM 136 are hand-fed: the operator moves the corner along the belt — quick to set up for mixed boxes and doors. The GECAM 135 clamps the box and runs the head along the whole edge by itself, which suits long edges and repeat work, and a second head doubles its output. For high volumes of one part, the PLC machines grind two corners or a whole tube-frame corner per cycle.
What radius can it make?

The oscillating fork of the GECAM 131 and GECAM 136 grinds a radius from 3/64″ to 3/8″ (R1 – R10 mm), or a sharp corner. The GECAM 135 grinds the weld flush; its PLUS version adds vertical, horizontal and oscillating head movement for radiusing.
How high a box can it take?

Corner height up to 5-7/8″ on the GECAM 131 and 7-7/8″ or 11-13/16″ on the GECAM 136 (19-11/16″ on request). The GECAM 135 is limited by edge length — 31-1/2″ or 59″ — and the six-head grinder takes boxes up to 5-7/8″ high.
Can you build a machine for my part?

Yes. Gecam designs special corner grinders around the part — the upper-corner, six-head and tube-frame machines on this page are examples. Send us a drawing or photo of the part and the weld, and the number of parts a shift.
GECAM or the value-line YQ?

The GECAM 131, 136 and 135 are built in Parma, Italy, for daily production on boxes, cabinets and doors, with an oscillating belt fork for radii and the automatic head travel of the 135. The value-line YQ machines, built in China, are the lower-cost choice for corner weld seams and R corners on water tanks, battery boxes and similar boxes — horizontal for edges up to 59.1″, vertical for corners up to 17.7″ high.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Hydraulic corner notchers — sheet metal notching machines to 1/4″
pages.desc: Hydraulic corner notchers that cut a 90° or 30° – 140° corner out of sheet to 1/4″ in one stroke: HNM 4F, 6F and 6V with T-slot table and automatic blade gap.
pages.intro: A corner notcher (notching machine) cuts a square or V-shaped corner out of a sheet in one stroke so the four sides fold up into a box, pan, tray or enclosure on the press brake — the hand-cut, hand-ground corner of the sheet-metal shop done in a second. The HNM range: the fixed 90° HNM 4F for 3/16″ and HNM 6F for 1/4″ mild steel with foot-pedal control and a small footprint, and the HNM 6V variable-angle notcher whose blades swing from 30° to 140° on a T-slot table with automatic blade-gap adjustment and four hydraulic hold-downs. Sold with a CSA-approved panel, blades and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada. NovoTech's value-line notchers, built in China, add the HNM-6 and HNM-6A hydraulic notchers for 1/4″ and the PNM-130 and PNM-150 pneumatic notchers for sheet to 1/8″.
points: HNM 4F and HNM 6F — fixed 90°, 3/16″ and 1/4″ mild steel, 20 – 25 cuts per minute
HNM 6V — 30° to 140° variable angle, 1/4″ mild steel, automatic blade gap, T-slot table
Stainless to 11 ga; blade lengths 7.8″ to 9.8″
NovoTech value line: HNM-6 / HNM-6A hydraulic 1/4″, PNM-130 / PNM-150 pneumatic
faq: Fixed 90° or variable angle?

Boxes, pans, trays and enclosures are 90° corners, and the HNM 4F and 6F cut them fastest at 20 – 25 strokes per minute. Hoppers, cones, chutes, duct transitions and any part whose sides are not square need the HNM 6V, whose blades set to any angle from 30° to 140° and whose T-slot table takes stops for repeat positioning.
What does automatic blade-gap adjustment do?

Shear blades need a gap that grows with the sheet thickness. On the HNM 6V the gap follows the thickness automatically, so the operator changes from 20 ga to 1/4″ without realigning the blades — and the cut edge stays clean on both.
Can the notcher cut stainless and aluminum?
Yes — 14 ga (HNM 4F) or 11 ga (HNM 6F / 6V) stainless, and aluminum up to the mild-steel capacity. Blades are hardened tool steel and are resharpened and shimmed back to size.
Corner notcher or ironworker notching station?

The ironworker's rectangular notching station cuts a slot into the edge of bar and plate; the corner notcher cuts the full square corner out of a large sheet laid on its table with a back gauge, at 20 – 30 strokes a minute. Sheet-metal shops that fold boxes daily want the notcher; structural shops are usually served by the ironworker.
Hydraulic or pneumatic notcher?

A hydraulic notcher cuts 3/16 – 1/4″ plate quickly and is the choice for a production shop or for heavier plate; a pneumatic notcher runs on shop air and cuts up to 1/8″ in sheet — quieter, no hydraulic oil, a lower price. The premium-line HNM notchers and the value-line HNM-6 / HNM-6A differ in build and price; both have adjustable stops and a sheet hold-down.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Corner welding machines — TIG and plasma corner welders, 1 to 4 axes
pages.desc: 1-, 2-, 3- and 4-axis TIG and plasma corner welders for bent boxes in steel, stainless and aluminum: GECAM CWS and WELCOR, laser seam reading.
pages.intro: A corner welding machine welds the corners of bent sheet-metal parts — boxes, cabinets, trays, enclosures, doors — with the torch driven by the machine at a set speed instead of by hand, so every corner comes out the same and the welder is free while it runs. NovoTech sells the corner welders of GECAM, built in Parma, Italy, from one axis to four: the part is clamped from inside against copper guides that hold the corner square and draw off the heat, the TIG or plasma torch welds at 0 to 47 in/min, and the parameters of every part are stored. One axis welds a straight corner seam — the CWS 200 and CWS 300 on parts to 59″ square, the WELCOR 400 X on corners to 15-3/4″ high; two and three axes weld a seam that runs in two or three directions in one cycle; the four-axis WELCOR adds torch rotation and a laser that reads the seam before welding. Mild steel, stainless steel and aluminum. The welded corner then goes to a corner grinder. Supplied with a CSA-approved panel, installed and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: 1-axis CWS 200 · CWS 300 · WELCOR 400 X for straight corner seams 7-7/8″ to 15-3/4″ high, parts to 59″ square
2-axis CWS 300 XY · WELCOR 400 XY and 3-axis WELCOR 400 XYZ for seams in two or three directions
4-axis WELCOR 400 XYZ-Φ with torch rotation and laser seam reading · TIG or plasma, 0 – 47 in/min
faq: What does a corner welding machine do?

It welds the corner seam of a bent part with the torch driven by the machine at a set speed: the operator places the part with its corner against the copper squaring guide, locks it with a button and presses start. The result is a straight, even weld on every corner whatever the operator's skill, and the welder can prepare the next part while it runs.
1, 2, 3 or 4 axes — which do I need?

One axis welds a straight corner seam — the corner of a plain box, up to 7-7/8″ high on the CWS 200, 11-13/16″ on the CWS 300 and 15-3/4″ on the WELCOR 400 X. On two axes (X and Y) the torch is driven in two directions: the WELCOR 400 XY welds seams up to 15-3/4″ on X and 4-5/16″ on Y. Three axes add Z — up to 1-15/16″ — so a seam that runs in three directions is welded in one cycle. The four-axis WELCOR adds torch rotation, from vertical to about 120°, and a laser that checks the edges and memorizes the path before welding. Send us a drawing of your part and we will tell you which one it needs.
What do the copper groups do?

The part is pressed from inside against copper — an outer unit 7-7/8″ or 11-13/16″ high and an inner unit from 1-15/16″ to 11-13/16″ chosen for the corner on the CWS and the WELCOR 400 to three axes; modular aluminum and copper pads from 3/8″ to 7-7/8″ thick, matched to the box, on the four-axis WELCOR. They hold the corner square during welding and draw the heat away, keeping the heat of the part down; cooled inner groups are recommended to avoid dark marks on the parts.
How must the corner be bent?

The two edges should meet on the corner — .0004″ (0.01 mm) apart and centred on it. Where the bend does not allow it, they may overlap by half the sheet thickness at most; on the CWS the gap between the edges must not exceed .008″ (0.2 mm). Good press brake work upstream pays off at the welder.
TIG or plasma — and is the power source included?

The machines work with a TIG or a plasma welding power source, which is not included. GECAM offers the Lorch T 250 — T 250 DC for mild and stainless steel, T 250 AC/DC also for aluminum — with a cooling unit and a torch group with a 9′10″ cable. Tell us the material, thickness and corner you weld and we will quote the machine with its power source.
Which parts fit?

Bent parts from 3-15/16 × 3-15/16″ to 59-1/16 × 59-1/16″ on the CWS 200, CWS 300 and CWS 300 XY (32-5/16″ square work table, 39-3/8″ to order), and to 39-3/8 × 39-3/8″ on the WELCOR 400 — on the four-axis the smallest box 1-15/16″ high. Mild steel, stainless steel and aluminum.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Bekamak double-column band saws
pages.desc: Heavy-duty double column band saws from Ø13″ to 87″ (330 – 2,200 mm): BMSY C semi-automatics, CGH / DG NC miter saws, BMSO CS / CGS servo saws, the XS line.
pages.intro: For heavy bar, billets, beams and bundles the bow runs between two hardened columns instead of pivoting, so the blade enters the material squarely and stays square through the cut. Bekamak builds semi-automatic and fully automatic versions, miter heads to 60°, servo feeding with NC job lists, the enclosed high-tech XS production saws, the high-speed TERRA 6 that runs its blade at up to 1,970 ft/min (600 m/min), the BMSO 1313CS for 51″ blocks and the gantry-type GANTRY 2200XS — from Ø13″ to Ø87″ (330–2200 mm). Known as double column, twin-column or dual column metal bandsaws, these horizontal band saw machines are the industrial choice for heavy solids, bundles and plate.
points: Twin-column guidance for square cuts in heavy stock
Semi-automatic, roller-feed and servo-feed NC models
Round capacities from Ø13″ (330 mm) to Ø87″ (2200 mm) — the GANTRY 2200XS for 50,000 kg pieces
faq: Why choose a double-column saw over a pivot saw?

Rigidity and capacity. The bow is guided on two columns, so there is no side load on the blade — cuts stay square in large solids and the blade lasts longer. Double-column saws also reach capacities a pivot bow cannot: Ø13″ (330 mm) up to Ø87″ (2200 mm) on the Bekamak range, with the GANTRY 2200XS at the top.
Can a double-column saw cut miters?

Yes — the BMSY CGH (single miter) and BMSY DG NC (double miter) swivel the whole bow assembly up to 60° under hydraulic or NC control, and the automatic CGS/CDGS NC models do the same with servo feeding.
What is a split vise (SV)?
The SV versions of the BMSY C saws have a second vise jaw close to the blade, so short pieces and remnants are clamped on both sides of the cut — useful for cutting slices from blocks and billets.
What is the XS line?
Bekamak's high-tech production saws: servo-driven bow feed and material feed, full enclosure and CNC control, designed for carbide blades, the fastest cycle times and unattended running.
What is different about the TERRA 6?

Blade speed. A conventional band saw runs at up to 395 ft/min (120 m/min); the TERRA 6 runs its 2-5/8″ band at up to 1,970 ft/min (600 m/min) on a 40 HP motor, so with the right carbide blade a Ø16-3/8″ (415 mm) solid bar that takes about 22 minutes on a conventional saw is cut in about 2 minutes. A load cell and a deflection sensor let the PC-based control correct the cutting parameters in real time, and the enclosed cabin, zero-remnant unloading and camera are built for unattended production of Ø26″ (660 mm) stock.
How big is the GANTRY 2200XS?

It cuts rounds from Ø20″ to Ø87″ (500–2200 mm) and blocks up to 94-1/2″ × 87″, pieces up to 23 ft (7 m) long and 50,000 kg, on a gantry frame 49 ft long — a saw for forges, steel mills and service centres that cut ingots and large billets. Servo bow and material feed, a 40 HP main motor and MES production software are standard.

pages.h1: Drill presses — gear-head, column, floor and bench drill presses
pages.desc: Industrial drill presses: gear-head drill presses 1 – 2″ in steel with power feed and tapping, inverter drill presses, belt-drive and stepless column drills.
pages.intro: A drill press holds the drill square to the work and feeds it with the force and control a hand drill cannot give — the first machine tool in most fabrication and maintenance shops. NovoTech's value-line drill presses are built in China to our specification: gear-head drill presses from 1″ to 2″ in steel with eight or twelve speeds, power feed and tapping, inverter drill presses that keep full torque at low speed, and belt-drive and stepless column drills. Parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Gear-head drill presses T-25 – T-50: 1″ to 2″ in steel, 8 – 12 speeds, power feed, tapping to M30
T5025 / T4025 compact gear-head drill presses: 1″ in steel, table tilting ±50°, forward / reverse, preset depth
TX530 inverter drill presses with two-range gearbox; TB column drills, belt drive or stepless by frequency converter
faq: Gear-head or belt-drive drill press?

A gear-head drill press changes speed with levers on a gearbox and transmits more torque at low speed — the speeds you need for 1″ and larger holes and for tapping — and it does not slip. A belt-drive drill press is quieter and smoother at high speed for small holes but needs the belts moved to change speed. Inverter (V) machines change speed steplessly from the panel and keep their torque at low speed with a two-range gearbox (TX530).
What drilling capacity do I need?

The rated capacity is the largest hole drilled in mild steel in one pass with a twist drill. Choose a machine one size above your largest everyday hole: a 1″ machine for general fabrication, 1-1/4 to 1-9/16″ for structural work and tapping, 2″ for heavy plates and flanges. Larger holes are faster and safer with an annular cutter on a magnetic drill or on the drill press.
Which drill presses tap?

The TX530 range taps 3/4 – 1″ with forward and reverse; the T-50 and T-50E tap M30 in steel; tapping is an option on most T-25, T-26, T-28 and T-30 models. Tapping needs a reversing spindle and low speed — tell us the largest tap and the material.
Single-phase or 3-phase?
The TB…V inverter column drills run on single-phase power; the gear-head drill presses have 3-phase two-speed motors, supplied for 600 V with a CSA-approved panel or for 208 / 240 / 480 V on request.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Electric press brakes — servo-electric and ball-screw, 3 to 220 tons (3 to 200 t)
pages.desc: Servo-electric and ball-screw press brakes sold in Canada: 3 to 220 US tons, no hydraulic oil, ±0.01 mm repeatability, twice the speed of a hydraulic brake.
pages.intro: An electric press brake drives the ram with servo motors and ball screws or belts instead of hydraulic cylinders, so it needs no hydraulic oil and no pump running idle. It repeats to ±0.0004″ (±0.01 mm), bends at up to 1.2″/s (30 mm/s), about twice as fast as a hydraulic press brake, and draws about 70 % less power. It is usually the better buy for 20 ga to 1/4″ sheet in a job shop, an enclosure or HVAC plant, or anywhere clean and quiet matters. NovoTech sells two lines in Canada, both on this page: the premium Dener DDM servo-electric press brakes from 44 to 220 US tons (40 to 200 t) and 5 to 13 ft with the ESA S875 3D control, and the DDS ball-screw brakes of 22 and 44 tons (20 and 40 t) for small parts; and NovoTech's own value-line electric press brakes, ball-screw driven, from 11 to 176 US tons (10 to 160 t) and 1.6 to 10.5 ft with Delem control, plus 3 to 13 ton (3 to 12 t) bench machines. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel and a 1-year warranty, installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. For 3/8″ plate, tonnage above 220 tons (200 t) or the lowest price per ton, see the hydraulic press brakes.

Value line: electric ball-screw brakes 11 – 176 US tons (10 – 160 t) × 1.6 – 10.5 ft with Delem control; 3 – 13 ton (3 – 12 t) bench brakes
±0.01 mm, power only while the ram moves, no hydraulic oil or filters — about twice the speed of a hydraulic brake on sheet
faq: Electric or hydraulic — which press brake should I buy?

Electric when the work is sheet — 20 ga to 1/4″, brackets, enclosures, panels, stainless and aluminum — and when accuracy, speed, energy and a clean floor matter: the servo drive repeats to ±0.01 mm, bends at about twice the speed of a hydraulic brake and draws power only while the ram moves. Hydraulic when the work is plate, 3/8″ and up, long parts over 13 ft, or tonnage above 220 US tons (200 t), and when the lowest price per ton decides. Many shops run one of each; the hydraulic press brakes have their own page.
Servo-electric or ball-screw — what is the difference?

Both are electric. The DDM servo-electric brake drives the ram through servo motors and a belt-and-pulley system across the whole bending length, which is how it reaches 220 US tons (200 t) and 13 ft with the force distributed evenly along the beam. The DDS and the value-line brakes drive the ram with two ball screws, one per side, each on its own servo motor — simpler, very accurate, and the right construction up to about 176 tons (160 t) and 10 ft.
Premium line or value line?

The premium DDM is built in Turkey by Dener with the 21.5″ ESA S875 W 3D control, 6-axis back gauges, laser angle measurement and robot cells as options, and parts stocked in Canada — the production electric brake. NovoTech's value-line electric brakes are built in China to our specification with Delem control and the same Estun servo components, at about two-thirds of the price — the electric brake for a job shop or a second machine for small parts. Both are installed and supported by the same NovoTech technicians.
How much tonnage and length do I need?

Air bending takes F = S² × 2 × R ÷ (1.4 × V) tonnes per metre of bend — the sheet thickness S and the V opening V in millimetres, the tensile strength R = 47 kg/mm² for mild steel (70 for stainless, 25 for aluminum), the formula behind the EUROSTAMP and Dener bending charts; in inches and US tons per foot it reads 575 × t² ÷ V. With the standard V of about 8 × the thickness, 3 mm needs about 24 t/m (8 US tons per foot), 6 mm 48 t/m (16), 1/4″ 54 t/m (18), 3/8″ in a 3″ V 80 t/m (27) and 1/2″ in a 5″ V 85 t/m (29). Multiply by the bend length and add about 20 % in reserve: 3 m × 6 mm is a 175-ton (159 t) press brake, 10 ft × 1/4″ a 200 – 220 US ton (181 – 200 t) machine, 10 ft × 3/8″ a 300 – 320 ton (272 – 290 t) machine and 13 ft × 1/2″ a 400 – 450 ton (363 – 408 t) machine. The tonnage calculator in the buying guide on the press brake page does the arithmetic for your thickness and length; tell us your thickest and longest bend and we size the brake and the tooling.
What does an electric press brake cost to run?

There is no hydraulic oil to buy, filter, cool or dispose of, no pump motor idling between bends, and the servo motors regenerate on the return stroke: Dener measures about 70 % less energy than a hydraulic brake of the same tonnage on sheet work, and the maintenance schedule is lubrication of the ball screws and guides. The machines are also quieter, which matters in a shop that runs the brake all day.
What tooling fits, and do you stock it?

European-style (Promecam / Amada) segmented tooling fits every line: the premium Dener brakes carry European-style top-tool holders, the value-line brakes their own clamping, and a sectioned punch set with a 2-V or 4-V die ships with every machine (a 4-V die with the Dener brakes, a 2-V die with the value line) — tell us which tooling standard your shop already has and we fit the holders to match. NovoTech stocks Eurostamp press brake tooling in Canada — punches, dies, radius, hemming and joggle tools, gooseneck and special profiles — and sizes it to your machine; quick-release, pneumatic and Wila hydraulic clamping and American-style adapters are options, not standard equipment.
What about safety and the Ontario pre-start review?

Side guards, an enclosed rear guard, interlocked doors and an anti-panic foot pedal with emergency stop are standard; DSP laser finger protection is standard on the WAD CNC press brakes and the Dener XL, and on the other machines DSP or Fiessler laser protection and light curtains are options we recommend for every CNC press brake. In Ontario a new press brake needs a pre-start health and safety review (PSR) under Regulation 851 before it runs.
Do you deliver, install and service in Canada?

Yes — NovoTech sells, installs and supports press brakes across Canada and the United States. Installation, commissioning and operator training are free of charge in the Greater Toronto Area; outside the GTA our technicians do the same work at an additional charge. Parts are stocked in Canada. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, 600 V standard (208 / 240 / 480 V on request), a 1-year warranty and remote diagnostics through the control.
What does delivery cost, and who unloads the machine?

A press brake ordered from the factory (back-ordered) travels in its container straight from the port, customs and the rail yard to your plant door: in the Greater Toronto Area that delivery is free; outside the GTA the freight is quoted and charged. A machine from NovoTech's stock is loaded, shipped and unloaded at the buyer's cost. In every case unloading is the buyer's responsibility and expense — the crane or forklift, the rigging and moving the machine onto its foundation — so book a rigger for the delivery day; we are glad to recommend riggers who know press brakes and to tell you the weight and lifting points.
Is the hydraulic oil included?

No — the hydraulic oil is bought by the customer. Before commissioning, fill the tank with ISO VG 46 anti-wear hydraulic oil (AW 46) in the quantity shown in the specification table for your model; our technician checks the level and bleeds the system during installation. Electric press brakes have no hydraulic oil at all.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: European-style press brake dies — 1V, multi-V, self-centring, hemming
pages.desc: 1V, 2V, 4V, self-centring, T, hemming and ESH insert dies for Amada-Promecam clamping, V 4 – 220 mm, made in Italy by EUROSTAMP, with DXF profiles.
pages.intro: EUROSTAMP dies for the European-style (Amada-Promecam) lower beam found on most press brakes sold in Canada. Six families: solid 1V dies from V18 to V220 mm (.71 – 8.66″) for sheet and plate; 2V, 4V and 3U dies that hold several openings in one block, with their holders; slim self-centring 1V dies on rails; T dies — a slim body on a 60 mm foot — for return flanges and closed profiles; mechanical and pneumatic hemming dies that pre-bend and close a hem with one punch; and the ESH insert dies, nitrided all over to 65 HRC. C45 and 42CrMo4 steel, induction-hardened on the V and shoulders, in 835 and 415 mm lengths and 805 mm sectioned sets — with DXF profiles for your CNC.
points: 1V dies V18 – V220 mm (.71 – 8.66″), rated to 67 US t/ft (200 t/m); 2V, 4V and 3U dies with holders
Self-centring 1V dies, T dies 80 and 120 mm high, hemming dies — mechanical and pneumatic
ESH insert dies nitrided to 65 HRC; 835 / 415 mm lengths and 805 mm sectioned sets; DXF profiles
faq: How do I choose the V opening?

For mild steel up to about 1/2″, start with a V of 8 times the thickness: V16 (5/8″) for 14 gauge, V24 for 1/8″, V50 for 1/4″. Thicker plate needs 10 to 12 times; aluminum can go to 6 times, stainless wants 8 to 10. A wider V needs less force and gives a larger inside radius (about 1/6 of the V) but a longer minimum flange (about 0.7 × V). The tonnage chart and the guide on the press brake tooling overview page work through it.
1V or 4V die?

A 1V die gives the best support and the highest load rating for one thickness, and the solid 60 mm block is the most rigid. A 4V die puts four openings on one 60 mm block — turn it to change the V — so one die covers a range of gauges, which suits job shops that change thickness several times a day. The 2V dies do the same with two openings.
What is the difference between a T die and a self-centring die?

Both are slim. A T die stands on a 60 mm (2.36″) foot and clamps in the lower beam like any European die; its narrow body leaves room for return flanges. A self-centring die is 14 mm wide and sits on a rail (2058 or 2059) that lines it up under the punch, so changing V openings is quick and needs no alignment.
How does a hemming die work?

In the first stroke the acute V on top of the die pre-bends the flange to about 30° with an acute or hemming punch; in the second stroke the punch closes on the spring-loaded upper plate and flattens the hem. One die and one punch do both steps without a tool change. The pneumatic (PN) versions open and close on shop air.
Can we get the tools as DXF files for our CNC?

Yes — every tool in these tables that has a DXF link can be downloaded straight from the page: the profile drawn in millimetres, ready to import into the tool library of a Delem, ESA or Cybelec control or into offline bending software. For the few tools without one, ask us and we get the drawing from EUROSTAMP.

pages.h1: European-style press brake punches — straight, acute and gooseneck
pages.desc: Straight, acute, gooseneck, sash, ESH same-height, radius and offset punches for Amada-Promecam clamping, made in Italy by EUROSTAMP, with DXF profiles.
pages.intro: EUROSTAMP punches for press brakes with European-style clamping — the Amada-Promecam standard used by Amada and Promecam and by dozens of other makers, from Accurpress, Baykal and Dener to Durmazlar, Ermaksan, Prima Power, Salvagnini and Yawei. Made in Italy from C45 and 42CrMo4 steel, induction-hardened to 55 – 60 HRC on the working surfaces, in 835 mm (32.9″) and 415 mm (16.3″) lengths and 805 mm (31.7″) sectioned sets with horns. Six families on this page: straight punches from 45° to 88° and heavy-duty punches with R6 – R10 tips for plate; acute 24° to 35° punches; gooseneck and sash punches for return flanges; the ESH series with one 120 mm working height for staged bending; radius holders with round elements R3 to R50; and offset (joggle) tools. The punches link to their DXF profiles for your CNC, and NovoTech quotes, ships and supports the tooling from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Straight 45° – 88°, acute 24° – 35°, gooseneck and sash punches 2.56 – 7.87″ (65 – 200 mm) high, rated to 50 US t/ft (150 t/m)
ESH same-height series: every punch 120 mm (4.72″), for staged bending in one setup
Radius holders with round elements R3 – R50 and offset tools Z 1 – 15 mm; DXF profiles to download
faq: Will these punches fit my press brake?

If your press brake clamps European-style (Amada-Promecam) tooling, yes. EUROSTAMP lists Amada, Promecam, Accurpress, Adira, Baykal, Boschert, Bystronic-Beyeler Euro-B, Colgar, Dener, Durmazlar, Ermaksan, Gasparini, Haco, Prima Power, Salvagnini, Yawei and many more as using this style. If you are not sure, send us a photo of the upper clamp and a punch you use now — or the model of the brake — and we confirm before you order. Adapters let other press brakes take these punches.
Straight or gooseneck punch?

A straight punch is stiffer and carries more load, so it is the first choice for open angles and plate. A gooseneck is relieved behind the tip: use it when a flange you have already bent comes back towards the punch — U-channels, pans, boxes with return flanges. The deeper the neck, the lower the load rating, so check the table before you bend thick plate on a gooseneck.
What tip radius should I choose?

In air bending the inside radius is set mostly by the V opening — about 1/6 of the V in mild steel — not by the punch. Choose a punch radius at or below that natural radius: R0.6 to R0.8 for sheet up to about 10 gauge, R1.5 to R3 for 3/16 to 1/4″, and the heavy-duty R6 – R10 punches for plate thicker than about 3/8″, where a sharp tip would crack the outside of the bend. A sharp R0.25 punch gives crisp corners in thin stainless and aluminum.
What are horns and sectioned sets?

A sectioned set is a punch or die cut into pieces that add up to a standard length — for European-style punches 805 mm (31.7″) made of 100 mm horns at each end and 10, 15, 20, 40, 50, 200 and 270 mm pieces. You assemble the exact length of a bend, and the horns — the ends relieved on the outside — let you bend the sides of a box without hitting the flanges already formed.
What is the ESH series?

ESH stands for EUROSTAMP Same Height: every punch in the series — straight, gooseneck, sash, 86°, 60°, 30° and 26° — has the same 120 mm working height, and the matching insert dies the same 60 mm. Several tools can be set up side by side in stations and used without re-setting the ram, which saves set-up time on parts with several different bends.
Can we get the tools as DXF files for our CNC?

Yes — every tool in these tables that has a DXF link can be downloaded straight from the page: the profile drawn in millimetres, ready to import into the tool library of a Delem, ESA or Cybelec control or into offline bending software. For the few tools without one, ask us and we get the drawing from EUROSTAMP.

pages.desc: Fiber laser cutting machines sold in Canada: shuttle table or pallet changer, laser-safe cabin, 4 × 4 ft compact machines to 8.5 × 41 ft, 1.5 to 80 kW.
pages.intro: A fiber laser cutting machine cuts inside a laser-safe cabin with fume extraction, and its shuttle table or pallet changer loads the next sheet while the first is being cut — the production laser that keeps cutting while the operator unloads, and the kind most shops buy from 5 × 10 ft up. NovoTech sells two lines in Canada, both on this page: the premium Dener lasers made in Turkey — the GFL with a space-frame gantry rated for 1.5 G and a shuttle table in 5 × 10 to 6.6 × 20 ft, 3 to 40 kW, and the Smart with a shuttle table in six sizes to 8.5 × 41 ft; and the value line — NovoTech's own ULE with a 15-second shuttle table to 41 ft, the Senfeng H series with pallet changer from 5 × 10 to 8.3 × 40 ft and 1.5 to 80 kW, the NP single-table lasers with a cover on the gantry, and compact lasers of 4 × 4 and 5 × 10 ft from 1.5 kW. Each family below has its full specification table, photos and brochure. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, chiller and nesting software, installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. For long and heavy plate see the large-format plate lasers.

faq: Shuttle table or pallet changer — what is the difference?

Both load the next sheet while the first is cut. A shuttle table (GFL, Smart, ULE, compact) has two tables that swap places in 15 – 30 seconds, one in the cabin cutting and one outside being loaded. A pallet changer (Senfeng H series) lifts the pallet with the cut sheet out of the cabin and slides the loaded pallet in, which is the arrangement a loading tower and sheet storage connect to for lights-out production. For a few sheets an hour the shuttle table is enough; for automation, the pallet changer. Some makers call the shuttle table an exchange table, a double table or a dual table — it is the same thing.
Premium line or value line?

The premium GFL and Smart are built by Dener in Turkey on stress-relieved frames — the GFL rated for 1.5 G — with Boji BLT autofocus heads and Raycus sources (Precitec and IPG on request), longer life at high duty and parts stocked in Canada: the machines for two shifts a day. NovoTech's value-line ULE and the Senfeng H series, NP and compact lasers are built in China with their own or Raycus sources in a wider range — 4 × 4 ft machines, 60 – 80 kW — at a lower price; NovoTech stocks the parts and does the service. Same cut quality at the same power.
What laser power do I need?

Power sets the thickness and the speed. As a guide for mild steel: 3 kW cuts 1/2″, 6 kW 3/4″ (and 1/4″ at over 300 in/min), 12 kW 1″, 20 kW 1-1/4″ and 30 – 40 kW 1-1/2″ and beyond; stainless and aluminum run about 20 – 30 % thinner at the same power, with nitrogen or air assist. Most Canadian job shops buying today choose 6 or 12 kW: thick enough for structural work, fast enough to pay for the machine on thin sheet. Tell us your material mix and we run the cutting chart for you.
Which table size?

The model number is the nominal working area in centimetres: 3015 = 10 × 5 ft (3,000 × 1,500 mm) — a standard 4 × 8 or 5 × 10 sheet; 4020 = 13 × 6.6 ft; 6020 = 20 × 6.6 ft for 6 × 20 plate; 6025 and 8025 = 20 and 26 ft × 8.2 ft; 12526 = 41 × 8.5 ft. The 5 × 10 machine is the Canadian standard; buy the 6020 if you cut 20 ft plate or want to nest several sheets without reloading; the 4 × 4 ft Senfeng compact is for small parts in a small shop.
Can the laser be automated?

Yes — a loading / unloading tower that feeds the pallet changer, sheet storage with several shelves for lights-out production, part sorting, and bevel heads for weld preparation. The Dener GFL and the Smart with shuttle table, the NovoTech ULE and the Senfeng H series are prepared for the tower; the Senfeng coil-fed lines go further and cut straight from the coil. Ask us for the automation layout.
What about assist gas and fume extraction?

Oxygen gives the fastest cut and an oxide edge on mild steel; nitrogen a clean, paint-ready edge on all metals; compressed air at 16 bar replaces nitrogen on sheet to about 1/4″ and cuts the gas bill to near zero — the intelligent air-cutting package is an option on both lines. The machines have pneumatic extraction compartments under the table and connect to a dust collector, which we can supply.
What is in a Dener laser as standard?

A Raycus fiber source, a Boji BLT autofocus cutting head with capacitive height sensing, collision protection and a quick-change optics drawer, a stress-relieved welded frame, six pneumatic fume-extraction compartments under the table and six scrap boxes on wheels, an S&A dual-circuit chiller, the FSCUT control with CypNest nesting software, a handwheel, a light curtain and automatic nozzle cleaning. Cutting gas regulators, dust collector connections and the CSA-approved panel with a 600 V transformer are included in the NovoTech package.
What does the machine need on site?

A level floor, 600 V 3-phase (with the transformer we supply) or 480 V, a chiller (included), assist gas, a dust collector and a compressed-air supply for air cutting. A 6 kW 3015 draws about 46 kW in total (Dener's figure for the GFL) and needs roughly 33 × 20 ft with its shuttle table. Delivery, installation and operator training are done by NovoTech from Mississauga, ON, Canada, and the Ontario pre-start health and safety review is prepared by us.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Sheet metal brakes and folding machines — hand, box and pan, hydraulic
pages.desc: Sheet metal brakes and folding machines sold in Canada, by kind: box and pan brakes, hand brakes, magnetic brakes, hydraulic and CNC folders, roofing brakes.
pages.intro: A sheet metal brake (folder) bends sheet by clamping it under a straight beam and swinging a folding leaf up around the edge — no punch and die, no marks on painted sheet, and long, straight bends in thin material that a press brake cannot hold flat. NovoTech sells six kinds in Canada, each on its own page: box and pan brakes with removable fingers for boxes and pans; straight hand brakes, foot-clamp folding machines and bench brakes for flashing, trim and duct; magnetic brakes that fold boxes of any depth; hydraulic, electric and CNC folding machines for 10 ga over 10 ft and production panels; portable roofing and siding brakes for the job site; and 3-in-1 shear, brake and roll machines for the small shop. Below, the six kinds compared, the questions we get asked and the buying guide. NovoTech's value-line brakes are built in China to our specification, with parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Box and pan brakes 12 – 157″ to 12 ga and 14 ga boxes 9″ deep; hand brakes and foot-clamp folders to 13 ft; bench brakes
Magnetic brakes 2 – 10 ft, 16 ga, boxes of any depth; hydraulic folders 10 ga × 10 ft; TFM / TFMS CNC folders 14 ga × 12 ft
Portable roofing and siding brakes 40″ – 12.5 ft with slitter; 3-in-1 shear, brake and roll machines 8 – 80″
faq: Box and pan brake, hand brake or magnetic brake — which do I need?

A hand (straight) brake has a one-piece clamping blade: the best choice for long straight bends — flashing, trim, duct panels. A box and pan brake has a blade made of removable fingers, so it folds the four sides of a box or a pan; with all the fingers in it works as a straight brake too. A magnetic brake has no clamping beam at all — an electromagnet holds a loose steel bar on the sheet — so it folds boxes of any depth, closed and narrow shapes and short return flanges that a box and pan brake cannot reach, at the cost of a lower capacity (16 ga to 8 ft). For 14 ga and heavier, or for production, choose a hydraulic or electric folding machine.
How are the capacities rated, and what about stainless and aluminum?

Brake capacities are given in gauge of mild steel over the full bending length. Stainless steel bends at about two gauges lighter (a 16 ga brake takes 20 ga stainless), aluminum at about two gauges heavier. Bending at less than full length lets a brake take somewhat heavier sheet; folding heavier material than rated bends the beams permanently.
Can a brake fold painted or coated sheet without marking it?

Yes — that is one of the reasons to fold instead of press-brake bending. The sheet is clamped and the leaf swings around the clamp edge without sliding over a die. The ALB roofing brakes have a silicone insert in the bending beam for pre-painted coil and copper; on the other brakes a strip of protective film on the sheet keeps the finish perfect.
When should I buy a hydraulic folding machine instead of a press brake?

When the work is long panels in thin and medium sheet — duct, enclosures, architectural cladding, flashing — up to 10 ga. A folder bends from one side with the sheet lying flat, so a long panel needs no support or second person, there are no punch and die to change, and painted sheet is not marked. A press brake is the better machine for short heavy parts, for thick plate, for many different bends in one part and for tight tolerances on small flanges.
What does a CNC folding machine add?

A CNC folder (TFM, TFMS) positions the back gauge for every flange and folds to a programmed angle, one bend after the other from a program of up to 99 bends — the operator only turns and feeds the sheet. Programs are stored for repeat parts, the control corrects the angle for springback and folds radii in small steps. It pays for itself on production panels — cladding, cassettes, enclosures, duct — where a hand-set folder needs a skilled operator for every part. The TFMS has a segmented upper beam for boxes.
What do I need to bend roofing flashing on site?

A portable roofing brake: the ALB brakes have an aluminum frame on folding legs, set up in 10 – 15 minutes, take 24 ga steel and 0.032″ aluminum over 7.2 – 12.5 ft, bend to 180° and slit the coil with a roller knife. For the shop, a box and pan brake or a magnetic brake does the same work in heavier gauges.
Do you still sell the brakes from the old website?

The brakes on this page replace the earlier roofing and box and pan brakes. If you need parts or service for a brake you bought from NovoTech before, call us at 647-526-5510 with the model and serial number.

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. pages.h1: H-frame hydraulic presses — production presses, 55 to 661 US tons
pages.desc: H-frame hydraulic presses sold in Canada: premium-line HDT, HSA single-action and HDD deep drawing presses, SMC hot plate and HCFP four-column presses.
pages.intro: An H-frame (straight-side) hydraulic press carries the cylinder in a crown between two side frames, so the frame stays square under load and takes the largest tables and tonnages — the press for dies: forming, blanking, coining, deep drawing and composite moulding, cycle after cycle. A four-column press does the same on four guide posts, open to the die from every side. NovoTech sells two lines in Canada, all on this page, small to large: the premium line, built in Turkey — the HDT Eco H-frame to 276 US tons and the production presses on a welded, machined monoblock frame with Siemens PLC, HMI touchscreen and light barriers — HSA single action, HDD double action deep drawing with a die cushion, SMC / HHRP hot plate presses and HCFP four-column presses, 110 to 661 US tons as standard, the H-frames to 3,307 US tons and the HCFP to 1,102 US tons to order; and the value line, built in China — HP-F four-column presses from 55 to 347 US tons, the F1/PLC models with a touchscreen. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. Parts, installation and service from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Premium line: HDT Eco H-frame presses 110 – 276 US tons with a T-slotted table and two-hand control
Premium-line production presses: HSA single action, HDD deep drawing, SMC / HHRP hot plate and HCFP four-column, 110 – 661 US tons, Siemens PLC and light barriers
NovoTech value line: HP-F four-column presses 55 – 347 US tons, F1/PLC models with touch-screen control
faq: Shop press or production press?

A shop press is operated by hand — joystick or two-hand buttons — for one part at a time: pressing, straightening, bending. A production press runs a die under PLC control with programmed speeds, pressures, dwell and return, light barriers instead of guards, automatic lubrication and remote diagnostics, for thousands of cycles a shift. The NovoTech premium line starts at 33 US tons with the CFS C-frame and goes to 3,307 US tons on the H-frame presses.
Single action or double action — what is a die cushion?

A single action press has one ram. A double action (deep drawing) press adds a die cushion in the lower table — a second cylinder that holds the blank holder with its own programmed force — so a flat blank can be drawn into a deep cup, pan or housing without wrinkling. The HDD H-frame and CFDD C-frame presses have the cushion built in; it is an option on the HCFP column press.
H-frame or four-column?

An H-frame press is the stiffest for its size and takes the widest tables — the choice for deep drawing, long dies and the largest tonnages. A four-column press guides the slide on four posts and is open to the die from all four sides, which suits automation, die loading from the side and parts that overhang the table. The HCFP and HP-F are four-column presses; the HSA, HDD, HHRP and HDT are H-frames.
Can the press be built to my die?

Yes — every series of the premium line is built to order in the table size, stroke, daylight and tonnage the die needs, from a 33 US ton C-frame to a 3,307 US ton H-frame, with quick die change, die loading arms, ejector, heated platens or a die cushion as required. Send us the die drawing and the cycle you need and we quote the press around it.
Premium-line or value-line press?

The premium-line shop and production presses are built in Turkey with European hydraulics and Siemens controls, for daily production work, straightening lines and custom sizes. The value-line presses are built in China for the repair shop, the maintenance department and lighter production — the same tonnages at a lower price, with built-on or separate power units.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Horizontal press brakes — hydraulic horizontal presses, 11 to 165 tons (10 to 150 t)
pages.desc: Horizontal press brakes that bend, punch, shear and straighten flat bar, pipe and busbar: NC hydraulic horizontal presses HP 10 to HP 150, 11 – 165 US tons.
pages.intro: A horizontal press brake is a hydraulic press laid on its side: the ram pushes the tool across a heavy steel table at bench height, so flat bar, angle, channel, pipe, solid bar and busbar lie flat in front of the operator while they are bent, punched, sheared, notched or straightened. With the right tooling one machine does the work of a small press brake, a bar bender, a heavy-wall pipe bender, a punch and a straightening press — the workhorse of maintenance and repair shops, gate, railing and fence makers, trailer and agricultural fabricators and the switchgear builders who bend copper busbar. NovoTech sells the HP series, built in Turkey for its premium line: six NC-controlled models from the 11-ton (10 t) HP 10 to the 110-ton (100 t) HP 100, and the 132- and 165-ton (120 and 150 t) HP 120 and HP 150 with a T-slot table and hardened support columns for straightening heavy sections. Every HP has a touch-screen control stand with manual, automatic and recipe modes and a foot pedal; a servo NC back gauge, a library of bending, punching, shearing, pipe and busbar tools and dies made for your part are available. Installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. NovoTech's value-line HB-10T, HB-25T and HB-40T hydraulic benders, built in China, bend flat bar to 6-1/4 × 1/2″.
points: HP 120 · HP 150: 132 – 165 US tons (120 – 150 t) · 19.7″ stroke · T-slot table and hardened support columns
Touch-screen NC with manual, automatic and recipe modes · servo NC back gauge · bending, punching, pipe and busbar tools
NovoTech value line: HB-10T / 25T / 40T hydraulic horizontal benders, 11 – 44 US tons (10 – 40 t)
faq: What is a horizontal press brake used for?

Bending, punching, shearing, notching and straightening bar stock with the part lying flat on a table at bench height. The ram moves horizontally, so long parts rest on the table and the operator watches the bend from the side. With its tooling one HP replaces a small press brake for flat bar, a bar and pipe bender, a punch and a straightening press: brackets and clamps, U-bolts and hooks, gate and railing parts, pipe saddles and offsets, reduced and expanded pipe ends, bent and punched copper busbar.
Which HP size do I need?

Size the press by the heaviest flat bar you bend the hard way in mild steel: HP 10 – 5-7/8″ × 1/4″, HP 20 – 7-7/8″ × 3/8″, HP 40 – 9-7/8″ × 5/8″, HP 60 – 11-13/16″ × 5/8″, HP 80 – 11-13/16″ × 13/16″, HP 100 – 11-13/16″ × 15/16″, HP 120 and HP 150 – 19-11/16″ × 1-3/16″ and 1-9/16″. Punching takes the most force: a Ø13/16″ hole in 1/2″ mild steel needs about 32 US tons (29 t), so an HP 40 or larger. Stainless steel needs about 1.5 times the force of mild steel.
How does the NC control work?

On the touch-screen of the control stand. In manual mode the ram works between the minimum and maximum stroke you set, while the pedal is pressed — for setting up and single parts. The automatic modes repeat the stroke cycle by cycle for series parts. In recipe mode a part with several operations is stored as a list of positions and run step by step; recipes are saved and reloaded for the next batch.
What does the automatic back gauge add?

A servo-driven NC back gauge, 3.3, 6.6 or 9.8 ft (1, 2 or 3 m) long, positions the part for every step of a recipe, so parts with several bends or holes at set distances come off faster and more repeatably than with a manual stop. Its pull-back retracts the stop while the part bends, so a part that swings against the gauge during the bend is not pushed off position.
Which tools are available?

Bending tools — radius punch with V-die, press brake punch and bolt punch with multi-V dies, narrow V-die, two-sided V and spring-loaded U-bending tools, profile and round bar bending tools; pipe tools — mandrel-less pipe bending, solid bar and thick-wall pipe bending, pipe end reduction and expansion, pipe clamping and pipe notching; wide-radius bending, straightening, punching and shearing tools; and busbar tools for shearing, punching, precision, vertical and Z-bending, corner notching and twisting. Dies are also designed and made for your part — send us the drawing.
Can an HP bend busbar?

Yes — with the busbar tools the HP shears, punches, bends flat and on edge, Z-bends, corner-notches and twists copper and aluminum busbar for switchgear, panel and battery builders, and the recipe mode repeats a busbar with several operations the same way every time.
What power supply does an HP press need?

Three-phase: the HP presses are supplied for 600 V with a CSA-approved panel as standard, and for 208 V, 240 V or 480 V 3-phase on request. Motors run from 1.5 HP on the HP 10 to 15 HP on the HP 100 and 10 HP on the HP 150.

pages.intro: Three-roll plate rolling machines with hydraulic roll positioning and motor-driven rolls: the operator pinches the sheet, pre-bends the leading edge, rolls the cylinder and opens the hydraulic drop-end to take it off. ISITAN's initial-pinch MRM-H covers 2.1 ft to 10 ft and plate to 1/2″ with two digital readouts and cone bending as standard, and the compact 3R HMD puts hydraulic back-roll positioning with a joystick on a cast-iron frame; The double-pinch 3R HS rolls plate to 1-1/8″ with extended shafts for profile rolls, and the translating-type 3R UHS takes plate to 3-1/2″ on 10.2 ft. For sheet and light plate, NovoTech's value-line HER hydraulic slip rolls, built in China, roll 12 ga to 1/2″ over 4 to 10 ft with all three rolls driven hydraulically.

3R HS double-pinch to 1-1/8″ (30 mm) and 3R UHS heavy-duty to 3-1/2″ (90 mm)

faq: How does an initial-pinch 3-roll plate roller work?

The sheet is clamped (pinched) between the top and bottom roll, the back roll is raised to pre-bend the leading edge, the sheet is fed through and rolled to the radius set by the back roll, and the drop-end is opened to remove the cylinder. The trailing edge is pre-bent by turning the sheet around — the one extra step compared with a 4-roll machine.
MRM-H or MRM-S — hydraulic or mechanical?

Both are initial-pinch rolls with the same roll sizes. The MRM-H moves its back and bottom rolls hydraulically and opens the drop-end hydraulically, which is faster, takes thicker plate at the same roll diameter and suits daily production; the MRM-S moves the back roll with a motor and opens the drop-end by hand at a lower price.
What thickness can the MRM-H roll?

From 20 ga sheet on the 1270x80 up to 1/2″ plate on the 250 mm roll models — see the capacity tables, which give the thickness at 1.5× and at 5× the top roll diameter. Capacities are for mild steel; stainless and high-strength plate need the next roll size up.
Plate roller or slip roll?

A slip roll is a light three-roll machine for sheet — duct, flues, tanks, hoppers, signage — with a top roll that swings out to slip the finished cylinder off. A plate roller rolls heavier plate and pre-bends the edges so the cylinder closes round. The HER hydraulic slip rolls bridge the two: all three rolls driven hydraulically, 12 ga to 1/2″ over 6′7″.

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase.

pages.h1: Hydraulic 4-roll plate rollers — NC and CNC machines, 2 to 20 ft
pages.desc: Hydraulic 4-roll plate rolling machines from 2.1 to 20 ft and plate to 3-3/8″, with NC / CNC control, cone rolls and automation. CSA panels, Canadian parts.
pages.intro: Four-roll plate rolling machines pinch the sheet between the top and bottom roll and bend it with two side rolls, so the plate is pre-bent at both ends and rolled into a full cylinder in one pass without flipping it. Two Turkish makers cover the whole range: ISITAN's 4R HMS hydraulic plate rollers run from a 2.1 ft bench-size roll to 10.2 ft machines for 3/8″ plate, with NC control, overhead crane and sheet feeder for production work, and the 4R OM and 4R HOM roll corrugated galvanized sheet; The 4R HS-L, 4R HS and heavy-duty 4R HSS go on to 20 ft and 3-3/8″ plate for wind towers, vessels and shipyards, with the NC cassette-type 4RH and the 4R HC cone roll beside them. Every 4 roll plate roller is sold with a CSA-approved panel and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: ISITAN 4R HMS: 36 models from 2.1 ft to 10.2 ft (650–3100 mm), up to 1/2″ (12 mm)

faq: 3-roll or 4-roll plate roller — which one do I need?

A 4-roll machine holds the sheet pinched between the top and bottom roll while the side rolls pre-bend and roll it, so both ends are pre-bent without turning the plate around and the operator never loses alignment — the better choice for production, thin or polished material and cones. A 3-roll initial-pinch machine does the same job with one more handling step at a lower price, which is why most job shops start with an MRM-H or MRM-S.
What does "capacity at 1.5× / 5× top roll Ø" mean?

Plate rolls are rated for a given diameter: the thicker the plate, the larger the minimum cylinder it can form. The manufacturer states two figures — the thickness the machine rolls into a tight cylinder of 1.5 times the top roll diameter, and the thickness it rolls at 5 times the top roll diameter. Tell us your plate thickness and the smallest diameter you make and we will size the machine from the capacity chart.
Can a 4R HMS roll cones?

Yes — a cone-bending device is standard on every 4R HMS, and the NC control stores the roll positions for repeat cones. Hydraulic side supports and the overhead crane keep large cones and thin material in shape while rolling.
How automatic can a plate roller be?

With the NC control the operator programs the roll positions once; the machine then bends to the stored program. Adding the vacuum sheet feeder, the hydraulic overhead crane and the part ejector turns the 4R HMS into a full automation line where the operator only loads blanks and removes finished cylinders at the welding station.

pages.h1: Hydraulic and CNC sheet metal folding machines — up to 10 ga × 10 ft
pages.desc: Powered sheet metal folding machines sold in Canada: hydraulic folders 10 ga × 4 – 10 ft and 3/16″ × 80 – 100″, electric and CNC folders 14 ga over 12 ft.
pages.intro: A powered folding machine clamps and folds the sheet with hydraulic cylinders or electric drives, so a 10 ft bend in 10 ga takes a foot pedal instead of two people and a CNC folder runs a 99-bend program with its back gauge while the operator only turns and feeds the sheet. NovoTech sells three kinds in Canada, all on this page: HW hydraulic folding machines, 10 ga over 4 to 10 ft with a manual back gauge, and the HW…E NC models with a touch screen and a servo back gauge, 3/16″ over 80 – 100″ and 10 ga over 10 ft — both with a hydraulic clamping beam, a folding beam driven by cylinders and segmented upper tools for boxes; EFM / EFMS electric folding machines, 16 to 20 ga over 80 – 120″, for the shop that wants power without hydraulics; and TFM / TFMS CNC electric folders, 14 ga over 122 and 145″, with a CNC back gauge to 48″ and ±0.004″ repeatability for production panels, cassettes and enclosures. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. NovoTech's value-line machines are built in China to our specification, with parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: HW hydraulic folders 10 ga × 4 – 10 ft with manual back gauge · HW…E NC folders 3/16″ × 80 – 100″ with touch screen and servo back gauge
TFM / TFMS CNC folders 14 ga × 122 – 145″: CNC back gauge 1/2 – 48-3/8″, ±0.004″, 99-bend programs, segmented beam on the TFMS
EFM / EFMS electric folders 16 – 20 ga × 80 – 120″: motor-driven clamping and folding, no hydraulics
faq: When should I buy a folding machine instead of a press brake?

When the work is long panels in thin and medium sheet — duct, enclosures, architectural cladding, flashing — up to 10 ga. A folder bends from one side with the sheet lying flat, so a long panel needs no support or second person, there are no punch and die to change, and painted sheet is not marked. A press brake is the better machine for short heavy parts, for thick plate, for many different bends in one part and for tight tolerances on small flanges.
Hydraulic, electric or CNC?

Hydraulic for the heaviest work — 10 ga over 10 ft and 3/16″ over 8 ft — and the lowest price per foot of capacity. Electric for 16 – 20 ga sheet where the shop wants powered clamping and folding without a hydraulic unit, oil or a three-phase pump. CNC when the same panels are made every day: the back gauge positions each flange from the program, the angle is corrected for springback and radii are folded in small steps, so an unskilled operator makes the part right first time.
What does a CNC folding machine add?

A CNC folder (TFM, TFMS) positions the back gauge for every flange and folds to a programmed angle, one bend after the other from a program of up to 99 bends — the operator only turns and feeds the sheet. Programs are stored for repeat parts, the control corrects the angle for springback and folds radii in small steps. It pays for itself on production panels — cladding, cassettes, enclosures, duct — where a hand-set folder needs a skilled operator for every part. The TFMS has a segmented upper beam for boxes.
How are the capacities rated, and what about stainless and aluminum?

In gauge (or inches) of mild steel over the full bending length; the specification tables give the stainless rating separately — about two gauges lighter — and aluminum goes about two gauges heavier. Folding at less than full length lets the machine take somewhat heavier sheet.
Can a folding machine fold painted or coated sheet without marking it?

Yes — that is one of the reasons to fold instead of press-brake bending: the sheet is clamped and the beam swings around the clamp edge without sliding over a die. Protective film on the sheet keeps pre-painted and brushed stainless perfect.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
