pages.h1: Hydraulic press brakes — CNC, hybrid and NC, 33 to 1,323 US tons (30 to 1,200 t)
pages.desc: Hydraulic press brakes sold, installed and supported in Canada: CNC brakes from 55 to 1,323 US tons, the mild hybrid XL and NC torsion-bar brakes from 33.
pages.intro: A hydraulic press brake bends sheet and plate between a punch and a V-die with two hydraulic cylinders, giving full force over the whole stroke at the lowest price per ton — the machine for plate, long parts and production. NovoTech sells three kinds in Canada, all on this page: CNC hydraulic press brakes with linear scales, servo valves, crowning and a graphic control — the premium Dener XL in 18 models from 66 to 661 US tons (60 to 600 t) and 5 to 20 ft, and NovoTech's own value line from 55 to 331 tons (50 to 300 t), heavy-duty and tandem to 1,323 tons (1,200 t) and 26 ft; hybrid press brakes — the mild hybrid servo motor and pump, an option on every XL that cuts energy by 42 – 58 %; and NC torsion-bar press brakes from 33 to 441 tons (30 to 400 t) for repeat parts in one material. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel and a 1-year warranty, and is installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. For a brake with no hydraulic oil see the electric press brakes; for 33 – 66 ton (30 – 60 t) machines over 4 – 5 ft, the compact press brakes.
points: CNC hydraulic: premium line 66 – 661 US tons (60 – 600 t) × 5 – 20 ft (ESA / Delem, 6-axis gauges); value line 55 – 331 tons (50 – 300 t), heavy-duty to 1,323 tons (1,200 t) × 26 ft
Hybrid: the mild hybrid servo pump on any XL — 42 – 58 % less energy, 17 – 75 % faster approach and return, quieter — and standard on every value-line WAD
NC torsion-bar 33 – 441 tons (30 – 400 t) with Estun control for repeat parts in one material — the simplest hydraulic brake to run and maintain
faq: CNC, hybrid or NC — which hydraulic press brake do I need?

A CNC brake measures the ram on linear scales and corrects it through servo valves, calculates the bend from the drawing, crowns the bed and changes material in the program — the machine for mixed work, tight angles and multi-bend parts, and the one most Canadian shops buy. The hybrid is a CNC brake with a servo pump: it costs a little more and pays it back in power, speed and noise when the brake runs all day. An NC brake positions the back gauge and the ram depth from a stored program with the cylinders kept in step by a torsion bar — rigid, cheap to maintain, right for the same parts in one material every day. For 4 – 7 ft work in sheet up to 8 ga, where a 100-ton (91 t) machine is more than you need, see the compact press brakes.
Premium line or value line?

The premium Dener XL is built in Turkey on the heaviest frame, with ESA or Delem controls, back gauges to 6 axes, sheet followers, robot cells and parts stocked in Canada — the machines for plate, 3/8″ and 1/2″ over 10 to 20 ft, two shifts, a long options list. NovoTech's value line is the same architecture — monoblock frame, servo valves, linear scales, Delem control — built in China to our specification at about two-thirds of the price: the right buy for a job shop that needs a 100 – 300 ton (91 – 272 t) CNC brake or an NC brake for repeat parts, and the only line that goes to 1,323 tons (1,200 t) and 26 ft. Both are installed and supported by the same NovoTech technicians.
How much tonnage and length do I need?

Air bending takes F = S² × 2 × R ÷ (1.4 × V) tonnes per metre of bend — the sheet thickness S and the V opening V in millimetres, the tensile strength R = 47 kg/mm² for mild steel (70 for stainless, 25 for aluminum), the formula behind the EUROSTAMP and Dener bending charts; in inches and US tons per foot it reads 575 × t² ÷ V. With the standard V of about 8 × the thickness, 3 mm needs about 24 t/m (8 US tons per foot), 6 mm 48 t/m (16), 1/4″ 54 t/m (18), 3/8″ in a 3″ V 80 t/m (27) and 1/2″ in a 5″ V 85 t/m (29). Multiply by the bend length and add about 20 % in reserve: 3 m × 6 mm is a 175-ton (159 t) press brake, 10 ft × 1/4″ a 200 – 220 US ton (181 – 200 t) machine, 10 ft × 3/8″ a 300 – 320 ton (272 – 290 t) machine and 13 ft × 1/2″ a 400 – 450 ton (363 – 408 t) machine. The tonnage calculator in the buying guide on the press brake page does the arithmetic for your thickness and length; tell us your thickest and longest bend and we size the brake and the tooling.
What is a hybrid press brake?

On a conventional hydraulic brake the motor and pump run at full speed all day, whether the ram moves or not. A hybrid drives the hydraulics with servo motors, so the pump turns only while the ram moves, at the speed the ram needs. Dener builds it two ways. The mild hybrid, an option on every XL, keeps the XL's hydraulic circuit and replaces only the AC motor and fixed pump with a servo motor and servo pump: Dener measures 42 – 58 % energy saving and 17 – 75 % faster approach and return against the standard XL, with less heat in the oil and a quieter shop, and everything else — frame, cylinders, valves, tooling, controls — is the XL. On NovoTech's value line, every WAD CNC brake has the mild hybrid drive as standard.
Which control comes with the machine?

The premium XL comes with the 15.6″ ESA S840 2D graphic touch-screen control (Delem DA-66S / 69S and the ESA S875 W 3D control are options): draw the profile, the control calculates the bend sequence, tonnage, back-gauge positions and crowning and checks the part for collisions with the tools and the machine. The value-line CNC brakes come with the 15″ Delem DA-53Tx — the 18.5″ DA-58Tx (2D graphic), the 24″ DA-66S and DA-69S, the ESA S840 and S875 W and the Cybelec CybTouch 12 are options; the NC brakes with the Estun E21PS (E315PS, Delem DA-41T or ESA S630 as options). All program in inches or millimetres, and the buying guide on the press brake page compares every one of them.
What back gauge and axes are available?

Every CNC machine has the Y1 and Y2 ram axes and an X back-gauge axis on a ball screw and linear guides. Options go up to the 6-axis gauge with X1, X2, R1, R2, Z1 and Z2 — two independently positioned fingers for angled flanges — plus a CNC crowning axis; the NC brakes have X and the depth stop. The back gauge is set by the control for every bend of the program.
What tooling fits, and do you stock it?

European-style (Promecam / Amada) segmented tooling fits every line: the premium Dener brakes carry European-style top-tool holders, the value-line brakes their own clamping, and a sectioned punch set with a 2-V or 4-V die ships with every machine (a 4-V die with the Dener brakes, a 2-V die with the value line) — tell us which tooling standard your shop already has and we fit the holders to match. NovoTech stocks Eurostamp press brake tooling in Canada — punches, dies, radius, hemming and joggle tools, gooseneck and special profiles — and sizes it to your machine; quick-release, pneumatic and Wila hydraulic clamping and American-style adapters are options, not standard equipment.
What about safety and the Ontario pre-start review?

Side guards, an enclosed rear guard, interlocked doors and an anti-panic foot pedal with emergency stop are standard; DSP laser finger protection is standard on the WAD CNC press brakes and the Dener XL, and on the other machines DSP or Fiessler laser protection and light curtains are options we recommend for every CNC press brake. In Ontario a new press brake needs a pre-start health and safety review (PSR) under Regulation 851 before it runs.
Do you deliver, install and service in Canada?

Yes — NovoTech sells, installs and supports press brakes across Canada and the United States. Installation, commissioning and operator training are free of charge in the Greater Toronto Area; outside the GTA our technicians do the same work at an additional charge. Parts are stocked in Canada. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, 600 V standard (208 / 240 / 480 V on request), a 1-year warranty and remote diagnostics through the control.
What does delivery cost, and who unloads the machine?

A press brake ordered from the factory (back-ordered) travels in its container straight from the port, customs and the rail yard to your plant door: in the Greater Toronto Area that delivery is free; outside the GTA the freight is quoted and charged. A machine from NovoTech's stock is loaded, shipped and unloaded at the buyer's cost. In every case unloading is the buyer's responsibility and expense — the crane or forklift, the rigging and moving the machine onto its foundation — so book a rigger for the delivery day; we are glad to recommend riggers who know press brakes and to tell you the weight and lifting points.
Is the hydraulic oil included?

No — the hydraulic oil is bought by the customer. Before commissioning, fill the tank with ISO VG 46 anti-wear hydraulic oil (AW 46) in the quantity shown in the specification table for your model; our technician checks the level and bleeds the system during installation. Electric press brakes have no hydraulic oil at all.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Hydraulic presses — shop, H-frame, C-frame and straightening presses
pages.desc: Hydraulic presses sold, installed and supported in Canada, by kind: shop and bench presses from 10 to 551 US tons, H-frame and four-column presses to 661.
pages.intro: A hydraulic press drives its ram with an oil cylinder — slowly, with the full force available anywhere in the stroke and a pressure you set — which is why the same kind of machine presses bearings, straightens shafts, bends plate and punches, forms and deep-draws sheet in a die. NovoTech sells four kinds in Canada, each on its own page: hydraulic shop presses — the H-frame workshop press of every repair shop, dealer and fabricator, from a 10-ton bench press to 551 US tons; H-frame hydraulic presses — straight-side and four-column production presses for dies, deep drawing and composite moulding, from 55 to 661 US tons and to 3,307 US tons to order; C-frame hydraulic presses — open on three sides for small dies, punching and assembly, from 22 to 276 US tons; and hydraulic straightening presses — portal and 3-axis presses whose cylinder travels to the bend over beams, plate and shafts, from 22 to 441 US tons. The premium line is built in Turkey with European hydraulics and Siemens controls, the value line in China for the repair shop and lighter production. Below, the four kinds compared, every model in one table, the buying guide and the questions we get asked; every press comes with a CSA-approved panel and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Hydraulic shop presses: premium-line DPM , mobile-cylinder DPM-K / DK, AT and AP, 33 – 220 US tons; value-line bench and workshop presses
H-frame hydraulic presses: premium-line HSA, HDD deep drawing and HCFP four-column to 661 US tons; value-line HP-F four-column
C-frame presses 22 – 276 US tons · straightening presses 22 – 441 US tons
faq: Which kind of hydraulic press do I need?

By the work. For pressing bearings, bushings and pins, straightening shafts and bending flat bar one part at a time, a shop press. For dies — forming, blanking, coining, deep drawing — run cycle after cycle under PLC control, an H-frame or four-column press, or a C-frame press when the dies are small and quick access matters more than table size. For beams, plate and long parts straightened where they lie, a straightening press with a moving cylinder. Send us the part and the force and we size the press.
What tonnage shop press do I need?

Most truck, equipment and fabrication shops run a 66 – 110 US ton press (DPM 1040-60 to DPM 1570-100, or the value-line HPP-60 and HPP-100): enough for pressing bearings and bushings, straightening shafts to Ø3″ and bending flat bar. Go to 165 – 220 US tons for large bearings, track pins, heavy shafts and forming plate. Beams and plate that need a moving ram are on the straightening press page.
H-frame, four-column or C-frame?

An H-frame (straight-side) press is the stiffest and takes the largest tables and tonnages — the choice for deep drawing and big dies. A four-column (column) press is open on all sides for die access and automation. A C-frame press is open on three sides, so small dies go in and out quickly and the press takes less floor space; its table size is limited because the C deflects, which is why the premium-line C-frame range stops at 276 US tons.
Premium-line or value-line press?

The premium-line shop and production presses are built in Turkey with European hydraulics and Siemens controls, for daily production work, straightening lines and custom sizes. The value-line presses are built in China for the repair shop, the maintenance department and lighter production — the same tonnages at a lower price, with built-on or separate power units.
Can the press be built to my die?

Yes — every series of the premium line is built to order in the table size, stroke, daylight and tonnage the die needs, from a 33 US ton C-frame to a 3,307 US ton H-frame, with quick die change, die loading arms, ejector, heated platens or a die cushion as required. Send us the die drawing and the cycle you need and we quote the press around it.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Hydraulic punching machines — single and double head, 33 to 193 tons
pages.desc: Hydraulic punching machines for plate, angle and flat bar: single-head HPM 30–175, double-head HPM DP, Siemens CNC punches and NC lines, holes to Ø2-1/4″.
pages.intro: A hydraulic punching machine (hydraulic punch press) makes round, oblong and shaped holes in plate, angle, flat bar and sections with a punch and die in one stroke — faster and cleaner than drilling, with no chips. The HPM range starts with the 33 US ton HPM 30 and 44 US ton HPM 40 bench-height punches, continues with the 72 to 193 US ton HPM 65 – 175 with a 24.6″ throat for holes to Ø2-1/4″ in plate to 1-1/4″, and grows into the HPM DP double-head punches for two operators, the HPM CNC with a 120 × 20″ Siemens-controlled table for bolted steel-construction parts and the HPM / HKM NC punching and cutting lines that copy hole patterns along angles, flat bar and beams. Punches and dies interchange with the HKM ironworkers. Supplied with a CSA-approved panel and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: HPM 30 – 175 single-station punches — 33 to 193 US tons, holes Ø1/4″ to Ø2-1/4″, throat to 24.6″
HPM DP double-head, HPM CNC with 120 × 20″ Siemens table, HPM / HKM NC feeding lines
Hydraulic stripper, press-brake tool, large-hole and section punching tools optional
faq: Punching machine or ironworker?

If holes are most of the work — base plates, gussets, clips, flat-bar brackets — a dedicated HPM punch has a deeper 24.6″ throat, a free table and a working height set for punching, and it can be fitted with an NC or CNC table. If you also shear angle, bar and flat and notch corners, the HKM ironworker puts all of it on one machine; the punches and dies are the same on both.
How thick can a hydraulic punch go?

Each model is rated for a hole diameter × thickness at its tonnage: Ø7/8″ × 3/8″ on the HPM 30, Ø1 × 13/16″ on the HPM 65, Ø1-5/8 × 1-1/4″ on the HPM 175. Larger holes in thinner plate are punched with the large-hole tool up to Ø4-7/8″ × 3/16″. The rule of thumb for mild steel is tonnage = hole circumference × thickness × 25 (US tons, inches).
What does the CNC table do?

The HPM CNC moves the plate under the punch on a 120 × 20″ table with X 63″ and Y 23.6″ travel at ±0.004″, so a hole pattern programmed once — by hand (MDI) or from a CAM file — repeats on every part. It is the machine for bolted steel-construction plates where every hole must line up with the mating member; an optional 3-head unit on the 115 and 175 keeps three tools ready.
What is an NC punching and cutting line?

An HPM punch or HKM ironworker with a 307 × 31″ NC feeding table: angles, flat bar and IPN / UPN beams are fed along the X axis to 244″ and the control copies the hole pattern at ±0.004″; on the HKM NC version the shear station then cuts the punched bar to length. It is the economical alternative to a CNC angle line for bracing, towers and ladders.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Hydraulic shears — swing beam and guillotine shears, 16 ga to 1-9/16″
pages.desc: Hydraulic shearing machines sold in Canada: swing beam shears 5/32″ – 3/4″ × 6.8 – 20 ft, variable-rake guillotines 1/4″ – 1-9/16″, light shears from 16 ga.
pages.intro: A hydraulic shear cuts sheet and plate to size in one stroke between a fixed lower blade and a moving upper blade driven by two hydraulic cylinders; the back gauge sets the width, hydraulic hold-downs keep the sheet flat and the control counts the strokes. It is the shear for plate — from 16 ga to 1-9/16″ and 26 ft here — where tonnage matters more than strokes per minute. NovoTech sells three kinds in Canada, all on this page: swing beam shears, the rugged everyday plate shear with the beam swung through the cut on two bearings — the premium BS / BSY to 5/8″ over 13.5 ft and the value-line QC12K from 5/32″ to 3/4″ over 20 ft; guillotine shears with a variable rake angle on a beam carried straight down on rollers, so thin sheet is cut flat and 3/4″ plate with less distortion — the premium DAS CNC to 3/4″ × 20 ft with the ESA 630 control and the value-line Q11K to 1-9/16″ × 26 ft; and the THS, HQ11 and HQ01 light hydraulic shears from 16 ga to 1/4″ over 51 – 120″ for the sheet-metal shop. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel and a 1-year warranty, installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. For sheet to 1/4″ all day with no hydraulics — guillotine, electric, bench and coil machines — see the mechanical shears.
points: Swing beam: premium BS / BSY 1/4″ – 5/8″ × 6.8 – 13.5 ft with NC back gauge; value QC12K 5/32″ – 3/4″ × 8 – 20 ft with Estun E21S
Guillotine: premium DAS CNC 1/4″ – 3/4″ × 10 – 20 ft, variable angle, ESA 630, 1 m ball-screw gauge; value Q11K 1/4″ – 1-9/16″ × 8 – 26 ft
Light hydraulic shears 16 ga – 1/4″ × 51 – 120″: THS, HQ11 and HQ01, quick-set blade clearance, manual, electric or NC back gauge
faq: Swing beam or guillotine shear?

A swing beam shear pivots the upper blade on two bearings and drives it down with two cylinders: a simple, rigid machine with few moving parts, a fixed cutting angle and a slightly curved blade path — the right shear for most fabrication shops cutting 5/32″ to 1/2″ sheet. A guillotine shear carries the blade beam on linear rollers so it comes straight down, and the rake angle is set by the control: thin sheet is cut at 0.5° fast and flat, thick plate at 3° or 4° with less twist and less force — the production machine, and the only choice above 3/4″.
Premium line or value line?

The premium BS / BSY and DAS shears are built by Dener in Turkey with European hydraulics, ESA or Delem controls, the heaviest frames and parts stocked in Canada — the machines for two shifts a day and the tightest, flattest cut, with the DAS CNC setting rake, gap and gauge from the material keyed in. NovoTech's value-line QC12K and Q11K are the same two designs — swing beam and variable-rake guillotine — built in China to our specification with Estun controls and Siemens motors at about two-thirds of the price, in more sizes (to 1-9/16″ and 26 ft). Both lines are installed and supported by the same NovoTech technicians, and the light hydraulic shears below them are the value-line answer for 16 ga to 1/4″.
What thickness and length do I need?

Capacities are rated for mild steel of 65,000 psi; stainless cuts about 60 % of the rated thickness and aluminum about 150 %. Choose the length from the sheet you buy: 8 ft (2,500 mm) for 4 × 8 sheet cut across, 10 ft (3,200 mm) for 5 × 10 sheet, 13 ft and up for plate. The 1/4″ × 10 ft swing beam shear (QC12K-6×3200) is the Canadian standard; a shop cutting 3/8″ and 1/2″ plate daily should look at the 10 or 13 mm guillotine.
Which control?

The BS / BSY come with an NC control for the back gauge and the stroke counter; the DAS with the ESA 630 CNC — back gauge, blade gap, cutting angle and stroke length programmed per material, with a parts memory and a 1 m ball-screw back gauge with retract. Delem controls are available on request.
What does the Estun E21S control do?

It positions the motorised back gauge (0.8 – 25.6″, 31.5″ on the long machines) with a servo, sets the cutting angle and displays the blade clearance from an encoder, counts strokes and stores 40 programs of 25 steps, in inches or millimetres; a retract function pulls the gauge back after the cut so the strip falls free. The E200PS and the Delem DAC-360T add programmable blade-gap adjustment.
What is standard on a Dener shear?

Hydraulic hold-downs (16 – 33 on the DAS), a squaring arm with scale, front support arms, a ball-transfer table, a shadow-line light, a photocell rear guard, a front finger guard, high-carbon high-chrome four-edged blades and the CSA-approved panel with a 600 V transformer. Pneumatic sheet supports with return-to-front, conveyors and longer arms are options.
How is the sheet supported?

Ball-transfer front tables, a squaring arm with scale and front support arms are standard; the back gauge carries support fingers and the cut strip drops onto the rear slide. A pneumatic sheet support that holds the piece during the cut and returns it to the front, a conveyor for strips and longer front arms are options for thin, large or finished sheet.
Floor space and power?

A 10 ft shear needs about 16 × 10 ft of floor with the back gauge travel; a 20 ft DAS about 27 × 12 ft. 600 V 3-phase with the supplied transformer or 480 V; the motors run from 15 to 60 HP. We lay the machine out for your building before you order.
What about safety and the Ontario pre-start review?

Finger guards along the blade, rear guard fences or photocells / light curtains, an anti-repeat single-stroke control and a mobile foot pedal with emergency stop are standard or available on every line; we recommend the photocell or light-curtain rear guard on every powered shear. In Ontario a new shear needs a pre-start health and safety review (PSR) under Regulation 851 before it runs.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Hydraulic shop presses — workshop and bench presses, 10 to 551 US tons
pages.desc: Hydraulic shop presses sold in Canada: premium-line DPM, DPM-K / DK, AT T-slot presses and AP press brakes from 33 to 220 US tons, value-line from 10.
pages.intro: A hydraulic shop press is the machine every repair shop, truck and equipment dealer and fabricator reaches for several times a day: pressing bearings, bushings and pins, straightening shafts and bar, bending flat bar and short plate, pushing a die for the odd forming job. NovoTech sells two lines in Canada, all on this page, small to large: the premium line, built in Turkey — DPM H-frame shop presses from 33 to 220 US tons (30 to 200 t) with two-speed joystick control, a pressure gauge and a relief valve against overload, and the DPM-K and DK presses whose cylinder travels across the frame on a hand wheel, so the ram meets the work instead of the work being shifted under the ram, the AT presses with T-slot tables for your own dies and the AP garage-type press brake for 1/4″ and 3/8″ plate, 110 to 165 US tons (100 to 150 t); and the value line, built in China — the EBP-10T hydraulic bench press for sheet-metal and louver tooling, the EBP-25T motorized workshop press of 28 US tons (25 t), the HPB presses with a brake function from 33 to 331 US tons (30 to 300 t), the HP motorized H-frame presses from 33 to 551 US tons (30 to 500 t) and the HPP-60 to HPP-160 motorized workshop presses with a moving cylinder, 66 to 176 US tons (60 to 160 t). Each family below has its full specification table and photos. For die work and production, see the H-frame and C-frame presses; for beams and plate, the straightening presses. Parts, installation and service from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Premium-line DPM shop presses 33 – 220 US tons: working widths 30.5″ to 61.8″, two-speed joystick, gauge and relief valve
DPM-K and DK with a mobile cylinder on a hand wheel; AT T-slot presses and AP press brakes 110 – 165 US tons (100 – 150 t)
NovoTech value line: EBP-10T bench press, EBP-25T workshop press, HPB brake presses, HP H-frame presses, HPP-60 – HPP-160 motorized workshop presses
faq: What tonnage shop press do I need?

Most truck, equipment and fabrication shops run a 66 – 110 US ton press (DPM 1040-60 to DPM 1570-100, or the value-line HPP-60 and HPP-100): enough for pressing bearings and bushings, straightening shafts to Ø3″ and bending flat bar. Go to 165 – 220 US tons for large bearings, track pins, heavy shafts and forming plate. Beams and plate that need a moving ram are on the straightening press page.
What do the model numbers mean — DPM 1040-60?

The first number is the clear working width between the columns in millimetres (1040 mm = 40.9″) and the second the press force in metric tons (60 t = 66 US tons). A 1570-100 press is 61.8″ wide at 110 US tons.
Why a mobile (sliding) cylinder?

On the DPM-K and DK the cylinder head travels across the frame on a hand wheel, so the ram comes to the work — a long shaft, a frame rail or a plate stays clamped while you straighten it point by point instead of shifting the part under a fixed ram. The DK series adds a wider 61.8″ – 74.8″ frame. The value-line HPP presses also have a cylinder that moves across the frame.
Hand pump, foot pedal or joystick?

The DPM and DPM-K presses come with two-speed joystick control; a hand pump for fine pressing, a foot pedal and a limit switch that stops the stroke at a set height are options. The value-line HPP presses pair the motorized two-step unit with a double-acting hand pump for fine positioning, and the EBP-25T has infinitely variable pressure and speed.
Can a press bend plate?

The AP garage-type press brake is a hydraulic press delivered with a 5-face prism bottom die and hardened top blade for bending 1/4″ (110 US tons) or 3/8″ (165 US tons) mild steel over 40″ or 60″ — the economical way to bend brackets and short plate without a full press brake. The value-line HPB presses are set up the same way, with replaceable top tools, a V-block and a support table with stops; the twin-cylinder D models bend widths of 47 – 71″. The AT press has T-slot tables for bolting your own forming, blanking and coining dies.
What is the EBP-10T bench press for?

The sheet-metal and HVAC shop: its 25″ throat and 6″ tool opening take the industry-standard bench and louver press tooling, so it punches round, square and oblong holes, punches and flares or beads, cuts louvers, notches corners, bends 90° in 3/8″ mild steel and shears 16 ga — and it works as a hydraulic arbor press as well.
Premium-line or value-line press?

The premium-line shop and production presses are built in Turkey with European hydraulics and Siemens controls, for daily production work, straightening lines and custom sizes. The value-line presses are built in China for the repair shop, the maintenance department and lighter production — the same tonnages at a lower price, with built-on or separate power units.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Hydraulic straightening presses — portal and 3-axis, 22 to 441 US tons
pages.desc: Hydraulic straightening presses sold in Canada: premium-line HSPS portal presses 110 – 441 US tons, DK-S 3-axis moving presses and sliding-table presses.
pages.intro: A straightening press leaves the workpiece lying still on the bed and brings the ram to the bend: the cylinder travels along a gantry and the gantry along the bed, or the press head moves on three axes, so a long beam, a plate, a rail, a shaft or a pipe is straightened point by point without craning it under a fixed ram. NovoTech's premium line, built in Turkey, has two families, small to large: the HSPS portal (gantry) straightening presses from 110 to 441 US tons, with beds from 39.4 × 78.7″ to 59.1 × 137.8″, the cylinder travelling along the gantry on a rack drive and the gantry along the bed; and the DK-S 3-axis moving straightening presses from 220 to 441 US tons, whose cylinder moves on X, Y and Z by motorized gear drive over a 100″ bed, with a remote control as an option; and NovoTech's value line, built in China — the HP-M1 presses from 22 to 220 US tons, whose table slides out of the frame, so large and heavy parts are loaded outside the press and rolled in. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. For shafts and bar in a repair shop, a shop press with a mobile cylinder is often enough. Parts, installation and service from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: HSPS portal straightening presses 110 – 441 US tons: beds 39.4 × 78.7″ to 59.1 × 137.8″, stroke 15.7 – 23.6″
DK-S 3-axis moving straightening presses 220 – 441 US tons: the head travels over a 100″ bed, 11.8″ stroke, remote control optional
Value-line HP-M1 presses with a sliding table, 22 – 220 US tons: parts loaded outside the press and rolled in
faq: Portal (HSPS) or 3-axis (DK-S)?

Both leave the workpiece on the bed and move the ram to the bend. The HSPS is a gantry that runs along the bed on a rack drive, with beds to 59.1 × 137.8″ — the choice for long beams, rails and plate. The DK-S carries its cylinder on X, Y and Z over a 100″ bed with motorized gear drives, from 220 to 441 US tons, for heavy plate, beams, profiles and round bar.
Which press for my parts?

It depends on the section, the material and the distance between the supports: the press has to bend the part slightly past straight. Send us the profile or the shaft diameter, the material grade, the length and how far it is out of straight, and we size the press, the bed and the supports.
Can a shop press straighten too?

Yes, for shafts, bar and smaller sections that can be moved under the ram. The DPM-K and DK shop presses carry the cylinder across the frame on a hand wheel, so a shaft or a frame rail stays clamped while it is straightened point by point. For beams, plate and parts too heavy or too long to move, a straightening press brings the ram to the work.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Ironworkers — hydraulic ironworker machines, 44 to 276 US tons
pages.desc: Hydraulic ironworkers sold in Canada, 44 – 276 US tons: punch, shear bar, angle and flat, and notch in one machine. HKM single- and double-piston, Q35Y.
pages.intro: A hydraulic ironworker (also sold as a steelworker or universal punch and shear) puts the five jobs of the structural shop on one machine: punching, round and square bar shear, angle shear at 90° and 45°, flat-bar and sheet shear and rectangular notching, each with its own station and LED light. The HKM range runs from the 44 US ton HKM 40 to the 193 US ton HKM 175 in two designs: single-piston machines in which one cylinder serves every station — compact and economical — and double-piston machines with two cylinders and two foot pedals so two operators punch and shear at the same time. Punches to Ø1-1/2″ are standard on every model; large-hole, section punching, beam and tee blades, V-notching, press-brake and keyway tools are optional. Below the NovoTech premium-line machines is NovoTech's own value line, the Q35Y single-cylinder ironworkers from 55 to 276 US tons, built in China to our specification and sold under our name with the tooling included. All sold with a CSA-approved panel and installed, tooled and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. The value line also has the compact M50, M55 and M60 ironworkers — 50 to 60 tons on one cylinder.
points: Single-piston HKM 40 · 45 · 60 · 65 V — 44 to 72 US tons, 4 – 5 work stations
Double-piston HKM 55 · 65 · 85 · 115 · 175 — 61 to 193 US tons, two operators at once
Angle to L 7-7/8 × 7-7/8 × 13/16″, flat bar to 15 × 1-1/8″, holes to Ø2-1/4″ in 7/8″ plate
NovoTech value line: M50 – M60 compact ironworkers, 50 – 60 tons
faq: Single-piston or double-piston ironworker?

A single-piston machine (HKM 40 – 65 V) uses one hydraulic cylinder for all stations, so one operator works one station at a time — the right choice for a fabrication shop that punches a few holes and cuts a few angles per job. A double-piston machine (HKM 55 – 175) has two cylinders and two foot pedals, so one operator can punch while another shears or notches: twice the output from one machine, plus an electrical back gauge as standard.
What size ironworker do I need?

Size it by the thickest material you punch and the largest angle you shear. The punching capacity is quoted as a hole diameter × thickness at the machine's tonnage — a 66 US ton HKM 60 punches Ø1-1/8″ through 9/16″ plate and shears L 4-3/4 × 4-3/4 × 1/2″ angle; the HKM 115 punches Ø1-3/8″ × 1″ and shears L 5-7/8 × 5-7/8 × 5/8″. Tell us your plate thickness, largest angle and flat bar and we will point to the model on its capacity chart.
What tooling comes with the machine?

A Ø7/8″ punch and die (Ø1″ on the HKM 115), the round and square bar blade set, the angle blade set, the flat-bar shear blades and — except on the HKM 40 — the rectangular notching blade set. Punches and dies to Ø1-1/2″ in any diameter, oblong or square are stocked in Mississauga, ON, Canada; large-hole punching sets go to Ø4-7/8″ with the optional tool.
Can an ironworker cut channel, I-beam and tee?

Yes, with the optional section blades on the shear station — UPN and IPN sections up to 11-3/4 × 4-7/8″ and tee to 5-7/8 × 9/16″ on the HKM 175 — and the section punching tools punch the flanges and webs of IPN, UPN, flat bar and angle.
Ironworker or band saw for cutting angle?

An ironworker shears a 4″ angle in one stroke and a few seconds, with no blade to wear and no chips; the cut is square with a slight deformation at the edge. A band saw takes a minute per cut but leaves a clean, mitre-capable cut on any section. Shops that cut hundreds of angles and flats a day keep both: the ironworker for brackets, clips and base plates, the saw for mitres and beams.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Large-format plate lasers — ground-rail and gantry machines to 164 ft
pages.desc: Large-format fiber plate lasers sold in Canada: Dener Smart semi-closed tables to 13 × 82 ft, ground-rail and gantry machines to 10 × 164 ft, 3 to 60 kW.
pages.intro: A large-format plate laser cuts long and heavy plate on a bed too long and too heavy for a cabinet machine: the plate lies on a fixed single table loaded by crane or forklift from the side, the gantry runs over it on a long frame or on rails in the floor, and the cover that keeps the beam and the spatter in travels with the gantry — semi-closed. High-power sources of up to 60 kW cut 1-1/2″ and beyond, with ±45° bevel heads for weld preparation and an oxy-fuel torch for the thickest plate. NovoTech sells two lines in Canada, both on this page: the premium Dener Smart semi-closed lasers made in Turkey, single tables from 8.2 × 20 to 13 × 82 ft with 3 to 40 kW; and the value line — the ULG ground-rail lasers with 42.7 or 85.3 ft beds up to 14.8 ft wide and 12 to 60 kW, and the R / TX gantry plate lasers from 10 × 20 to 10 × 164 ft with 6 to 60 kW and bevel cutting. Each family below has its full specification table, photos and brochure. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, chiller and nesting software, installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. For sheet work on a shuttle table see the fiber laser cutting machines.
points: Premium: Smart semi-closed single tables 8.2 × 20 to 13 × 82 ft, 3 – 40 kW, ±0.01 mm — the cabin travels with the gantry
Value: ULG ground-rail lasers, 42.7 or 85.3 ft beds × up to 14.8 ft, 12 – 60 kW; R / TX gantry plate lasers 10 × 20 to 10 × 164 ft, 6 – 60 kW, ±45° bevel, oxy-fuel
For shipyards, structural steel, heavy equipment and plate service centres — 1-1/2″ and beyond
faq: Semi-closed — what does it mean?

The table stays open and the cover rides on the gantry: the laser-safe cabin or hood moves with the cutting head over the plate, so the beam, the spatter and most of the fumes stay under it while the crane or forklift can reach the table from any side. It is the arrangement for plate too long or too heavy for a shuttle table; the fume extraction runs in zones under the slats along the whole bed.
When does a ground-rail laser make sense?

When the plate is longer than about 40 ft, wider than 10 ft or heavier than a table machine carries. On the ULG the gantry runs on rails set in the floor and the plate lies on a separate support table, so the table takes up to 202,000 lb (91.8 t) — a 2″ plate the full 85 × 14.8 ft weighs about 103,000 lb — without loading the axes. Structural, bridge, tower, mining and heavy-equipment fabricators use it for thick plate that used to go to plasma or oxy-fuel. It needs a prepared foundation for the rails, crane access along the table and extraction sized to the cutting zones; we plan the layout with you. The ULG-A is the faster gantry (262 ft/min, 1.1 G); the ULG-C leaves 11.8″ under the beam with a 60 kW source.
Plate gantries, bevels and oxy-fuel?

The R and TX series are gantry lasers with 10 and 13 ft wide tables from 20 to 164 ft long and 6 to 60 kW sources, replacing plasma and flame cutting of plate to 2″ and beyond. The TX carries a ±45° bevel head so weld preparations are cut in the same pass; the TXP adds an oxy-fuel torch for plate to 4″ on the same table. Shipyards, structural steel, bridges and heavy equipment are the customers.
What laser power do I need?

Power sets the thickness and the speed. As a guide for mild steel: 3 kW cuts 1/2″, 6 kW 3/4″ (and 1/4″ at over 300 in/min), 12 kW 1″, 20 kW 1-1/4″ and 30 – 40 kW 1-1/2″ and beyond; stainless and aluminum run about 20 – 30 % thinner at the same power, with nitrogen or air assist. Most Canadian job shops buying today choose 6 or 12 kW: thick enough for structural work, fast enough to pay for the machine on thin sheet. Tell us your material mix and we run the cutting chart for you.
What about assist gas and fume extraction?

Oxygen gives the fastest cut and an oxide edge on mild steel; nitrogen a clean, paint-ready edge on all metals; compressed air at 16 bar replaces nitrogen on sheet to about 1/4″ and cuts the gas bill to near zero — the intelligent air-cutting package is an option on both lines. The machines have pneumatic extraction compartments under the table and connect to a dust collector, which we can supply.
What does the machine need on site?

A level floor, 600 V 3-phase (with the transformer we supply) or 480 V, a chiller (included), assist gas, a dust collector and a compressed-air supply for air cutting. A 6 kW 3015 draws about 46 kW in total (Dener's figure for the GFL) and needs roughly 33 × 20 ft with its shuttle table. Delivery, installation and operator training are done by NovoTech from Mississauga, ON, Canada, and the Ontario pre-start health and safety review is prepared by us.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Laser cutting machines for sheet and plate, 1.5 to 80 kW
pages.desc: Laser cutting machines sold, installed and supported in Canada: fiber lasers with shuttle table, sheet-and-tube lasers, plate lasers, 3D and coil-fed lines.
pages.intro: A fiber laser cutting machine cuts sheet and plate from a DXF file with a focused beam — mild steel to 1-1/2″ and beyond with the high-power sources, stainless and aluminum to 1″ — at speeds no plasma or punch can match, with a clean edge and no tooling. NovoTech sells five kinds in Canada, each on its own page: fiber lasers with a shuttle table or pallet changer that load the next sheet while the first is cut, the production machine from 4 × 4 ft compact models to 8.5 × 41 ft and 80 kW; sheet-and-tube combination lasers with a rotary chuck beside the table; large-format plate lasers — semi-closed single tables, ground-rail and gantry machines to 10 × 164 ft with bevel heads; 3D laser cells for formed parts; and coil-fed lines that cut straight from the coil. Each kind comes in a premium line made in Turkey or a value line built to our specification, as sections on the same page. Below, the kinds compared and the laser power guide; every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, chiller, nesting software, a 1-year warranty and installation, training and parts from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq: Shuttle table, sheet-and-tube, plate, 3D or coil-fed — which laser should I buy?

By how many sheets a day and what they are. A laser with a shuttle table or pallet changer keeps cutting while you load the next sheet and keeps fumes and the beam inside its cabin — the production machine, and the one most shops buy from 5 × 10 ft up. A large-format plate laser — a semi-closed single table, a ground-rail or a gantry machine — is for heavy plate and very long beds, with the cover travelling on the gantry, bevel heads and oxy-fuel. A sheet-and-tube laser adds a rotary chuck beside the table for a shop that cuts both and has room for one machine. 3D cells cut formed parts; coil-fed lines cut straight from the coil. Each kind has its own page with the premium and value lines side by side.
Premium line or value line?

The premium Dener lasers are built in Turkey on frames rated for up to 1.5 G, with Boji BLT autofocus heads and Raycus sources (Precitec and IPG on request), the longest life at high duty and parts stocked in Canada — for two shifts a day. NovoTech's own value line and the Senfeng value line are built in China with their own or Raycus sources, in a wider range — 4 × 4 ft compact machines, 60 – 80 kW plate gantries, sheet-and-tube combos, coil-fed lines — at a lower price; NovoTech stocks the parts and does the service for all of them. Same cut quality at the same power; the premium machine is faster between parts and lasts longer at high duty.

Power sets the thickness and the speed. Most Canadian job shops buying today choose 6 or 12 kW: thick enough for structural work, fast enough to pay for the machine on thin sheet. Tell us your material mix and we run the cutting chart for you.
Which table size?

The model number is the nominal working area in centimetres: 3015 = 10 × 5 ft (3,000 × 1,500 mm) — a standard 4 × 8 or 5 × 10 sheet; 4020 = 13 × 6.6 ft; 6020 = 20 × 6.6 ft for 6 × 20 plate; 6025 and 8025 = 20 and 26 ft × 8.2 ft; 12526 = 41 × 8.5 ft. The 5 × 10 machine is the Canadian standard; buy the 6020 if you cut 20 ft plate or want to nest several sheets without reloading; the 4 × 4 ft Senfeng compact is for small parts in a small shop.
Single table, shuttle table or pallet changer?

A single-table machine (Senfeng NP and compact, and the large-format Smart semi-closed, ULG and R / TX plate lasers) stops while you unload and load — fine for a few sheets an hour, the lowest price, and the only way to carry very long or heavy plate. A shuttle table or pallet changer (Dener GFL and Smart with shuttle table, NovoTech ULE, Senfeng H series) swaps tables in 15 to 30 seconds, so the laser cuts while the operator loads: the difference between 40 and 70 % spindle time on a busy machine, and the base for a loading tower later.

Can the laser be automated?

The Dener GFL and the Smart with shuttle table, the NovoTech ULE and the Senfeng H series are prepared for the tower; the Senfeng coil-fed lines go further and cut straight from the coil. Ask us for the automation layout.

pages.h1: Laser welders — handheld from 0.8 kW, robotic cells to 20 kW, cladding
pages.desc: Laser welders and laser welding machines sold in Canada: portable and handheld laser welders to 3 kW, robotic welding cells to 20 kW, cobot MIG, cladding.
pages.intro: A fiber laser welder joins stainless, aluminum, galvanized and mild steel sheet with a narrow, deep seam at five times the speed of TIG, with almost no heat distortion and no grinding afterwards; handheld, it takes a day to learn, and on a robot it runs the same weld all shift. NovoTech sells Senfeng laser welding equipment in Canada: the portable air-cooled S series at 0.8 to 1.5 kW on wheels, the HWM handheld welders at 1.5 to 3 kW with wire feed for joints to 9/32″, robotic laser welding cells from 1.5 to 20 kW with positioners and tracks, teaching-free and collaborative MIG robots, and the laser cladding machines that rebuild shafts, rolls and bores with a metallurgically bonded wear layer. Senfeng makes its own sources and heads in Jinan, China; CE / FDA / ETL certified and CSA approved. Installed and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Handheld: S series 0.8 – 1.5 kW air-cooled, 99 – 121 lb · HWM 1.5 – 3 kW, welds to 9/32″, 4-in-1 head
Robotic: RW laser cells 1.5 – 20 kW · RMW teaching-free and CMW cobot MIG welders 350 / 500 A
Cladding: 6 / 12 kW robot cells, lathe-type machines to 20 ft and a portable system for on-site repair
faq: What can a handheld laser welder do that TIG cannot?

Speed and heat. A 1.5 kW laser welds 16 ga stainless at 10 – 15 in/min with a seam that needs no grinding, puts a fraction of the heat into the part — thin sheet, boxes, cabinets and railings stay flat — and welds dissimilar thicknesses, galvanized and aluminum that TIG struggles with. An operator who has never welded produces clean seams after a day of training. It does not replace MIG on heavy plate: the 3 kW HWM welds 9/32″ mild steel in a single pass and the robotic 6 – 20 kW cells go to 9/16″.
S series or HWM — which handheld welder?

The S series is the portable machine: 0.8, 1.2 or 1.5 kW, air-cooled with no chiller, 99 – 121 lb on wheels and a 220 V single-phase plug — for a shop that moves it between jobs or takes it on site. The HWM is the production welder: 1.5, 2 or 3 kW with a water chiller, a 33 ft cable, a wire feeder and the 4-in-1 head that welds, cleans the weld, cuts sheet and seam-welds — for a station that welds all day and for joints to 9/32″.
Is it safe to use in a shop?

A class 4 laser needs a controlled area: the welders ship with a CE face shield, laser-resistant gloves and clothing, and the gun fires only with the safety clamp on the workpiece. We recommend the welding booth with laser-protective glass for a fixed station, and fume extraction as for any welding. Operator training is part of the installation.
When does a robot make sense?

When the same joint is welded hundreds of times a day: tanks, frames, boxes, exhaust, furniture. The RW laser cells run 1.5 to 20 kW on a 6-axis robot with a positioner so the seam is always in position; the CMW cobot is the simplest entry — a 350 or 500 A MIG torch on a collaborative arm, programmed by guiding it by hand over the part, on a cart you wheel to the job; the RMW scans the part with a camera and writes its own program, for batches of one.
What is laser cladding used for?

Repairing and hardening: worn shafts, hydraulic cylinder rods, rolls, valve seats, pump housings and dies get a new wear- or corrosion-resistant surface — stainless, nickel, cobalt or carbide alloys from powder — fused to the base metal with a thin heat-affected zone, far stronger than thermal spray and with less distortion than overlay welding. Layers to 25/64″ (10 mm), machined afterwards. Mining, oil and gas, hydro, pulp and paper and steel mills are the usual customers.
What does the machine need on site?

The S series plugs into a 220 V outlet; the HWM, robots and cladding machines run on 3-phase — we supply the transformer for 600 V. Shielding gas (argon or nitrogen), compressed air for the cutting and cleaning modes, a fume extractor, and for the cladding machines a powder supply. Delivery, installation and training by NovoTech from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.desc: Pittsburgh lock formers for 26 – 16 ga duct, an auxiliary roll former for button lock and drive cleat, a pneumatic lock seamer for round duct, diamond roll.
pages.intro: A lock former (Pittsburgh machine) rolls the edge of a duct panel into the Pittsburgh lock — the pocket the matching flange is hammered into to close a rectangular duct — and, with other roll sets, double seams, drive cleats, button locks and flanges. NovoTech's value-line HVAC machines are built in China to our specification: the PF20G lock former for 26 – 20 ga, the PF16G for 25 – 16 ga with six roll forms as standard, and the AX20G auxiliary roll former whose roll sets change in under five minutes; and the PIC50 diamond roller former, which embosses a 2-3/4″ diamond pattern into 20 ga sheet up to 50″ wide for decorative panels. Parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada. ISITAN's LS-13P pneumatic lock seamer, made in Turkey, closes the longitudinal lock seam of round ducts and pipes from Ø3.9 to 5.1″ in 18 ga, up to 51″ long.
points: PF20G and PF16G Pittsburgh lock formers, 26 – 16 ga; AX20G roll former with button lock, drive cleat and 6-in-1 flange rolls

faq: What is a Pittsburgh lock, and what gauge can a lock former take?

The Pittsburgh lock is the standard longitudinal seam of rectangular duct: the lock former rolls a pocket on one edge of the panel, the other edge is bent to a 90° flange, the flange goes into the pocket and the lip is hammered (or closed with a seam closer) over it. The PF20G forms it in 26 to 20 ga, the PF16G in 25 to 16 ga mild steel; galvanized steel is the usual material.
PF20G, PF16G or AX20G?

The PF20G is the compact lock former for light duct — Pittsburgh, flange attachment and right angle in 26 – 20 ga, with double seam and drive cleat rolls as options. The PF16G takes duct to 16 ga and has six roll forms as standard — Pittsburgh, flange attachment, right angle, double seam, drive cleat and Z — on one machine. The AX20G is an auxiliary roll former for the joints a lock former does not make: button locks, Acme double seams, drive cleats and a 6-in-1 set of flanges and standing seams, with roll sets that change in five minutes.
How much material does a Pittsburgh lock use?
About 1″ of sheet for the pocket; the adjustable auto-guides set the edge so the pocket depth is consistent and material waste stays at a minimum. Allow for it when you lay out the blanks.

pages.h1: Magnetic sheet metal brakes — 2 to 10 ft, 16 gauge, boxes of any depth
pages.desc: Magnetic sheet metal brakes sold in Canada: EB625 to EB3200, 16 ga over 2 – 8 ft and 18 ga over 10 ft, 3.3 – 13.2 US tons of clamping, boxes of any depth.
pages.intro: A magnetic sheet metal brake clamps the sheet with an electromagnet in the bed instead of a mechanical beam: a loose steel clamping bar is held down by 3.3 to 13.2 US tons of magnetic force, and because there is no beam frame at the ends, a short bar folds the side of a box of any depth, closed shapes, narrow channels and short return flanges that a box and pan brake cannot reach. NovoTech sells the EB range in Canada, all on this page: six models from the EB625 at 2 ft to the EB3200 at 10 ft, 16 ga mild steel over 2 to 8 ft and 18 ga over 10 ft, each with a set of clamping bars, a radius bar and a back stop, and the leaf angle read on a scale. The family below has its full specification table and photos. NovoTech's value-line brakes are built in China to our specification, with parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Six models, 2 – 10 ft: 16 ga × 2 – 8 ft and 18 ga × 10 ft mild steel; 3.3 – 13.2 US tons of clamping
No end frames: boxes of any depth, closed and narrow shapes, short return flanges; clamping bars from 1″ and a radius bar included
Single-phase 120 / 240 V, foot switch, 180° leaf, two-stage clamping for positioning
faq: What can a magnetic brake fold that a box and pan brake cannot?

Anything the end frames of a conventional brake would block: the fourth side of a deep box, a closed or narrow channel, a short return flange, a flange inside a panel, a box with a lip. The clamping bars are loose pieces from 1″ long up, placed wherever the fold is, and the magnet holds whatever is under them. The price is capacity — 16 ga mild steel on the short models, 18 ga on the 10 ft — so for 14 ga and heavier the box and pan or hydraulic brakes are the machines.
How strong is the clamping, and does the sheet slip?

The EB brakes clamp with 3.3 to 13.2 US tons across the full length, two-stage: a light hold to position the sheet, full force to fold. The sheet does not slip in rated material; the clamping bar edge gives the bend radius, and a radius bar is supplied for larger radii. The magnet releases the instant the foot switch is let go.
How are the capacities rated, and what about stainless and aluminum?

In gauge of mild steel over the full length: 16 ga on the EB625 to EB2500 and 18 ga on the EB3200. Stainless steel bends at about two gauges lighter, aluminum at about two gauges heavier; shorter folds with a short clamping bar take heavier material than the full-length rating.
What power does a magnetic brake need?

Single-phase 120 or 240 V — a wall outlet: the electromagnet draws power only while the foot switch is pressed. No hydraulics, no three-phase, so the brake can go anywhere in the shop or on a trailer.
What voltage do these machines run on?

pages.h1: Bekamak manual band saws
pages.desc: Gravity-feed manual metal band saws BMS 230DG and 270DG: double-miter heads to 60°, hydraulic descent, Ø9″ to 10-5/8″, plus the BMH 170 power hacksaw.
pages.intro: Gravity-feed pivot saws built by Bekamak in Turkey for maintenance shops, fabricators and anyone cutting a few pieces at a time: the operator positions the bar, closes the vise and lowers the bow; a hydraulic cylinder controls the descent and the double-miter head swivels both ways for angle cuts. Below them, the BMH 170 hydraulic power hacksaw — the simplest and lowest-cost Bekamak saw, for Ø6-3/4″ bar a piece at a time. Premium-line construction with CSA-approved panels and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada. Searching for a manual metal bandsaw, a gravity-feed horizontal band saw for metal or a small band saw machine for the shop? These are the ones NovoTech stocks and supports.
points: Hydraulic-damped gravity feed with adjustable cutting pressure
Double-miter head: +60° right, −45° left
Round capacities Ø9″ (230 mm) and Ø10-5/8″ (270 mm); BMH 170 hacksaw to Ø6-3/4″ (170 mm)
faq: What does “gravity feed” mean on a band saw?

The saw bow descends under its own weight; a hydraulic cylinder with an adjustable valve controls how fast it drops, so the operator sets the cutting pressure for the material. After the cut the operator lifts the bow back up by hand.
Can a manual band saw cut miters?
Yes. The BMS 230DG and 270DG heads swivel to both sides — +60° to the right and −45° to the left — with an angle scale and fast stops at 30°, 45° and 60°, so one setup covers most structural miters.
Band saw or power hacksaw?

A band saw cuts continuously with an endless blade, so it is faster, cuts larger sections and leaves a better surface; the BMH 170 power hacksaw cuts on the forward stroke of a flat 13-3/4″ blade under hydraulic feed. It takes Ø6-3/4″ (170 mm) at 0° and Ø4-3/8″ at 45°, weighs 584 lb, uses inexpensive hacksaw blades and costs less than any band saw — the choice for a maintenance shop or a few cuts a day.
When should I move up to a semi-automatic saw?

When you cut more than a few dozen pieces a day, or when the operator is tied up holding the bow. A semi-automatic saw clamps hydraulically, cuts at a preset feed and lifts the bow by itself, so the operator only loads material. See the Bekamak semi-automatic band saws page.
What voltage do these saws run on?
Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V with a CSA-approved electrical panel; 208 V, 240 V or 480 V 3-phase are available on request.

pages.h1: Mechanical shears — guillotine, bench and coil shears, 20 ga to 1/4″
pages.desc: Mechanical shears sold in Canada: direct-gear SRGM guillotines, 1/8″ and 1/4″ to 13.8 ft with return-to-sender and cut-to-length versions, bench shears.
pages.intro: A mechanical shear drives the cutting beam from an electric motor instead of hydraulic cylinders — through a gearbox and crank (direct gear) or a gearbox — so there is no hydraulic power pack to leak or warm up, the cut is the same on the first and the thousandth stroke, and the machine runs up to 35 strokes a minute: the shear for sheet and light plate all day. NovoTech sells them in Canada in two lines, all on this page: the premium-line SRGM direct-gear guillotines, built in Turkey with European motors, gearboxes and electrics — the light-type SRGM-H for 1/8″ mild steel and the SRGM for 1/4″ from 43″ to 13.8 ft, the SRGM-HFR / FR with a return-to-sender sheet support that brings the cut piece back to the operator, and the SRGM-HCL / CL built into cut-to-length coil lines; and NovoTech's value line — the Q11 electric shears for 14 ga to 5/32″ over 49″ to 100″ with a manual back gauge and counter or, on the Q11 NC, a PLC and motorised back gauge, the EBQ01 motorized bench shears for 18 ga over 26″ and 20 ga over 41″, and the PS-1220×1.5GT that slits 16 ga × 48″ coil into strips and cuts them to length. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel and a 1-year warranty, installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. For plate thicker than 1/4″, and for the light hydraulic shears, see the hydraulic shears.
points: SRGM-H light type, 1/8″ × 3.6 – 10 ft, 35 strokes/min · SRGM standard, 1/4″ × 3.6 – 13.8 ft, 31 strokes/min — premium line, made in Turkey
SRGM-HFR / SRGM-FR with return-to-sender: the cut blank comes back to the front, off-cuts drop to the rear; SRGM-HCL / CL for cut-to-length coil lines
Value-line Q11 electric shears 14 ga – 5/32″ × 49 – 100″ with manual or NC back gauge
EBQ01 motorized bench shears, 18 ga × 26″ and 20 ga × 41″ · PS-1220×1.5GT coil slitting and cut-to-length machine, 16 ga × 48″
faq: Mechanical or hydraulic shear — which is better?

For sheet to 1/4″ a direct-gear mechanical shear is the faster and simpler machine: 31 – 35 strokes a minute from a motor and gearbox, no hydraulic power pack, no oil to heat up, no valves or seals to service, and the same cut quality on the first and the thousandth stroke. Hydraulic shears earn their price from 3/8″ plate upwards, where the beam needs tonnage rather than speed — those are the Dener BS / DAS and the NovoTech value-line QC12K / Q11K on their own pages; the shears overview compares all four lines in one table.
What does direct-gear mean?

The motor drives the cutting beam through a gearbox and crank directly — there is no flywheel and clutch between them, as on an older mechanical shear. The beam makes one stroke per pedal press, stops at top dead centre and cannot repeat a stroke on its own; the motor runs only while the beam cycles, which also makes the machine quiet and economical.
How is the capacity rated, and what about stainless and aluminum?

Capacities are the maker's ratings for mild steel over the full blade length: 1/4″ (6 mm) on the SRGM 1100 and 1360, 3/16″ on the 1560, 5/32″ on the 2060 – 3200 and 1/8″ on the 4200; 1/8″ (3 mm) on the SRGM-H range. Stainless steel is harder to shear, so count on about 60 % of the mild-steel thickness — 14 ga stainless on a 1/8″ machine, 11 ga on a 1/4″ machine; aluminum cuts to the full rated thickness and more. On the value line: 5/32″ on the Q11-4 electric and NC shears, 14 ga on the Q11-2 models, 18 ga and 20 ga on the EBQ01 bench shears and 16 ga on the PS-1220 coil slitter.
Which length do I need — 4 ft, 5 ft, 8 ft, 10 ft?

The model number is the maximum shearing length in millimetres: 1100 = 43″, 1360 = 53.5″ (a 4 × 8 sheet cut across), 1560 = 61″ (5 ft), 2060 = 81″ (6.8 ft), 2560 = 101″ (8.4 ft, a 4 × 8 sheet lengthwise), 3060 = 10 ft, 3200 = 10.5 ft, 4200 = 13.8 ft. Most sheet-metal shops run a 2560 or 3060 so a full sheet is cut both ways; HVAC and signage shops are well served by the 1360 – 2060.
What is the back gauge, and is it NC?

The back gauge is the stop behind the blade that sets the width of the cut strip. The SRGM, SRGM-FR and SRGM-HFR come with an NC-controlled back gauge with 29.5″ stroke — the operator keys in the dimension on the controller and the gauge moves there; a 39.4″ stroke, the ELGO P40T or FUJI Monitouch touch-screen control and a front-operated manual gauge with ball screw are options. The SRGM-H has a manual back gauge as standard and the NC gauge as an option. On the value line, the Q11 electric shears have a manual back gauge with a millimetre counter, wound to the dimension by hand, with an electric gauge as an option; the Q11 NC takes the dimension from a touch-screen PLC and positions the gauge itself, with programs for the parts you cut every week (24.8″ of travel); the EBQ01 bench shears have a 0 – 19.7″ back gauge.
What does return-to-sender do?

On the FR and HFR series a sheet support behind the blade tilts after the cut and carries the cut piece back under the blade to the front of the machine, while off-cuts fall to the rear. One operator cuts blanks and strips without walking round the machine or needing a helper at the back — the biggest time saver on a shear that cuts small parts all day. The standard version is manual; the pneumatic version adds return-to-rear for scrap.
How long do the blades last, and can they be turned?

The blades are high-carbon, high-chrome tool steel: the top blade has two cutting edges and the bottom blade four, so each is turned to a fresh edge before it needs regrinding. The blade gap is set from the front of the machine to the sheet thickness, which keeps the edges sharp and the cut burr-free. Replacement blades are stocked in Mississauga, ON, Canada.
Can it cut at an angle?

Yes — the optional 0 – 180° angular cutting device on the table positions the sheet for mitre and trapezoid cuts against the squaring arm; the standard squaring arm has a T-slot, a stopper and a ruler for square cuts.
What does the A model add — Q11-3x1250A?

A light-curtain rear guard instead of a fence, so nobody reaches into the rear of the shear while it cycles, a pneumatic sheet catcher behind the blade and a front sheet pallet for stacking the cut blanks — the Q11 set up for a production station rather than a cut-now-and-then shear. The light curtain and catcher are options on the other Q11 models; the NC machines have an interlocked rear guard and the pneumatic catcher as standard.
When is a coil slitter worth it?

When you buy sheet in coil, or cut the same strips and blanks every day — roofing and siding trim, flashing, duct, cable tray. The PS-1220×1.5GT pays off coil up to 48″ wide, slits it into up to seven strips in thin sheet (two in 16 ga) and cuts them to length at 35 strokes a minute, so blanks come off the outfeed table without a shear operator squaring each sheet. Coil costs less per pound than cut sheet and has no drop at the end of every sheet.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Milling machines — turret, universal and drilling-milling machines
pages.desc: Milling machines sold in Canada: turret mills with horizontal spindle, universal and ISO50 mills, drill-mills, keyseaters and a head resurfacing machine.
pages.intro: Milling machines cut flat faces, slots, steps, pockets and keyways with rotating cutters while the table moves the work under them. NovoTech's value-line milling machines are built in China to our specification: knee-type turret mills with a horizontal spindle as well as the vertical head, universal mills with a head that swivels through 360°, heavy ISO50 universal mills with power feed and rapid traverse on all axes and tables up to 79″, drilling-milling machines that drill 2″, a mini mill-drill and a radial drill-mill, a keyseater and a slotting machine for keyways and splines, and the KSM-850 resurfacing machine for cylinder heads and blocks. Parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Turret mills X6325W – X6336WA: vertical head to 7,200 rpm, horizontal spindle, power feed, tables to 64 × 14″
Universal mills XQ6226, X6436 and heavy ISO50 LM-1450 / X5750 with tables to 79″ and servo feeds
ZX drilling-milling machines for 2″ drilling; TX-20 and DM-20; B5012 keyseater and B5013 slotter; KSM-850 head resurfacer
faq: Turret mill, universal mill or drill-mill?

A turret (Bridgeport-type) mill has a vertical head that tilts and a knee that moves the table up and down — the most flexible machine for one-off parts, slots and pockets. A universal mill adds a horizontal spindle and arbor for side and slab milling and gang cutters, and swivels its head through 360°. A drill-mill drills and mills on one column without a knee: the lower-cost choice when most of the work is drilling with some face milling.
What do ISO40 and ISO50 mean?

They are the sizes of the spindle taper that holds the tool holder: ISO40 (NT40, the same size as CAT40 and BT40) for general milling, ISO50 for heavier cuts and larger face mills. R8 and MT tapers are found on small mills. Tell us what tooling you already have — adapters are available.
Power feed and DRO?

Power feed moves the table at a steady rate for a better finish and less operator fatigue; a digital readout (DRO) shows the table position to 0.0002″ and replaces the dials for most work. The X6336 and LM-1450 have power feed on all three axes, the X6336 with rapid traverse and a three-axis DRO; DROs are available on most models — ask us when you quote.
What does a cylinder head resurfacing machine do?

It mills the gasket face of a cylinder head or an engine block flat and smooth again after warping or corrosion, so the new head gasket seals. The KSM-850 feeds the part under a Ø13″ cutter head with CBN inserts for cast iron and PCD for aluminum, with variable head speed and table feed for the finish the gasket needs, on heads and blocks up to 33.5″ long.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.desc: Slip rolls and motorized 3-roll plate rolling machines from 3.4 to 10 ft and plate to 3/8″, with cone bending and composite-panel rolls. CSA panels.
pages.intro: Mechanical plate rolling machines for aluminum, HVAC ducting, signage panels, machine guards and sheet-metal enclosures: a planetary gearbox or gear train drives the rolls, the back roll is adjusted by motor or hand wheel and a manual drop-end releases the cylinder. The MRM-S rolls up to 3/8″ plate on working lengths to 10 ft and has a composite-panel version with a Delrin-coated top roll; the IRM and RM are the value-priced motorized plate rollers small workshops ask for. All with CSA-approved panels, parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada. For sheet, NovoTech's value-line ESR electric slip rolls, built in China, roll 22 ga to 1/4″ with cone rolling for the HVAC and sheet-metal shop.
points: MRM-S: 21 models to 10 ft (3050 mm) and 3/8″ (10 mm) plate
IRM and RM: value-priced motorized rolls from 3.4 ft, up to 3/16″
Cone bending, wire grooves and brake motor standard

faq: MRM-S, IRM or RM — what is the difference?

Roll diameter and construction. The MRM-S has 130–220 mm rolls on a welded frame with planetary drive and motorized back roll and takes plate to 3/8″; the IRM has 110–140 mm rolls on cast-iron frames for sheet to 3/16″; the RM has 90–95 mm rolls on a reinforced steel frame for sheet to 11 ga. Choose by the thickest sheet and the smallest diameter you roll.
Can I roll aluminum composite panels (Alucobond) without marking them?

Yes — the MRM-S composite-panel version has a top roll covered in segmented hard-plastic (Delrin) rings so the painted panel is not marked. It is used for curved signage, architectural cladding and outdoor design work.
Do motorized plate rollers bend cones?

Every MRM-S, IRM and RM has a cone-bending device: one end of the top roll is lowered so the sheet travels faster on the wide end. The optional digital readout on the back roll makes repeat cones easier.
Plate roller or slip roll?

A slip roll is a light three-roll machine for sheet — duct, flues, tanks, hoppers, signage — in 22 ga to 1/4″, with a top roll that swings out to slip the finished cylinder off. A plate roller rolls heavier plate and pre-bends the edges so the cylinder closes round. The HER hydraulic slip rolls, with the hydraulic 3-roll plate rollers, bridge the two, to 1/2″ over 6′7″.

pages.h1: NC mandrel benders — pipe, tube and exhaust benders to Ø8-5/8″
pages.desc: NC mandrel benders sold in Canada: ISITAN SFB hydraulic mandrel benders with 10″ touchscreen NC from Ø1-1/4″ to Ø3-1/2″, heavy mandrel benders to Ø8-5/8″.
pages.intro: An NC mandrel bender is a hydraulic bender whose bend angles are stored in a numeric control: the operator feeds and rotates the tube to a stop — or a servo carrier does it — and the machine bends each angle to the programmed value, with a mandrel inside the tube for thin walls and tight radii. NovoTech sells two makers' NC benders in Canada, all on this page, small to large: ISITAN of Bursa, Turkey — the compact SFB 32 benders for Ø1-1/4″ tube, the SFB 38-NC/A benders for aluminum window and door profiles, the SFB NC/C with a servo-rotation carrier and hydraulic collet for series production and the SFB NC in five sizes from Ø1-1/2″ × 11 ga to Ø3-1/2″ × 8 ga with 100 programs of 20 bends; then CSM of Tainan, Taiwan — the two-head F38 / F50 symmetric benders that bend both ends of a tube at once, the TSRJ / TDRJ with servo feed and rotation and the TNCPB with manual feed to Ø4″, and the single-axis TNCB NC hydraulic pipe benders to Ø8-5/8″. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. The pipe bender most exhaust, handrail, furniture and fabrication shops in Canada actually need — mandrel bending with programmed angles, without the price of a full CNC; CSA-approved panels and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: ISITAN SFB 32 compact Ø1-1/4″ · SFB 38-NC/A aluminum-profile benders · SFB NC/C carrier and SFB NC Ø1-1/2″ × 11 ga to Ø3-1/2″ × 8 ga
10″ touchscreen NC · 100 programs × 20 bends · hydraulic mandrel, clamping and pressure die · up to 15.1 ft feed
CSM F38 / F50 symmetric benders · TSRJ / TDRJ and TNCPB NC benders to Ø4″ · TNCB NC pipe benders to Ø8-5/8″
faq: What is the difference between the SFB NC and the SFB NC/C?

On the SFB NC the operator feeds and rotates the tube by hand to the gauge bracket and the NC controls the bend angle. The NC/C adds a carrier with a hydraulic collet and a servo rotation axis: feed to the carrier's adjustable stops, the servo turns the tube to the programmed angle between bends, and the carrier screen shows feed and rotation. For parts with several bends in different planes it is faster and far more repeatable.
NC or CNC?

An NC bender programs the bend angles; the operator handles feed and rotation (servo rotation on the NC/C, servo feed and rotation on the CSM TSRJ / TDRJ). A CNC bender drives all three axes with servos from a drawing. If you bend hundreds of the same multi-plane part a shift, see our CNC tube benders; for mixed work, exhaust, handrails and furniture, an NC bender pays back faster.
What about the mandrel — when do I need it?

Thin-wall tube bent to a tight radius (CLR under about 2× the diameter) wrinkles on the inside and flattens on the outside without support. The mandrel supports the tube from inside; every SFB has a hydraulic mandrel and bends with or without it, and a wiper die and ball mandrel are available for the thinnest walls.
What do you need from me to quote tooling?

Six things: material type, tube or profile size, wall thickness, the smallest centreline radius (CLR) you bend, the maximum bend angle and the maximum tube length. Every bender comes with one die set in the size you request; extra sets, ball mandrels and wiper dies are quoted from the same list.
What voltage do the benders run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on the BK-42 and other models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase.

pages.h1: CNC panel benders — four-side bending, 47 to 165″ bend width
pages.desc: CNC panel benders sold in Canada: the Dener 79″ machine, Senfeng BDC push-down and suction-cup benders 47 – 126″, NovoTech value-line PB-M and PB-A to 165″.
pages.intro: A panel bender is the machine that replaces a press brake for boxes, doors, enclosures, panels and HVAC parts: the blank is clamped by a blank-holder and a bending blade folds the flange up or down, hems it or forms a box corner in 0.2 s, while the manipulator turns the part to bend the next side — all four sides in one setup, no tooling changes, no skilled operator. NovoTech sells the Dener panel bender in Canada: blanks to 78.7 × 49.2″ (2,000 × 1,250 mm), flanges to 6.7″, 14 ga mild steel, 16 ga stainless and 1/8″ aluminum, 15 servo axes with 0.001 mm positioning, 100 % electric at about 2.8 kW average draw. Automatic loading and unloading arms turn it into an unattended cell. Below it is NovoTech's own value line: the PB-M press-arm panel benders in nine sizes from 63 to 165″ and the PB-A with automatic tool change in four sizes to 126″, built in China to our specification with the same 0.2 s bends and 14 ga capacity, and the Senfeng BDC panel benders under their own brand — push-down machines from 59 to 126″ with 13 to 16 servo axes and the suction-cup BDC1200 / 1500 for thin door and appliance panels. All installed and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Blanks to 78.7 × 49.2″, flanges to 6.7″ (11.8″ on request), 1 mm minimum radius, boxes from 5.5 × 7.5″ inside
14 ga mild steel, 16 ga stainless, 1/8″ aluminum — 0.2 s per bend, 295 ft/min feeding

faq: Panel bender or press brake?

A press brake bends one line at a time and the operator handles the part between bends; a panel bender clamps the blank once and forms every side — up, down, hems, box corners — automatically, in 0.2 s per bend and with the same accuracy on the first and the thousandth part. For boxes, doors, cabinets, enclosures, appliance and HVAC panels in sheet to 14 ga it is five to ten times faster than a brake and needs no skilled operator or tooling changes. For plate, long single bends, deep boxes or small batches of unusual parts the press brake stays the better machine — most shops run both.
What sheet can it bend?

Mild steel to 14 ga (2.0 mm), stainless to 16 ga (1.5 mm), aluminum to 1/8″ (3.0 mm); blanks to 78.7 × 49.2″ (2,000 × 1,250 mm) and flange heights to 6.7″ (170 mm), 11.8″ on request; minimum bend radius 1 mm, minimum four-side box 5.5 × 7.5″ inside. Pre-painted and film-covered sheet is bent without marking thanks to the brush table and blade geometry.
How is it programmed?

From the 3D model or a DXF on the 3D control: the software unfolds the part, sets the bending sequence and simulates it, with automatic compensation for springback. A new part is programmed in minutes and runs without test bends; programs can be prepared offline on a PC.
Can it run unattended?

With the optional loading and unloading arms the machine takes blanks from a stack and places finished parts on a pallet, so it runs lights-out behind a laser. The 15-axis servo drive and the 2.8 kW average consumption make it the cheapest machine on the floor to keep running.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
