faq: Pipe bender, tube bender, mandrel bender — what is the difference?

"Pipe" is sized by nominal pipe size (NPS) and schedule, "tube" by outside diameter and wall, but the machines are the same: a bend die, a clamp and a pressure die draw the material around the radius. A mandrel bender adds an internal mandrel so thin-wall tube can be bent to a tight radius without wrinkling; the CNC and NC benders on these pages are mandrel benders, the BK, TB, SPB and value-line benders bend without a mandrel. Every capacity on these pages is given as OD × wall in inches and gauge.
How do I choose a tube bender?

Start with the largest tube (OD × wall and material), the tightest centreline radius and the number of bends per part — that sets mandrel or not and the model size. Then the volume: a hydraulic or rotary draw bender for occasional bends, an NC mandrel bender for programmed angles with manual feed, a carrier or servo-feed NC for repeatable multi-plane parts, and a CNC when parts come from a drawing in hundreds. Send us a part drawing and we will size the machine and tooling.
Which tube benders does NovoTech stock?

We keep the SFB 38-NC and 51-NC and the BK-050 in Mississauga, ON, Canada, and bring CNC models, carrier models and the larger 76 and 90 sizes in to order with their tooling. In-stock machines carry the 7-day money-back guarantee. CSM benders are quoted with the tooling for your part drawings.
CSM or ISITAN?

Both are mandrel benders sold, installed and supported by NovoTech. The ISITAN SFB benders (Turkey) cover Ø1-1/4″ to Ø3-1/2″ with NC and CNC models for the job shop and fabricator. CSM covers a far wider range — from Ø15/32″ brake line to Ø8-5/8″ pipe — with all-electric and hybrid machines, stacked tools, boosters and automation for series production. Send us the part drawing and the tube and we quote the right machine from either range.
Do you install tube benders and train operators?

Yes — our technicians commission the bender anywhere in Canada, set up the first tooling, prove out your part and train operators on the NC or CNC. Remote assistance over the network is built into the CNC models, and we support every machine by video call.

Six things: material type, tube or profile size, wall thickness, the smallest centreline radius (CLR) you bend, the maximum bend angle and the maximum tube length. Every bender comes with one die set in the size you request; extra sets, ball mandrels and wiper dies are quoted from the same list.

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on the BK-42 and other models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase.

pages.h1: Tube notchers and pipe notching machines
pages.desc: Belt-sander tube and pipe notchers for tube 11/16″ to 3-1/2″ OD at any angle to 50°, ten dovetail drums included — handrails, roll cages, tube frames.
pages.intro: A tube notcher (pipe notcher or coping machine) grinds a saddle-shaped notch into the end of a tube so it fits tightly against the tube it joins — the joint of every welded handrail, roll cage, trailer, gate and furniture frame. ISITAN's PN belt-sander notchers cope that saddle in seconds, square or at any angle up to 50°, with ten dovetail drums from Ø3/4″ to 3″ included so the notch matches the mating tube. Both sit beside the cold saw and take the hand grinding out of tube fabrication — with CSA-approved panels and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada. NovoTech's value-line notchers, built in China, add the PRS tube end grinders that notch tube from Ø3/4 to 5-3/4″ with a belt, the motorized PTN-30 hole-saw notcher, the UTN40 end-mill notchers and the PTN-12U.
points: Pipe notchers — tube 11/16″ to 3-1/2″ OD, notching to 50°, 10 dovetail drums standard
PN 17/90 with 4 × 47″ belt; compact PN 20/76 with movable clamp and 4 × 79″ belt
NovoTech value line: PRS belt tube-end grinders to Ø5-3/4″, PTN-30 hole-saw notcher, UTN40 end-mill notchers
faq: What is a tube notcher for?

When one tube meets another in a T or at an angle — handrail posts, roll cages, furniture and bike frames, trailer and gate frames — the end has to be coped to the curve of the tube it joins so the weld closes without gaps. The PN notcher grinds that saddle on a sanding belt against a drum of the mating tube's diameter in seconds, square or at any angle to 50°.
Which notcher — PN 17/90 or PN 20/76?

The PN 17/90 takes the larger range, 11/16″ to 3-1/2″ OD, on a 4 × 47″ belt with easy belt adjustment. The PN 20/76 is the compact notcher for 13/16″ to 3″ OD with a longer 4 × 79″ belt and a movable clamp. Both come with the same ten dovetail drums and 3 HP motor.
Belt notcher or hole-saw notcher?

A hole-saw notcher cuts the cope with a hole saw of the mating tube's diameter — slow, and the saw dulls on stainless. The PN grinds the cope on a sanding belt wrapped around a dovetail drum, so it is faster, works on any material and leaves a clean, square-to-weld edge; the drum is swapped in seconds for the next tube size.
Hole saw, end mill or belt — which notching method?

A hole-saw notcher (PTN-30) is the lowest-cost way to cut a saddle: one inexpensive bi-metal hole saw per tube size, any angle, clean enough for most welding. An end-mill notcher (UTN40) cuts faster and more precisely, without coolant, and one cutter covers several sizes. A belt notcher (PRS) grinds the saddle against a contact roller: no burr, no sharp tooling, works on thin-wall stainless and aluminum and also finishes and deburrs. The premium-line PN machines are motorized notchers for production.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Pipe polishing machines and tube sanders — automatic and orbital
pages.desc: Pipe polishing machines and tube sanders for straight and bent tube, Ø3/16″ to Ø15-3/4″: BT 114-S with automatic feeder, orbital, centreless and large-pipe.
pages.intro: A pipe sander (pipe polisher, tube polishing machine) runs abrasive belts or brushes over round or square tube to grind off rust, scale and weld discolouration, give stainless steel a satin or brushed finish and prepare tube for painting or plating. NovoTech has four kinds: the BT 114-S, NovoTech's premium-line sander with two belts and an automatic feeder for straight and bent tube Ø3/8″ to Ø4-1/2″; the Eurofintec 141 and 144 orbital sanders, whose belts orbit the tube so straight and bent round and oval tube is finished all round without turning, Ø3/8″ to Ø5-7/8″; the Eurofintec 128 S, 128 SL and 128 DL centreless sanders for bar and tube Ø3/16″ to Ø5-7/8″ and the 228 for pipe up to Ø15-3/4″; and the 728 tube brushing machine. Cut tube ends are deburred on the 143, on a page of its own. Eurofintec machines are built in Parma, Italy, by Gecam. Supplied with a CSA-approved panel and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: BT 114-S: automatic feeder, two 37 × 2″ belts, straight and bent tube Ø3/8″ – 4-1/2″
141 · 144 orbital sanders for bent tube Ø3/8″ – 5-7/8″ · 128 centreless Ø3/16″ – 5-7/8″ · 228 to Ø15-3/4″

faq: Which pipe sander do I need?

For handrail, furniture and fabrication work in mixed sizes, straight and bent: the BT 114-S with its automatic feeder (Ø3/8″ – 4-1/2″) or the 141 / 144 orbital sanders (Ø3/8″ – 5-7/8″, round and oval). For long runs of straight bar and tube to an even satin or polished finish: a 128 centreless sander, two heads on the 128 DL for two grits in one pass. For pipe over Ø5-7/8″: the 228, to Ø15-3/4″. Cut tube ends go on the 143 tube end deburring machine.
What finish does a belt pipe sander give?

The finish follows the belt: a coarse grit removes rust, scale and weld colour; 180 – 240 grit gives the brushed, satin finish of architectural stainless handrail; finer belts and non-woven belts prepare for mirror polishing. Two belts run at once on the BT 114-S, so a cutting belt and a finishing belt can be fitted together.
Does it polish bent tube?

The BT 114-S and the 141 and 144 orbital sanders do: the BT 114-S head and feeder follow bends up to 45°, and on the orbital sanders the belts orbit the tube as it is pushed through the head, so elbows and frames are finished after bending. Centreless machines finish straight bar and tube only.
Round and square tube on the same machine?

The BT 114-S takes round pipe from Ø3/8″ to Ø4-1/2″ and square tube, passed through flat side by side, two faces at a time. The orbital and centreless sanders are for round tube (the orbital sanders oval too); the 143 tube end deburring machine deburrs the ends of round and square tube.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Plate bevelers — cold beveling machines for plate and pipe to 4-3/4″
pages.desc: Plate bevelers sold in Canada: self-feeding cold beveling machines from Spain, Cevisa CHP shearing bevellers for V, X, K and Y bevels, milling bevellers.
pages.intro: A plate bevelling machine prepares plate and pipe edges for welding: it sits on the edge, feeds itself along it and cuts the bevel cold — V, X, K or Y, at the angle and depth the weld procedure calls for — so there is no flame cut to clean, no heat-affected zone, no slag and no hours of grinding. NovoTech sells the bevellers of CEVISA, built in Vitoria, Spain, since 1969 and used by boiler and tank makers, structural fabricators, shipyards, wind-tower and offshore builders in more than 60 countries. On this page, small to large: the CHP 7, CHP 12 and CHP 12 INV standard shearing bevellers for plate, tube and discs from 1/8″ to 1-9/16″ thick; the CHP 12G, CHP 21G and CHP 21G INV with the bevel angle adjustable from 20° to 45°; the CHP 12G REV and CHP 21G REV that turn over to bevel the lower edge without turning the plate; and the CHP 30G, CHP 60G, CHP 60G INV and CHP 100G milling bevellers, which machine bevels up to 3-15/16″ wide at 15° to 70° in any material — Hardox, Armox, duplex and stainless included — on plate up to 4-3/4″. Supplied with a CSA-approved panel, installed and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. For chamfers on smaller parts, the NovoTech value-line CMD-80 and CMD-4 bench machines cut 15 – 45° chamfers up to 1/4″ and 5/32″, and the DM5 and DM5A hand units 3/16″ at 45°.
points: Shearing bevellers CHP 7 – CHP 21G: plate and tube 1/8″ – 1-15/16″, bevels to 1-1/8″ at up to 8.5 ft/min
Adjustable angle (20° – 45°), inverted (INV) and reversible (REV) models for X and K bevels without turning the plate
Milling bevellers CHP 30G – CHP 100G: machined bevels to 3-15/16″, 15° – 70°, any material, plate to 4-3/4″
faq: What does a plate bevelling machine do?

It cuts the bevel a full-penetration weld needs on the edge of a plate or pipe — V, X, K or Y, at a set angle and depth — and feeds itself along the edge while it cuts. Compared with a cutting torch and a grinder it leaves a clean, even bevel with no heat-affected zone, no slag and no scale to grind off, ready to weld, and it does it at several feet a minute with one operator who does not have to hold or guide it.
Shearing or milling beveller?

A shearing beveller (CHP 7 to CHP 21G) takes the bevel off with a resharpenable shear cutter: the fastest and lowest-cost bevel per foot in mild steel, stainless and aluminum, on plate and tube up to 1-15/16″ and bevels up to 1-1/8″. A milling beveller (CHP 30G, 60G, 100G) machines the bevel with a milling head: a machined finish in any material — Hardox, Armox, duplex, super duplex — at the same capacity, angles from 15° to 70°, transition and J bevels, and bevels up to 3-15/16″ wide on plate to 4-3/4″.
Which size do I need?

Start from the widest bevel face and the thickest plate you prepare. CHP 7: bevels to 3/8″ on 1/8″ – 5/8″ plate and thin tube, also aluminum. CHP 12 / 12G: 11/16″ bevels on 1/4″ to 1-9/16″ (12G 1-3/16″). CHP 21G: 1-1/8″ bevels on 3/8″ – 1-15/16″ plate, for continuous production. CHP 30G: 1-3/8″ machined bevels to 1-15/16″ plate; CHP 60G: 2-3/8″ on plate to 2-3/4″ (3-15/16″ special); CHP 100G: 3-15/16″ on plate to 4-3/4″. In stainless steel the shearing machines take 80 – 90 % of their mild-steel bevel in several runs and about two-thirds in one run; the milling machines keep their full capacity.
What do INV and REV mean?

An INV (inverted) machine works upside down and bevels the lower edge of the plate, so the lower half of an X or K bevel is cut without turning a heavy plate over; running an INV under its standard twin (CHP 12 + 12 INV, 21G + 21G INV, 60G + 60G INV) cuts both bevels in one pass. A REV (reversible) machine turns over on its frame in under a minute and does both bevels by itself — one machine, one operator.
Can it bevel pipe and discs?

Yes, the shearing models bevel tube and pipe as well as plate: from Ø3-15/16″ inside (Ø5-7/8″ on the CHP 21G family), on the inside or the outside, with the pipe horizontal or vertical, and discs and tank heads from Ø13-3/4″. The milling bevellers are for plate, flat bar and square bar.
What does it cost to run?

Little: the shearing cutters last about 3,300 ft (1,000 m) of bevel and are resharpened, Cevisa rates the machines maintenance-free, and a 20 ft plate edge is bevelled in under three minutes on a CHP 12. The milling heads use standard indexable inserts. We quote cutters, inserts and angle devices with the machine.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.intro: A plate roller (plate rolling machine) bends flat plate or sheet into cylinders and cones by passing it between three or four rolls. Every ISITAN and NovoTech premium-line plate roller NovoTech sells in Canada: hydraulic 4-roll plate rolling machines with NC control for production, hydraulic and motorized 3-roll plate rollers for the fabrication shop, and motorized slip rolls for HVAC and sheet-metal work — from a 3.4 ft slip roll to 20 ft heavy-duty machines that roll 3-3/8″ plate. Built in Turkey by ISITAN (since 1959) and for the NovoTech premium line, supplied with CSA-approved panels and supported from NovoTech's warehouse in Mississauga, ON, Canada. Looking for a plate roller machine, sheet metal roller, slip roller or plate bending rolls? These are the ones we stock and service. points: Hydraulic 4-roll plate rollers — 2.1 to 20 ft, up to 3-3/8″ plate, NC / CNC and automation
Hydraulic and motorized 3-roll plate rollers — initial pinch, cone bending

faq: Plate roller, plate roll, slip roll, bending rolls — are these the same machine?

Largely yes. "Plate roller", "plate rolling machine" and "plate bending rolls" all describe the three- or four-roll machine that rolls flat plate into cylinders and cones; "slip roll" or "sheet metal roller" is the light-gauge version for sheet up to about 14 ga, whose top roll slips open to remove the part. We use the manufacturer's terms on each page so you can match them to the capacity tables.
How do I choose the size of a plate roller?

Three numbers: the longest cylinder you roll (working length), the thickest plate you roll at that length, and the smallest diameter you need. Plate rolls are rated at 1.5× and 5× the top roll diameter — a machine that rolls 1/4″ plate into a 20″ cylinder will not roll 1/4″ into a 10″ cylinder. Send us those three numbers and we will point to the models on the capacity tables.
Which plate rollers does NovoTech keep in stock?

We stock the popular MRM-S motorized rolls in Mississauga, ON, Canada, and bring 4R HMS and MRM-H hydraulic machines in to order with their options. In-stock machines carry the 7-day money-back guarantee.
Do you install plate rollers and train operators?
Yes — our technicians commission the machine anywhere in Canada, level it, check the roll parallelism and train your operators on pre-bending, cones and the NC control where fitted.
What voltage do ISITAN plate rollers run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase.

pages.h1: Press brake tool holders, adapters, clamps and accessories
pages.desc: Intermediates, adapters between clamping styles, safety clamps and EUROGRIP, lower die holders, adjustable dies V24 – V400, urethane tooling and gauges.
pages.intro: Everything around the punches and dies: European-style intermediates (Z1 and Z2, adjustable or fixed, heavy-duty CrMo) and upper adapters that let one press brake run another style's tools; safety clamps and EUROSTAMP's own EUROGRIP clamping, manual and pneumatic; lower adapters, solid die holders to 4,100 mm and tangs made to your machine; adjustable dies from V24 to V400 mm for plate; urethane and nylon tooling, film and cloth for parts that must not be marked; and gauges, squares, safety buttons and tooling cabinets. Made in Italy by EUROSTAMP, quoted and shipped by NovoTech.
points: Intermediates Z1 / Z2 and upper adapters between 12 clamping systems; heavy-duty versions to 54 US t/ft
EUROGRIP manual and pneumatic clamping; safety clamps; lower adapters and die holders to 13.5 ft
Adjustable dies V .94 – 15.75″ to 202 US t/ft; urethane tooling, film, gauges and cabinets
faq: What is an intermediate and why adjustable?

The intermediate is the block between the ram and a European-style punch that holds the clamp. The adjustable versions have a wedge that lets you set each section a few hundredths of a millimetre lower — manual crowning — so the angle stays the same along a long bend on a brake without automatic crowning. Z1 (27 mm body, axis 7 mm) and Z2 (40 mm body, axis 20 mm) differ in size: match the ones on your machine.
Can one press brake use tooling of another style?

Yes, through adapters: upper adapters take European-style punches on Trumpf / Wila, Beyeler, LVD, Weinbrenner, CBC, EHT, Durmazlar, Darley, Baykal and Colgar rams, and 4362 takes Trumpf / Wila punches on a European ram; lower adapters do the same for dies. An adapter adds height and costs some load capacity — check both before you buy.
When is an adjustable die worth it?

When you bend plate in many thicknesses: one 3191 covers V65 to V180 mm — the job of eight or ten solid dies — and the rollers on the shoulders reduce marking and force. For thin sheet and repeat work, solid 1V dies remain cheaper and more precise.

pages.h1: Press brake tooling — punches, dies and adapters for every clamping
pages.desc: EUROSTAMP press brake tooling in Canada: punches, dies, holders and adapters made in Italy for Amada-Promecam, Trumpf, Wila, Bystronic, LVD and American.
pages.intro: NovoTech sells and supports EUROSTAMP press brake tooling in Canada: punches, dies, holders, adapters and clamping made in Italy by a company that has built nothing but press brake tooling since 1970. Six pages cover the range — European-style (Amada-Promecam) punches and dies for most press brakes in Canadian shops, Trumpf and Wila-style tooling, Bystronic and LVD-style tooling, American-style tooling with the .500″ tang, and the holders, adapters and accessories that let one press brake run another style's tools. Every table gives the angle, height, tip radius or V opening and load rating of each tool in inches and millimetres, with DXF profiles to load into your CNC. Below the range: how to choose a V opening and the tonnage chart for air bending.
points: Over 700 punches, dies, holders and accessories, in full lengths and sectioned sets — European, Trumpf, Wila, Bystronic, LVD and American styles
C45 and 42CrMo4 steel, induction-hardened 55 – 60 HRC up to 3 mm (.118″) deep; special tools to your drawing
DXF profiles to download; adapters between clamping styles; quoted and shipped from Mississauga, ON, Canada
faq: Which tooling fits my press brake?

It depends on the clamping, not the brand of the machine. Most press brakes in Canadian shops — Amada, Accurpress, Baykal, Dener, Durmazlar, Ermaksan, Yawei and many more — clamp European-style (Amada-Promecam) tools. Trumpf, Darley and Safan use Trumpf or Wila (New Standard) clamping; Bystronic and Beyeler use type R, RF or RF-A; LVD has its own; and many older North American brakes take American-style tools with a .500″ tang. Send us the model of your brake or a photo of the clamp and a tool, and we confirm before you order.
How do I choose the V opening?

Start with V = 8 × the sheet thickness for mild steel up to about 1/2″ — V24 (about 1″) for 1/8″, V50 (2″) for 1/4″ — and 10 to 12 × for heavier plate. Aluminum works with 6 ×, stainless with 8 – 10 ×. The inside radius comes out at about 1/6 of the V and the shortest flange you can bend at about 0.7 × V. The guide and the tonnage chart below work through it.
How much tonnage does a bend need?

For 90° air bending of mild steel, tons per foot ≈ 575 × t² ÷ V, with the thickness t and the V opening in inches: 1/4″ in a 2″ V needs about 18 US tons per foot of bend, so a 10 ft bend needs about 180 tons (163 t). Stainless needs about 1.5 times as much, soft aluminum about half. The tooling must be rated above the tonnage per foot, and the press brake above the total.
What do the load ratings in the tables mean?

The maximum force the tool takes per unit of length — EUROSTAMP gives it in tonnes per metre, we add US tons per foot. If a bend needs 15 tons per foot, use a punch and a die rated above 15 US t/ft (45 t/m). Concentrated loads on a short piece of tool are the usual way tools crack: a 1 ft part bent with 30 tons puts 30 tons per foot on the tool.
Do you make special tools?

Yes. EUROSTAMP's technical department designs special punches and dies — profiles, radii, offsets, combined tools — for parts standard tooling cannot bend. Send us the part drawing and the press brake model, and we come back with a proposal and a price.
What steel is the tooling made of?

C45 medium-carbon steel, raw or tempered, and Italian 42CrMo4 chrome-molybdenum steel for the heavier and slimmer tools. The working surfaces are induction-hardened to 55 – 60 HRC up to 3 mm (.118″) deep, so the tip and shoulders resist wear while the body stays tough. The ESH insert dies are nitrided all over to 65 HRC.
Can we get the tools as DXF files for our CNC?

Yes — every tool in these tables that has a DXF link can be downloaded straight from the page: the profile drawn in millimetres, ready to import into the tool library of a Delem, ESA or Cybelec control or into offline bending software. For the few tools without one, ask us and we get the drawing from EUROSTAMP.

pages.h1: Press brakes — hydraulic, electric and compact, 16 to 1,323 US tons (15 to 1,200 t)
pages.desc: Press brakes sold, installed and supported in Canada: hydraulic CNC, hybrid and NC press brakes to 1,323 US tons, servo-electric to 220, compact from 16.
pages.intro: A press brake bends sheet and plate between a punch and a V-die; the control sets the back gauge, the ram depth and the angle, and the operator loads the sheet and presses the pedal. NovoTech sells three kinds in Canada, each on its own page: hydraulic press brakes — the lowest price per ton and full force over the whole stroke, from 33-ton (30 t) NC machines to CNC brakes of 1,323 US tons (1,200 t) and 26 ft, in a premium line made in Turkey and a value line built to our specification; electric press brakes, servo-driven with no hydraulic oil, 3 to 220 US tons (3 to 200 t), which bend sheet about twice as fast as a hydraulic brake and draw about 70 % less power; and compact press brakes from 16 to 66 tons (15 to 60 t) over 2 to 8 ft for the sheet-metal shop. Below, the three kinds compared, every family by brand and the questions we get asked; every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, a 1-year warranty and installation, training and parts from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Hydraulic — CNC 55 – 1,323 US tons (50 – 1,200 t) × 4 – 26 ft, mild hybrid XL and WAD, NC torsion-bar from 33 tons (30 t)
Electric — servo-electric 44 – 220 tons (40 – 200 t) × 5 – 13 ft and ball-screw 3 – 176 tons (3 – 160 t): ±0.01 mm, no oil, power only while the ram moves
Compact — Dener XL 1560, 66 tons (60 t) × 5 ft, value-line WAD-50T CNC and WC67K-30T NC compacts, HBV bending brakes 16 – 35 tons (15 – 32 t)
faq: Hydraulic, hybrid or electric — which press brake should I buy?

Hydraulic gives the lowest price per ton and full force over the whole stroke — the machine for thick plate, long parts and the widest tonnage range (33 to 1,323 US tons (1,200 t) here). A hybrid is a hydraulic brake with servo-driven pumps — the mild hybrid option on the Dener XL (42 – 58 % less energy, faster, quieter) — for a shop that runs the brake all day. An electric brake (Dener DDM, NovoTech WADG) has no oil at all. It repeats to ±0.0004″ (±0.01 mm), bends at up to 1.2″/s (30 mm/s), about twice as fast as a hydraulic brake, and draws about 70 % less power, so it is usually the better buy for 16 ga to 1/4″ sheet in a job shop or a clean environment. Above about 150 tons (136 t) and on 3/8″ plate, hydraulic still wins. For 4 – 5 ft work in sheet to 3/16″, the compact brakes on their own page are the right size.
Premium line or value line?

Both kinds come in two lines, on the same page. The premium line is made in Turkey by Dener on the heaviest frame, with ESA or Delem controls, the longest options list and parts stocked in Canada — the machine for plate and production, two shifts a day. NovoTech's own value line is the same architecture — monoblock frame, servo valves, linear scales, Delem control — built in China to our specification at about two-thirds of the price: the right buy for a job shop that needs a 100 – 300 ton (91 – 272 t) CNC brake, an electric brake for sheet or an NC brake for repeat parts. The compact page has the smallest of both lines — the Dener XL 1560 and the value-line WAD-50T and WC67K-30T — for HVAC, enclosures and brackets where a 100-ton (91 t) machine is more than you need. All are installed and supported by the same NovoTech technicians.
How much tonnage and length do I need?

Air bending takes F = S² × 2 × R ÷ (1.4 × V) tonnes per metre of bend — the sheet thickness S and the V opening V in millimetres, the tensile strength R = 47 kg/mm² for mild steel (70 for stainless, 25 for aluminum), the formula behind the EUROSTAMP and Dener bending charts; in inches and US tons per foot it reads 575 × t² ÷ V. With the standard V of about 8 × the thickness, 3 mm needs about 24 t/m (8 US tons per foot), 6 mm 48 t/m (16), 1/4″ 54 t/m (18), 3/8″ in a 3″ V 80 t/m (27) and 1/2″ in a 5″ V 85 t/m (29). Multiply by the bend length and add about 20 % in reserve: 3 m × 6 mm is a 175-ton (159 t) press brake, 10 ft × 1/4″ a 200 – 220 US ton (181 – 200 t) machine, 10 ft × 3/8″ a 300 – 320 ton (272 – 290 t) machine and 13 ft × 1/2″ a 400 – 450 ton (363 – 408 t) machine. The tonnage calculator in the buying guide on the press brake page does the arithmetic for your thickness and length; tell us your thickest and longest bend and we size the brake and the tooling.
CNC or NC?

An NC brake positions the back gauge and the ram depth from a stored program, with the two cylinders kept in step by a torsion bar — rigid, cheap to maintain, right for the same parts in one material every day. A CNC brake measures the ram on linear scales and corrects it through servo valves, calculates the bend from the drawing, crowns the bed and changes material in the program — the machine for mixed work, tight angles and multi-bend parts. NovoTech's value line has both; the Dener CNC brakes come with 2D or 3D graphic controls. The buying guide below explains and compares every control.
What tooling fits, and do you stock it?

European-style (Promecam / Amada) segmented tooling fits every line: the premium Dener brakes carry European-style top-tool holders, the value-line brakes their own clamping, and a sectioned punch set with a 2-V or 4-V die ships with every machine (a 4-V die with the Dener brakes, a 2-V die with the value line) — tell us which tooling standard your shop already has and we fit the holders to match. NovoTech stocks Eurostamp press brake tooling in Canada — punches, dies, radius, hemming and joggle tools, gooseneck and special profiles — and sizes it to your machine; quick-release, pneumatic and Wila hydraulic clamping and American-style adapters are options, not standard equipment.
What about safety and the Ontario pre-start review?

Side guards, an enclosed rear guard, interlocked doors and an anti-panic foot pedal with emergency stop are standard; DSP laser finger protection is standard on the WAD CNC press brakes and the Dener XL, and on the other machines DSP or Fiessler laser protection and light curtains are options we recommend for every CNC press brake. In Ontario a new press brake needs a pre-start health and safety review (PSR) under Regulation 851 before it runs.
Do you deliver, install and service in Canada?

Yes — NovoTech sells, installs and supports press brakes across Canada and the United States. Installation, commissioning and operator training are free of charge in the Greater Toronto Area; outside the GTA our technicians do the same work at an additional charge. Parts are stocked in Canada. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, 600 V standard (208 / 240 / 480 V on request), a 1-year warranty and remote diagnostics through the control.
What does delivery cost, and who unloads the machine?

A press brake ordered from the factory (back-ordered) travels in its container straight from the port, customs and the rail yard to your plant door: in the Greater Toronto Area that delivery is free; outside the GTA the freight is quoted and charged. A machine from NovoTech's stock is loaded, shipped and unloaded at the buyer's cost. In every case unloading is the buyer's responsibility and expense — the crane or forklift, the rigging and moving the machine onto its foundation — so book a rigger for the delivery day; we are glad to recommend riggers who know press brakes and to tell you the weight and lifting points.
Is the hydraulic oil included?

No — the hydraulic oil is bought by the customer. Before commissioning, fill the tank with ISO VG 46 anti-wear hydraulic oil (AW 46) in the quantity shown in the specification table for your model; our technician checks the level and bleeds the system during installation. Electric press brakes have no hydraulic oil at all.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Profile machining centres, copy routers and end mills for windows
pages.desc: A 9-axis profile machining centre to 21′ 4″, 3-axis CNC drilling and milling machines, copy and drainage routers and end mills for window profiles.
pages.intro: Before a window frame is assembled, its profiles are machined for the hardware — lock and handle places, hinge and espagnolette slots, drainage slots — and its mullions are end-milled to fit the frame. NovoTech supplies these machines from Plastmak, built in Bursa, Turkey, from template-guided to fully automatic: copy routers that follow a template (the SC 501, 502S and 512 with triple drilling units, the SC 521S for drainage slots and the SC 542 for aluminum); the SC 211 and SC 211S end milling machines; the SC 5000 and SC 5000S 3-axis CNC drilling and milling machines with three spindles; and the SC 4550, a 9-axis machining and cutting centre that takes profiles up to 21′ 4″ (6,500 mm) from a magazine and delivers them machined, cut and labelled. Supplied with a CSA-approved panel, installed and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: SC 4550: 9 axes, 10 spindles, profiles 78-3/4″ – 255-7/8″, cut at 30° – 150°
SC 5000 · 5000S: 3-axis CNC, 3 spindles at 18,000 rpm, travel 15-3/8 × 7-7/8 × 7-7/8″
Copy routers SC 501 · 502S · 512 · 521S · 542 · end mills SC 211 · 211S, cutters to Ø6-5/16″
faq: Copy router or CNC?

A copy router repeats a cut-out from a template: quick to set up, inexpensive, ideal for a few profile systems. A CNC is programmed instead — new hardware or a new profile system is a new program, not a new template — and the SC 5000 and 5000S make every cut-out of a profile in one clamping, the SC 5000S from DXF drawings. The SC 4550 adds a magazine, cutting and labelling for unattended work.
What does an end milling machine do?

It cuts the end of a mullion (transom) to the shape of the frame profile it meets, so the T-joint closes tight and can be screwed. A stack of cutters matching the profile does it in one pass; the SC 211S changes the whole stack with one button when the profile series changes and mills at angles from −45° to +45°.
Which machines work on aluminum?

The SC 502S, 512, 542, 5000S, 4550 and 211S work on aluminum as well as PVC, with 18,000 rpm spindles and cooling where aluminum needs it; the SC 501, 521S and 5000 are for PVC, and the SC 211 mills both.
What does the SC 4550 do?

It takes up to seven profiles from its magazine, measures each, clamps it on a 3-axis holding station, grooves, drills, marks and mills it with ten spindles and cuts it with a servo saw at any angle from 30° to 150° — profiles 78-3/4″ to 255-7/8″ long. Finished parts leave on a conveyor with a printed barcode label, and the offcuts go to a cart.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.intro: Window and door shops turn PVC (vinyl) and aluminum profiles into frames in a set order: cut, machine the hardware places, weld or crimp the corners, clean the welds, mill the mullion ends, cut the glazing beads and assemble. NovoTech supplies the machines for every step from Plastmak, built in Bursa, Turkey: single-, double- and 4-corner PVC welders and CNC corner cleaners; a 9-axis profile machining centre, 3-axis CNC drilling and milling machines, copy routers and end milling machines; a hydraulic corner crimper, screwing and sash assembly machines, portable machines and conveyors; and complete production groups for 40 to 220 windows a shift. The saws have their own page — upcut, double-head, bead and miter saws. Every machine is supplied with a CSA-approved panel, installed and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. Below, each page in brief.
points: PVC welding & corner cleaning — 1, 2 and 4-corner welders, knife and CNC corner cleaners

faq: What machines does a PVC window shop need?

At the least a saw, a copy router for the hardware and drainage holes, a welder, a corner cleaner, an end milling machine for the mullions and a glazing bead saw — the six machines of the PVC single-head group, about 40 – 60 windows a shift. Double-head saws and welders double that; a 4-corner welder, CNC corner cleaner and 3-axis CNC take a shop past 200 windows a shift.
What is different for aluminum windows?

Aluminum frames are not welded but joined with corner cleats and crimped — on the SC 902 — and the profiles are cut on saws with cooling and hydro-check feeds, machined on copy routers or CNCs with cooled 18,000 rpm spindles and end-milled on the heavier SC 211S. The aluminum double-head group puts those machines together.
PVC, uPVC or vinyl?
The same material: rigid PVC, called uPVC in Europe and vinyl in North America. Every machine on these pages that is marked PVC works on vinyl window and door profiles.
Can you plan a complete shop?

Yes. Tell us the windows and doors you make, the profile systems and the output you need; we propose the machines, a layout and the air and power supply — as in Plastmak's workshop plan — then install and commission the line and train your operators.
Do you install the machines and train operators?

Yes. Our technicians install and commission every machine anywhere in Canada, set it up for your profiles and train the operators; spare parts and tooling are supplied from Mississauga, ON, Canada, and we support every machine by video call.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. pages.h1: PVC window welding machines and corner cleaners — 1 to 4 corners
pages.desc: Vinyl window welding machines from a single-head 25° – 180° welder to 4-corner welders and a welding and cleaning line, with knife and CNC corner cleaners.
pages.intro: A PVC (vinyl) window frame is joined by welding: the mitred profile ends are pressed against a heated plate until they melt, then pushed together and held while the seam cools; the bead of melted plastic left on the corner is cleaned off afterwards. NovoTech supplies the welders and corner cleaners of Plastmak, built in Bursa, Turkey: the SC 101 single-head welder for any angle from 25° to 180°; the SC 100 double-head welder for profiles 13-3/8″ to 126″ long; the SC 100 Gold Plus, which welds all four corners of a frame up to 145-11/16 × 106-5/16″ at once, and the Gold Plus Full line that adds a robot and a CNC cleaner; the SC 601 corner cleaner with three knives; and the SC 6000 and SC 6000S CNC corner cleaners. All three welders can make a 0.2 mm (.008″) seam. Supplied with a CSA-approved panel, installed and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: SC 101 single-head, 25° – 180° · SC 100 double-head, profiles 13-3/8″ – 126″ long and to 6-5/16″ high
SC 100 Gold Plus: four corners at once, frames to 145-11/16 × 106-5/16″ · Gold Plus Full welding and cleaning line
SC 601 three-knife corner cleaner · SC 6000 and 6000S CNC cleaners, up to 500 frames a shift
faq: How does a PVC welder work?

The two mitred profiles are clamped and pressed against a Teflon-covered heating plate until their ends melt; the plate is withdrawn and the ends are pressed together and held while the joint cools — welding, cooling and temperature set for each profile type. A 0.2 mm seam limits the weld bead to 0.2 mm (.008″), so laminated and coloured profiles need little or no cleaning.
Which welder for my output?

The single-head SC 101 welds one corner at a time — four cycles a frame, any angle, the right start for small shops and arched windows. The double-head SC 100 welds two corners at once, and the SC 100 Gold Plus all four, so a frame is welded in one cycle and comes out square. The Gold Plus Full carries the frame on to a CNC cleaner by robot, with no operator in between.
Why clean the corners?

Welding leaves a bead of melted PVC on the faces and in the gasket grooves of every corner; left on, it stops gaskets and hardware from seating and looks poor. The SC 601 cleans the corner and faces with knives in one PLC cycle; the CNC cleaners also clean seal grooves, radii and laminated profiles — the SC 6000S with 10 tools and automatic profile recognition.
What frame sizes fit the 4-corner welder?

Frames from 16-1/8 × 19-1/2″ (410 × 495 mm) up to 145-11/16 × 106-5/16″ (3,700 × 2,700 mm), with profiles 1-9/16″ to 7-7/8″ high and up to 5-7/8″ wide. With the gasket press option the range is 20-1/2 × 20-1/2″ to 143-11/16 × 104-5/16″.

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Rebar benders and rebar cutters
pages.desc: Rebar benders and rebar cutters sold, installed and supported in Canada: benders to Ø2-3/8″, portable 110 V benders, hydraulic cutters, stirrup benders.
pages.intro: Stationary and portable rebar benders, hydraulic and mechanical rebar cutters, stirrup and spiral benders, and fully automatic shear lines — built by GöçMakSan (GMS) in Turkey since 1960, supplied with CSA-approved panels and supported from NovoTech's warehouse in Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Bend up to Ø2-3/8″ (60 mm) · cut up to Ø2-3/8″ (60 mm)
Portable 110/220 V single-phase units for the job site
Spare parts, tooling and service in Canada
faq: Which rebar bender do I need for 15M, 20M and 25M bars?

A B 36 or BS 36 bends single bars up to 35M (#11) and two 20M bars at once in normal steel, and is the usual choice for a rebar shop running 10M to 25M. For site work on 10M–20M a portable BT 26 or MG 26 Junior on 110/220 V is enough. For 30M–45M bars choose a B 45x1, B 50 or the BS 50/BS 60.
Can I run a rebar bender on single-phase power?

Yes — the portable MG 20B, MG 26 Junior, BT 24x5 and BT 26 benders and the POWER 24 cutter have a built-in transformer and run on 110 V or 220 V single-phase. The stationary B, BS, SL, SX, H, M and SH machines are three-phase and are supplied for 600 V; 208 V, 240 V or 480 V are available on request.
Do the machines come with a CSA-approved electrical panel?
Yes. Every machine NovoTech supplies has a CSA-approved electrical panel wired for Canadian voltage, with overload protection on the benders.
Can a standard rebar bender make stirrups?

Yes. The B series and the portable BT benders make stirrups with the standard pins and rollers; an optional spiral stirrup attachment is available for B and BS series only. For continuous stirrup production from coil use the automatic SLS 12 on the automatic lines page.
What does the 45 / 65 / 85 kg/mm² capacity mean?

The three columns are the manufacturer's ratings for rebar of different tensile strengths: 45 kg/mm² (≈ 64,000 psi), 65 kg/mm² (≈ 92,500 psi) and 85 kg/mm² (≈ 120,900 psi). Canadian Grade 400W rebar has a minimum tensile strength of 540 MPa (≈ 55 kg/mm²), so the 65 kg/mm² column is a safe guide for everyday Canadian bar.
Are spare parts, blades and tooling available in Canada?
Yes. NovoTech stocks cutting blades, bending pins, rollers and electrical parts for GMS machines in Mississauga, ON, Canada, and provides technical support, installation and training.

pages.desc: Rebar benders and rebar bending machines in Canada: B and BS benders to Ø2-3/8″ (60 mm), portable 110 V benders, stirrup, spiral and dowel benders.
pages.intro: Every GMS rebar bender NovoTech supplies in Canada: stationary B and BS series benders for the rebar shop, portable MG and BT benders for the job site, SL stirrup benders, SX and AXIS spiral benders, hydraulic dowel bar benders and the MAX 40 combined bender-cutter. All with programmable angles, left-and-right bending and a CSA-approved electrical panel.
points: Stationary benders from Ø1″ (26 mm) to Ø2-3/8″ (60 mm)
Portable 110/220 V single-phase benders for the site
Stirrup, spiral and dowel bar bending
faq: Which rebar bender do I need for 15M, 20M and 25M bars?

A B 36 or BS 36 bends single bars up to 35M (#11) and two 20M bars at once in normal steel, and is the usual choice for a rebar shop running 10M to 25M. For site work on 10M–20M a portable BT 26 or MG 26 Junior on 110/220 V is enough. For 30M–45M bars choose a B 45x1, B 50 or the BS 50/BS 60.
Can I run a rebar bender on single-phase power?

Yes — the portable MG 20B, MG 26 Junior, BT 24x5 and BT 26 have a built-in transformer and run on 110 V or 220 V single-phase. The stationary B, BS, SL and SX machines are three-phase and are supplied for 600 V; 208 V, 240 V or 480 V are available on request.
Can a standard rebar bender make stirrups?

Yes. The B series and the portable BT benders make stirrups with the standard pins and rollers; an optional spiral stirrup attachment is available for B and BS series only. For continuous stirrup production from coil use the automatic SLS 12 on the automatic lines page.
What is the difference between the B series and the BS series?

The BS series has a longer table and two bending sleeves, so it bends faster and handles longer, heavier bars — up to Ø2-3/8″ (60 mm) on the BS 60. The B series is more compact and covers Ø1″ to Ø2″ (26–50 mm).
How many bends per shift can a stationary bender make?
A B 45x1 bends about 1,100 pieces of rebar in an 8-hour shift with one operator, with the angle programmed and the machine cycling automatically.

pages.h1: Rebar cutters — hydraulic and electric cutting machines to Ø2-3/8″
pages.desc: Rebar cutters and rebar cutting machines in Canada: the portable POWER 24, hydraulic and mechanical cutters to the SH 60 for Ø2-3/8″ (60 mm) bar. CSA panels.
pages.intro: Hydraulic and mechanical rebar cutters built by GMS in Turkey and supplied in Canada by NovoTech: the H series hydraulic cutters on cast-iron wheels for sites and shops, the fast M series mechanical cutters, the double-acting SH 45 and SH 60 for heavy bar, and the portable POWER 24 on single-phase power. Every model cuts two smaller bars at once.
points: Cut single bars up to Ø2-3/8″ (60 mm), or two bars at once
Hydraulic, mechanical and double-acting hydraulic cutters
Portable 110/220 V single-phase POWER 24
faq: Hydraulic or mechanical rebar cutter — which one should I buy?

A hydraulic H series cutter is quiet, needs less maintenance and can stop mid-stroke, which suits construction sites and general shops. A mechanical M series cutter cuts faster (0.8 s per cut) and suits a rebar shop cutting all day. For bar above Ø2″ (50 mm) or continuous heavy work choose the double-acting SH 45 or SH 60.
Can I run a rebar cutter on single-phase power?

The portable POWER 24 has a built-in transformer and runs on 110 V or 220 V single-phase. The H, M and SH cutters are three-phase and are supplied for 600 V; 208 V, 240 V or 480 V are available on request.
What does the 45 / 65 / 85 kg/mm² cutting capacity mean?

The three columns are the manufacturer's ratings for rebar of different tensile strengths: 45 kg/mm² (≈ 64,000 psi), 65 kg/mm² (≈ 92,500 psi) and 85 kg/mm² (≈ 120,900 psi). Canadian Grade 400W rebar has a minimum tensile strength of 540 MPa (≈ 55 kg/mm²), so the 65 kg/mm² column is a safe guide for everyday Canadian bar.
Are replacement cutting blades available in Canada?
Yes. NovoTech stocks cutting blades, hydraulic parts and electrical components for GMS cutters in Mississauga, ON, Canada. Blades are reversible and can be turned to a fresh edge before replacement.
Is there a machine that both cuts and bends?
Yes — the MAX 40 combined machine cuts up to Ø1-1/8″ (30 mm) and bends up to Ø1-3/8″ (36 mm). You will find it on the rebar benders page.

pages.h1: Riveting machines — hydraulic orbital riveters, rivets to Ø1-3/16″
pages.desc: Orbital riveting machines sold, installed and supported in Canada: value-line XM-5 to XM-30 hydraulic orbital riveters, solid rivets Ø3/16″ to Ø1-3/16″.
pages.intro: An orbital (rolling) riveting machine forms the head of a solid rivet by rolling the rivet end into shape instead of hammering it, with about a tenth of the force of punch riveting: the part keeps its fit and the head comes out smooth, without vibration or noise. It replaces hammering, punching and hot riveting on hinges, chain links, brake parts, appliances and hardware, and with other tools the machine works as a normal press. NovoTech's value-line XM riveters, built in China, come in six sizes, small to large, for solid rivets from Ø3/16″ (XM-5, 1,911 lbf) to Ø1-3/16″ (XM-30, 22,481 lbf), with 11 rivet head forms and tables from Ø4.7″ to 19.7 × 14″. The specification table and photo are below. Parts, installation and service from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: XM-5 to XM-30 orbital riveters: solid rivets Ø3/16″ to Ø1-3/16″, 1,911 – 22,481 lbf
11 rivet head forms; tables Ø4.7″ to 19.7 × 14″; works as a normal press with other tools
Low noise, no vibration — replaces hammering, punching and hot riveting
faq: Which XM riveter for my rivet?

Choose by the largest solid rivet you set: XM-5 to Ø3/16″, XM-8 to Ø5/16″, XM-10 to Ø3/8″, XM-16 to Ø5/8″, XM-20 to Ø13/16″ and XM-30 to Ø1-3/16″. Send us a drawing of the part and the rivet and we confirm the size and the head form.
Orbital riveting or pressing the rivet?

Pressing or punching sets the whole head at once and needs about ten times the force, which can distort the part and loosen the fit. The orbital head rolls the rivet end outward a little at a time, so the force stays low, the head comes out smooth and the part keeps its fit — the reason it is used for hinges, chain links and brake parts.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Portable roofing and siding brakes (aluminum brakes), 40″ to 12.5 ft
pages.desc: Portable roofing and siding brakes sold in Canada: ALB aluminum brakes with roller slitter, 24 ga steel over 7.2 – 12.5 ft, and BSM shear-and-brake machines.
pages.intro: A portable roofing and siding brake folds flashing, trim, drip edge and fascia on site: an aluminum frame on folding legs, set up in 10 to 15 minutes, that clamps 24 ga steel or 0.032″ aluminum coil, bends it to 180° and slits the coil with a roller knife. NovoTech sells three kinds in Canada, all on this page: the ALB aluminum brakes, six models from 7.2 to 12.5 ft with a silicone insert in the bending beam for pre-painted coil and copper, a slitter on a track and a carrying stand; the BSM1550 and BSM3150 shear and brake machines that bend 22 ga over 61″ and 124″ and slit it over 59″ and 122″, with gas springs that lift the bending beam and carry the slitter head, on a mobile stand; and the BSM1016, BSM1220 and BSM2540 folding brakes with a slitter on a fold-away stand, 20 – 22 ga over 40 to 100″. The CD-24 coil dispenser feeds 24″ trim coil to the brake. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. NovoTech's value-line brakes are built in China to our specification, with parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: BSM1550 / BSM3150 shear and brake machines 22 ga × 61″ and 124″, slitter head on gas springs · BSM folding brakes with slitter 22 – 20 ga × 40 – 100″
ALB brakes 7.2 – 12.5 ft: 24 ga steel, 0.032″ aluminum, 0.024″ copper; bend to 180°, 22.8″ throat
Roller slitter on a track cuts the coil to width on the brake; silicone insert protects painted and copper coil
Aluminum frame on folding legs, 132 – 220 lb, carried on the truck; CD-24 trim coil dispenser
faq: What do I need to bend roofing flashing on site?

A portable roofing brake: the ALB brakes have an aluminum frame on folding legs, set up in 10 – 15 minutes, take 24 ga steel and 0.032″ aluminum over 7.2 – 12.5 ft, bend to 180° and slit the coil with a roller knife. Add the CD-24 dispenser for trim coil. For the shop, a box and pan brake or a magnetic brake does the same work in heavier gauges.
Which length should I buy?

Long enough for the longest piece you make in one bend — 10 ft for fascia and drip edge is the common choice, 12.5 ft for commercial trim — and no longer, because the brake is carried: the 7.2 ft model weighs 132 lb, the 12.5 ft model about 220 lb. Longer pieces are made in two overlapping bends.
Does the slitter come with the brake?

Yes: a roller slitter on a track cuts the coil to width on the brake before folding, so a 24″ coil becomes drip edge, J-channel and fascia without a separate shear. Replacement cutting wheels are stocked in Mississauga, ON, Canada.
What is a slitting brake, and what does a shear and brake machine add?

A slitting brake has a slitter that runs along the clamping beam to cut a strip from the sheet before folding it — the tool for trim and flashing from coil. The BSM1016, BSM1220 and BSM2540 have a slitting device that comes off; the BSM1550 and BSM3150 shear and brake machines carry the slitter head on gas springs and slit 22 ga over 59″ and 122″, with a gas spring that lifts the bending beam, on a mobile stand.
Will it mark painted coil?

No — the bending beam has a silicone insert and the clamping surfaces are smooth aluminum, made for pre-painted steel and aluminum coil and for copper. Keep the protective film on the coil for a flawless finish.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Hydraulic and rotary draw pipe benders — pipe, tube and bar to Ø3-1/8″
pages.desc: Hydraulic and rotary draw pipe benders sold in Canada: ISITAN BK rotary draw benders, premium-line TB 34 / TB 42 and SPB 60 / 76 benders, to Ø3-1/8″.
pages.intro: A rotary draw bender clamps the tube to a rotating bend die and draws it around the die radius without an internal mandrel, and a hydraulic pipe bender bends pipe around a die with a hydraulic ram — the simplest machines for handrail, gate, fence, furniture, plumbing, exhaust and repair bends in pipe, tube and bar. NovoTech sells three lines in Canada, all on this page: ISITAN's BK series, four rotary draw benders from the 1 HP BK-42 for 1-1/4″ pipe to the BK 030 (76) for Ø3″ × 11 ga steel tube, bending pipe, tube, solid and flat bar and box section with one included tooling set; NovoTech's premium line, built in Turkey — the TB 34 electric bench bender for 1″ NPS pipe, the 17-ton hydraulic TB 42 for 1-1/4″ NPS pipe and the SPB 60 and SPB 76 NC draw benders with a 500-program memory for Ø2-3/8″ and Ø3″ pipe; and NovoTech's value line, built in China — the EHB-10 electric hydraulic pipe bender and the TB-3 and HTB-1000 benders for 2″ schedule 40 pipe, the HTB-25T 25-ton tubing bender and the TBM-60 electric bender to 2-1/2″, the HTB-2000 exhaust bender with an expander-swager and the JTB hydraulic PLC tube benders to Ø3-1/8″. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. For thin-wall tube to a tight radius, see the NC and CNC mandrel benders.
points: ISITAN BK rotary draw benders: 1/8″ to 2-1/2″ NPS pipe, Ø3″ × 11 ga steel tube, bar and box section — one tooling set included
NovoTech premium line: TB 34 electric and 17-ton TB 42 hydraulic pipe benders · SPB 60 / SPB 76 NC draw benders with 500 programs
NovoTech value line: EHB-10, TB-3 and HTB-1000 for 2″ pipe · HTB-25T and TBM-60 · HTB-2000 exhaust bender · JTB hydraulic PLC tube benders to Ø3-1/8″
faq: Rotary draw or mandrel bender?

A rotary draw bender clamps the tube to a bend die and draws it around; without an internal mandrel it suits thicker walls and radii of about 2× the diameter and up — handrail, gate, fence and furniture work. Thin-wall tube to a tight radius needs the mandrel support of an NC or CNC mandrel bender. The BK capacity table lists the maximum tube, bar and box section for each model.
Which BK for stainless handrail?

The BK-050 bends Ø2-3/8″ × 14 ga 304/316 stainless tube and the BK-H 060 Ø2-3/8″ × 12 ga — the common 1-1/2″ and 2″ handrail sizes with room to spare. The hydraulic BK-H 060 draws from one direction, which makes sequential bends on long rails easier.
Does it come with tooling?

The BK benders come with one set — bend die, clamp die and counter die — in the size you request. Additional sets for other diameters, square tube, flat bar and box section are quoted with the machine; tell us material, size, wall, CLR and angle.
BK, SPB or TB?

For the occasional bend in pipe up to 1-1/4″ NPS, the premium-line TB 34 (electric, digital angle stop) or TB 42 (17-ton hydraulic) is the simplest and lowest-cost premium machine. For railing, gate and furniture work in pipe, tube, bar and box section, the ISITAN BK series with its programmable controls and capacity to Ø3″ tube. For repeated multi-bend parts in pipe to Ø2-3/8″ or Ø3″, the SPB 60 or SPB 76 with a 500-program NC. Thin-wall tube to a tight radius needs a mandrel bender.
Rotary-draw, push-type or roll bending?

A rotary-draw bender (JTB, TBM-60, HTB-25T, TB-3, HTB-1000) pulls the tube around a die with a clamp and a follower — a tight, accurate bend with little flattening, the method for roll cages, railings, frames and exhaust. A push-type hydraulic pipe bender (EHB-10) pushes the pipe into a die between two supports — simple and fast for plumbing and electrical pipe, where some ovality is acceptable. For large radii, rings and spirals, see the tube rollers on the angle rolls page.
What do I need to tell you to choose the dies?

The outside diameter (or the square size), the wall thickness, the material and the centre-line radius (CLR) of the bend — usually 2 to 4 times the tube diameter. Tube and pipe sizes differ: 1-1/2″ schedule 40 pipe is 1.900″ OD, while 1-1/2″ tube is 1.500″ OD — the die must fit the OD exactly.
What voltage do the benders run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on the BK-42 and other models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase.

pages.h1: Bekamak semi-automatic band saws
pages.desc: Bekamak BMSY semi-automatic band saws: hydraulic vise, automatic bow return, miter heads to 60°, Ø9″ to Ø17-3/8″ (230–440 mm). Specs in inches and mm.
pages.intro: The workhorse of most fabrication shops: the operator loads the bar and presses start; the hydraulic vise clamps, the bow cuts at the set feed rate and lifts clear when the cut is done. Bekamak's BMSY pivot saws come with single- or double-miter heads for structural steel, inverter blade speed and hydro-mechanical blade tension — from Ø9″ to Ø17-3/8″ (230–440 mm). If you are looking for a semi-automatic metal bandsaw, a hydraulic horizontal band saw for metal or an industrial band saw machine with a hydraulic vise, this is the page.
points: Hydraulic vise, automatic bow return, inverter blade speed
Single- or double-miter heads to 60°; DGH models add a hydraulic vise
Round capacities from Ø9″ (230 mm) to Ø17-3/8″ (440 mm)
faq: What is the difference between a semi-automatic and a fully automatic band saw?

A semi-automatic saw makes one cut per start: it clamps, cuts and lifts the bow, then waits for the operator to feed the next piece. A fully automatic saw also feeds the material to length (by rollers or a shuttle vise) and repeats the cycle for the programmed quantity. See the Bekamak automatic band saws page.
Single miter or double miter?

A single-miter head (BMSY 320G/GL) swivels to one side, so angled parts are cut by flipping the bar. A double-miter head (BMSY DG/DGH) swivels both ways — +60° right, −45° left — which saves handling on frames and trusses with opposite angles.
What does the DGH suffix mean?

DGH models have a hydraulic vise — the DG versions clamp the material by hand. The rest of the saw is the same: double-miter head swung by hand on the angle scale, hydraulic feed cylinder and automatic bow return.
Can these saws cut bundles?
Yes, with the optional hydraulic top clamping, which presses a bundle of tubes or bars down while the side vise holds it. Ask us about bundle sizes for the model you need.

pages.h1: 3-in-1 shear, brake and roll machines — 8″ to 80″
pages.desc: 3-in-1 sheet metal machines sold in Canada: shear, brake and slip roll on one frame from 8″ to 52″ in 20 – 16 ga, and the motorized E3-IN-1 to 80″ and 14 ga.
pages.intro: A 3-in-1 machine puts a shear, a brake and a slip roll on one frame: the starter machine for the small sheet-metal, HVAC and hobby shop, and the compact machine for a maintenance department that cuts, folds and rolls a few parts a day. NovoTech sells two kinds in Canada, both on this page: hand-operated 3-in-1 machines from 8″ to 52″, 20 to 16 ga, with a guillotine shear, a finger brake and three rolls on one bench frame; and the motorized E3-IN-1 that shears 1/8″, bends 14 ga and rolls 12 ga over 52 and 80″ with a 4.7 HP motor. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. NovoTech's value-line machines are built in China to our specification, with parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Motorized E3-IN-1, 52″ and 80″: shears 1/8″, bends 14 ga, rolls 12 ga, 4.7 HP
Hand-operated 3-in-1 machines 8 – 52″: shear, finger brake and slip roll, 20 – 16 ga mild steel on one bench frame
Minimum rolling diameters per model; removable fingers for boxes; back gauge for the shear
faq: Is a 3-in-1 machine as good as three separate machines?

No — it is as good as the three machines a small shop would otherwise not have. The shear, brake and roll share one frame and one capacity rating, so each is lighter than a dedicated machine of the same width, and changing from one function to another takes a minute. For a shop that cuts, folds and rolls a few parts a day in 20 – 16 ga it is the right buy; for production, buy the dedicated shear, box and pan brake and slip roll.
Which size do I need?

By the widest sheet you cut or fold in one piece: the 12″ and 24″ models for enclosures and small parts, 40″ and 52″ for duct and panel work, 80″ (E3-IN-1) for full sheets. The capacity — 20 to 16 ga on the hand-operated models, 1/8″ shear and 14 ga brake on the motorized — is the same across the width.
How small a cylinder can it roll?

The minimum rolling diameter is set by the roll diameter and is listed per model in the table; the slip roll section also has grooves for wire and the top roll lifts to slip the finished cylinder off.
How are the capacities rated, and what about stainless and aluminum?

In gauge of mild steel over the full width; stainless about two gauges lighter, aluminum about two gauges heavier. The hand-operated models rate copper, brass and aluminum separately in the specification table.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Metal shears — hydraulic and mechanical shears, 20 ga to 1-9/16″
pages.desc: Metal shears sold, installed and supported in Canada, by kind: hydraulic swing beam, guillotine and light shears from 16 ga to 1-9/16″, mechanical shears.
pages.intro: A metal shear (sheet metal shearing machine, guillotine shear, shear cutter) cuts plate and sheet to size in one stroke between a fixed bottom blade and a top blade on the moving beam — the first machine in every sheet-metal, HVAC, signage and fabrication shop, before the press brake. NovoTech sells two kinds in Canada, each on its own page: hydraulic shears — swing beam and variable-rake guillotine plate shears to 1-9/16″ and 26 ft, in a premium line made in Turkey and a value line built to our specification, and light hydraulic shears from 16 ga to 1/4″ for the sheet-metal shop; and mechanical shears, with no hydraulics at all — direct-gear SRGM guillotines for 1/8″ and 1/4″ at 31 to 35 strokes a minute, electric and NC electric shears, motorized bench shears and a coil slitting and cut-to-length machine. Below, the two kinds compared and the questions we get asked; every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, a 1-year warranty and installation, training and parts from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Hydraulic: swing beam 5/32″ – 3/4″ × 6.8 – 20 ft and guillotine 1/4″ – 1-9/16″ × 8 – 26 ft; premium BS / BSY and DAS CNC, value QC12K / Q11K; light hydraulic shears 16 ga – 1/4″
Mechanical: SRGM direct-gear guillotines 1/8″ × 3.6 – 10 ft and 1/4″ × 3.6 – 13.8 ft, 31 – 35 strokes/min
Electric and NC electric shears 14 ga – 5/32″ × 49 – 100″, motorized bench shears and a 48″ coil slitting and cut-to-length machine
faq: Hydraulic or mechanical shear — which should I buy?

By the material and the hours. For sheet to 14 ga in a sheet-metal, HVAC or signage shop, the lowest-priced powered machines are the motorized bench shears, the Q11 electric shears and the light hydraulic shears, 26″ to 120″. For 1/8″ and 1/4″ all day, a mechanical guillotine shear is the faster and simpler machine: direct-gear drive, 31 – 35 strokes a minute, no hydraulics, with return-to-sender and cut-to-length versions. From 1/4″ plate up — 3/8″, 1/2″, to 1-9/16″ over 20 and 26 ft — the hydraulic shears are the machines, swing beam for the everyday plate shear and a variable-rake guillotine for production and thick plate. A mechanical shear has no hydraulic power pack, no oil to heat up and no valves or seals to service, and cuts the same on the first and the thousandth stroke; a small hydraulic shear is the quietest way to cut 14 ga to 5/32″ a few times an hour. Each kind comes in a premium and a value line on its page, and every machine is installed and supported by the same NovoTech technicians.
Premium line or value line?

The premium hydraulic shears (Dener BS / BSY and DAS CNC) and mechanical shears (SRGM) are built in Turkey on the heaviest frames with European hydraulics, motors and controls and parts in Mississauga, ON, Canada — for two shifts a day and the tightest cut. NovoTech's value line — the QC12K / Q11K hydraulic shears with Estun controls, the light hydraulic shears and the electric, bench and coil machines — is built in China to our specification at about two-thirds of the price, the right buy for a job shop. Both lines are sections on each page, so the comparison is side by side.
Swing beam or guillotine?

On a swing beam shear the beam pivots on two bearings and the cylinders swing it through the cut — few parts, a low price and a rake angle fixed by the design, which is fine for plate. A guillotine shear carries the beam straight down on rollers with a variable rake angle, so the same machine cuts thin sheet flat and fast at a small angle and thick plate at a steeper one; it also keeps the blade gap set automatically. For a plate shop cutting mostly 3/8″ and up, a swing beam shear (Dener BS, NovoTech QC12K); for a job shop that cuts everything from 16 ga to 3/4″ and beyond, a guillotine (Dener DAS, NovoTech Q11K).
How is the capacity rated, and what about stainless and aluminum?

Capacities are the makers' ratings for mild steel (about 65,000 psi) over the full blade length. Stainless steel is harder to shear, so count on about 60 % of the mild-steel thickness — 14 ga stainless on a 1/8″ machine, 11 ga on a 1/4″ machine, 3/8″ on a 5/8″ machine; aluminum cuts to the full rated thickness and about 50 % more. Tell us your thickest material and we size the shear with a margin.
Which length do I need?

The model number is the maximum shearing length in millimetres: 1250 – 1360 = 49 – 53.5″ (a 4 × 8 sheet cut across), 1500 – 1560 = 5 ft, 2000 – 2060 = 6.6 – 6.8 ft, 2500 – 2560 = 8.2 – 8.4 ft (a 4 × 8 sheet lengthwise), 3000 – 3200 = 10 – 10.5 ft (5 × 10 sheet), 4000 = 13 ft, 6000 = 20 ft plate. Most sheet-metal shops run an 8 or 10 ft machine so a full sheet is cut both ways; HVAC and signage shops are well served by 52 – 81″; plate shops buy 10 to 20 ft.
What is the back gauge, and is it NC?

The back gauge is the stop behind the blade that sets the width of the cut strip. The value-line light hydraulic and electric shears have a manual gauge with counter, an electric gauge or a PLC-positioned gauge depending on the model; the SRGM and the hydraulic plate shears come with an NC back gauge — the operator keys in the dimension and the gauge moves there — and the Dener DAS with a 1 m ball-screw gauge set by the CNC together with the blade gap and the cutting angle.
What about safety and the Ontario pre-start review?

Finger guards along the blade, rear guard fences or photocells / light curtains, an anti-repeat single-stroke control and a mobile foot pedal with emergency stop are standard or available on every line; we recommend the photocell or light-curtain rear guard on every powered shear. In Ontario a new shear needs a pre-start health and safety review (PSR) under Regulation 851 before it runs.
Do you deliver, install and service in Canada?

Yes — every shear is shipped to Mississauga, ON, Canada, unloaded, levelled, commissioned and the operators trained by NovoTech; blades and parts for all four lines are stocked here. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, 600 V standard (208 / 240 / 480 V on request) and a 1-year warranty.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Sheet and tube combination lasers — one machine for sheet and tube
pages.desc: Sheet-and-tube fiber lasers sold in Canada: a sheet laser with a rotary chuck beside the table, from the ULET with shuttle table to 41 × 8.2 ft, tube Ø13.8″.
pages.intro: A sheet-and-tube laser puts a rotary chuck and tube supports beside the cutting table, so the same head cuts flat sheet from the table and holes, copes and lengths in round, square and rectangular tube from the chuck — one machine, one source and one footprint for a shop that cuts both. NovoTech sells two families in Canada, both on this page and both from the value line: the ULET with its shuttle table for sheet from 10 × 5 to 41 × 8.5 ft and tube to Ø13.8″, 1.5 to 40 kW; and the Senfeng HM series with a dual exchange table for 5 × 10 to 8.3 × 20 ft sheet and Ø8.6″ × 20 ft tube, 1.5 to 30 kW. Each family below has its full specification table, photos and brochure. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, chiller and nesting software, installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. For a dedicated tube machine with bundle loading see the tube laser cutters.
points: ULET: sheet 10 × 5 to 41 × 8.5 ft on a shuttle table plus tube to Ø13.8″ and 40 ft, 1.5 – 40 kW
HM series: sheet 5 × 10 to 8.3 × 20 ft on a dual exchange table plus Ø8.6″ × 20 ft tube, 1.5 – 30 kW
One head, one source, one footprint — tube supports and chuck fold away when cutting sheet
faq: Sheet and tube on one machine — what does the ULET add?

The ULET adds a pneumatic rotary chuck and tube supports to the sheet laser with shuttle table: round, square and rectangular tube to Ø8.7″ or Ø13.8″ and 20, 30 or 40 ft long, cut with the same source and head, and sheet to 41 × 8.5 ft and 40 kW. A shop that cuts tube every day is better served by a dedicated ULT tube laser with a loader.
What is the HM sheet-and-tube combination?

An H series sheet laser with a rotary chuck and tube supports on the side: the same 6 to 30 kW source and head cut 5 × 10 to 8.3 × 20 ft sheet with the pallet changer and round, square or rectangular tube from Ø0.7 to 8.6″ and 20 ft long. For a shop that cuts both but cannot justify two machines — switching takes the time to load the tube.
Combination laser or a separate tube laser?

A combination laser is the right buy when tube is a part of the work, not all of it: it cuts tube to Ø13.8″ with the same head and source, loaded one bar at a time by hand, and costs far less than two machines. A dedicated tube laser loads from a bundle, supports long bars at both ends, cuts faster and runs unattended — the machine when tube is the main product. The tube laser cutters have their own page.
What laser power do I need?

Power sets the thickness and the speed. As a guide for mild steel: 3 kW cuts 1/2″, 6 kW 3/4″ (and 1/4″ at over 300 in/min), 12 kW 1″, 20 kW 1-1/4″ and 30 – 40 kW 1-1/2″ and beyond; stainless and aluminum run about 20 – 30 % thinner at the same power, with nitrogen or air assist. Most Canadian job shops buying today choose 6 or 12 kW: thick enough for structural work, fast enough to pay for the machine on thin sheet. Tell us your material mix and we run the cutting chart for you.
What about assist gas and fume extraction?

Oxygen gives the fastest cut and an oxide edge on mild steel; nitrogen a clean, paint-ready edge on all metals; compressed air at 16 bar replaces nitrogen on sheet to about 1/4″ and cuts the gas bill to near zero — the intelligent air-cutting package is an option on both lines. The machines have pneumatic extraction compartments under the table and connect to a dust collector, which we can supply.
What does the machine need on site?

A level floor, 600 V 3-phase (with the transformer we supply) or 480 V, a chiller (included), assist gas, a dust collector and a compressed-air supply for air cutting. A 6 kW 3015 draws about 46 kW in total (Dener's figure for the GFL) and needs roughly 33 × 20 ft with its shuttle table. Delivery, installation and operator training are done by NovoTech from Mississauga, ON, Canada, and the Ontario pre-start health and safety review is prepared by us.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Sheet metal hand brakes — straight brakes, folders and bench brakes
pages.desc: Sheet metal hand brakes sold in Canada: straight brakes from 12″ to 13 ft in 22 – 12 ga, foot-clamp folding machines with a one-piece blade, and bench brakes.
pages.intro: A sheet metal hand brake clamps the sheet under a one-piece beam and swings a folding leaf up around the edge by hand — long, straight, clean bends in thin sheet with no punch and die and no marks on painted material. NovoTech sells three kinds in Canada, all on this page: straight hand brakes from a 12″ bench model to 13 ft, in 22 to 12 ga, for flashing, trim and duct panels; foot-clamp folding machines with one-piece blades from 36 to 119″ whose clamping beam closes from a foot pedal so both hands guide the sheet, to 12 ga; and bench brakes and offset brakes for the bench and the job box. The folding machines with segmented blades are with the box and pan brakes, and the BSM slitting brakes and shear and brake machines with the roofing and siding brakes. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. NovoTech's value-line brakes are built in China to our specification, with parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Straight hand brakes 12″ – 13 ft, 22 to 12 ga mild steel; counterweighted leaf, adjustable clamping and radius
Foot-clamp folding machines 36 – 119″, 22 to 12 ga: pedal clamping, both hands on the sheet, one-piece blades
Bench brakes 14 – 39″ and offset brakes, 20 – 18 ga
faq: Hand brake, box and pan brake or magnetic brake — which do I need?

A hand (straight) brake has a one-piece clamping blade: the best choice for long straight bends — flashing, trim, duct panels. A box and pan brake has a blade made of removable fingers, so it folds the four sides of a box or a pan; with all the fingers in it works as a straight brake too. A magnetic brake has no clamping beam at all — an electromagnet holds a loose steel bar on the sheet — so it folds boxes of any depth, closed and narrow shapes and short return flanges, at the cost of a lower capacity. For 14 ga and heavier, or for production, choose a hydraulic or electric folding machine. Each kind has its own page.
What does a foot-clamp folding machine add over a hand brake?

The clamping beam is closed by a foot pedal through a linkage instead of a hand lever, so the operator keeps both hands on the sheet to position it against the back stop — faster for repeat parts and safer for long, floppy sheet. The folding leaf is still swung by hand, with an adjustable angle stop for repeat bends.
How are the capacities rated, and what about stainless and aluminum?

Capacities are given in gauge of mild steel over the full bending length. Stainless steel bends at about two gauges lighter (a 16 ga brake takes 20 ga stainless), aluminum at about two gauges heavier. Bending at less than full length lets a brake take somewhat heavier sheet; folding heavier material than rated bends the beams permanently.
Can a brake fold painted or coated sheet without marking it?

Yes — the sheet is clamped and the leaf swings around the clamp edge without sliding over a die, so pre-painted and stainless sheet stays clean; a strip of protective film keeps a mirror finish perfect.
What is an offset brake?

An offset brake makes the small Z-shaped step (offset) at the edge of a panel in one stroke, for lap joints and door panels. The ZWJ-20 and ZWJ-36 make 1/2″ offsets up to 90° in 20 ga steel and 18 ga aluminum. For slitting brakes, see the roofing and siding brakes.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
