pages.h1: Metal deburring and finishing machines, 5-7/8″ to 53-1/8″ wide
pages.desc: Gecam wide-belt deburring, edge rounding, deslagging and brush deburring machines and benches for laser-, punch- and plasma-cut parts, dry or wet, to 53″.
pages.intro: A metal deburring machine takes the burr, slag and sharp edges off laser-, punch- and plasma-cut parts and gives them an even finish — in one pass on a conveyor, where hand grinding takes minutes per part and never comes out the same twice. NovoTech sells the machines of Gecam, built in Parma, Italy, small to large: wide-belt deburring and satin-finishing machines from the 5-7/8″ G15 to the 53-1/8″ G135, dry or wet, with an abrasive belt, top brushes and Scotch-Brite brushes in one pass; edge rounding machines that round every edge to 5/64″ (2 mm), inside holes too, or both sides of the part at once; the G65DCC, which breaks the slag off thick plasma and oxy-fuel parts; and, for shops that do not need a wide-belt line, CUB brush machines, the EASY T brushing workstation and GCB crossed-belt benches for heavy, long and shaped parts. Supplied with a CSA-approved panel, installed and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. For the shop that starts deburring by machine, the NovoTech value-line MGM-300 (12″) and BFM-2560 (24″, with a wet dust collector) are wide-belt machines for laser-cut and punched parts, and the R series dry sanders take one to three sanding heads over 24.8″ or 51.2″.
points: Wide-belt deburring and satin finishing, 5-7/8″ to 53-1/8″ wide · parts .020″ to 4-3/4″ thick, dry or wet
Edge rounding to 5/64″ (2 mm), both sides in one pass on the GT06 and GT13 · G65DCC deslagging for plasma parts 3/8″ – 4-3/4″
CUB conveyor brush machines, the EASY T vacuum-table workstation and GCB crossed-belt benches for heavy and shaped parts
faq: What does a deburring machine do?

It removes the burr that laser cutting, punching, shearing and plasma cutting leave on a part's edges, rounds the sharp edges and evens out the surface — in one pass on a conveyor, where hand grinding takes minutes per part and never comes out the same twice. Deburred parts are safe to handle, bend and weld cleanly, and take paint and powder coating evenly right to the edge.
Belt, brushes or both?

The abrasive belt (R) cuts the burr off and levels the surface; top brushes (X, T) and brush carousels (B4, B8) round the edges, inside holes too; cylindrical Scotch-Brite brushes (B) give a satin finish. Most shops combine them — a belt and top brushes deburr and round in one pass, and a Scotch-Brite brush at the end leaves an even grain.
Do you also sell corner grinders?

Yes. Corner grinders (also called corner sanders or weld seam sanders) grind the weld on the corner of a welded box, cabinet, door or tray flush or to a radius. They have their own page: the hand-fed GECAM 131 and 136, the GECAM 135 that runs the full length of an edge up to 59″ by itself, and PLC corner grinders for series work — see Corner grinders in the menu, or the button at the top of this page.
Which machine for plasma and oxy-fuel parts?

The G65DCC: its D belt on a soft rubber roller breaks the slag off the bottom edge of parts 3/8″ to 4-3/4″ thick and strip brushes on two transverse belts round the edges in the same pass. For thinner plasma parts with light dross a G65 with belt and top brushes is usually enough.
Can it round edges on both sides at once?

Yes — the GT06 and GT13 run strip brushes on cross belts above and below the part and round every edge on both sides in one pass, leaving the faces as they were. The G135RB8 works from the top with the deepest radius, 5/64″ (2 mm).
What do the letters R, X, B, b, B4 and T stand for?

They are Gecam's working groups, named in the order the part meets them. R is an abrasive belt on a rubber contact roller — it takes off the burr and levels the surface. X is a double row of rotating, oscillating top brushes that round the edges, inside holes and slots too, and T a single row of them. B is a cylindrical Scotch-Brite brush for the finish and b an external one below the outfeed. B4 is a carousel of four abrasive brushes for heavier edge rounding. A G65 RXB, for example, deburrs, rounds and satin-finishes in one pass.
Which width do I need?

Take the widest part you cut and add a little margin: 5-7/8″ (G15) and 11-13/16″ (G30) for small laser and punched parts, 25-9/16″ (G65, GM65) for most job-shop work, 43-5/16″ (GM110) and 53-1/8″ (G135) when you deburr nested parts or full sheets. Thickness is not the limit — every machine takes parts up to 4-1/8″ or 4-3/4″ — but the groups are: plain deburring needs a belt, edge rounding needs brushes.
How much dust extraction does a deburring machine need?

Each machine has a hood at every working group and needs a dust collector of the airflow in its table: 1,177 CFM (2,000 m³/h) for the G15, G30, GM65 and GM110, 2,354 CFM for the G65 and 3,531 CFM for the G135. We quote a matching collector with the machine. Wet machines need no dust collector — the water takes the dust to the sludge tank.
Can it handle small parts?

Yes, with the right options: a vacuum table holds small parts of any material on the conveyor, and a magnetic track holds small steel parts. The rubberized pressure rollers before and after each group keep parts flat as they pass. Very small or awkward parts are better finished on a brush workstation such as the EASY T.
Dry or wet?

Dry machines with dust extraction suit most steel and stainless work. Choose a wet machine when the heat of dry grinding would deform the parts, or when you want no grinding dust in the shop: the G30 WET and G65/135 WET spray water directly on every tool and collect the sludge in an external tank.
Why round the edges of laser-cut parts?

A laser or punch leaves a sharp, square edge that cuts hands and gloves and on which paint and powder coating pull thin — the edge is the first place a coated part rusts. A rounded edge is safe to handle and takes an even coat. The G135RB8 rounds edges to a 5/64″ (2 mm) radius; the GT06 and GT13 round the edges evenly on both sides at once.
One side or both sides?

The G135RB8 works the top of the part, with the deepest radius and a belt for heavy burrs. The GT06 and GT13 work the edges from above and below in the same pass, so parts are not turned over and fed twice, and they leave the faces untouched — the choice for galvanized, brushed or pre-painted sheet.
Do the brushes mark coated or brushed sheet?

The strip brushes of the GT06 and GT13 work the edges and leave the faces as they were, so galvanized, brushed and pre-painted surfaces are kept. The G135RB8 is also suitable for surface-treated material; set its belt group off when the face must not be touched.
Brush machine or wide-belt deburring machine?

A CUB brush machine deburrs and satin-finishes flat parts with cylindrical brushes — a clean, even finish and light deburring at a much lower price. Heavy burrs, edge rounding to a set radius and high volumes call for a wide-belt machine with an abrasive belt and top brushes, further up this page.
Which parts suit the EASY T?

Parts a conveyor cannot carry or would not finish evenly: thick plates up to 5-7/8″, heavy brackets, shaped and bent parts, and single pieces. The vacuum table holds the part while the operator guides the brush; the second tool on the arm is a quick tilt away.
What is a crossed-belt bench used for?

Long and shaped parts — profiles, frames, panels, parts with flanges — that the operator deburrs, rounds and satin-finishes against the belt, choosing a roller, shoe or brush and its position along the belt for each job. The motorized table carries parts up to 220 lb, and the optional suction-cup manipulator holds shaped parts in any position.
Do you install the machines and train operators?

Yes. Our technicians install and commission the machine anywhere in Canada, set up the groups and abrasives for your parts and train the operators; abrasives, brushes and parts are supplied from Mississauga, ON, Canada, and we support every machine by video call.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Surface grinders — TGH-B 450 NC surface grinder, 17.7 × 35.4″ table
pages.desc: Surface grinder for sale in Canada: the Dener TGH-B 450 precision NC surface grinder, 17.7 × 35.4″ table, 15.7 × 31.5″ magnetic chuck, Ø13.8″ wheel.
pages.intro: A surface grinder finishes flat, parallel and square faces to tenths: the part sits on a magnetic chuck on a table that runs back and forth under a grinding wheel, the wheel steps across at each stroke and comes down a few tenths at a time until the face is true. NovoTech sells the Dener TGH-B 450 in Canada, built in Kayseri, Turkey: a 17.7 × 35.4″ (450 × 900 mm) table on scraped, Turcite-B coated V and flat guideways, driven hydraulically at 16 – 82 ft/min, a Ø13.8″ (350 mm) wheel on a direct-drive spindle with 21.7″ (550 mm) under the wheel centre, and AC servo motors on ballscrews for the cross and vertical axes under a Mitsubishi NC with a 10″ touchscreen — the operator sets the stock to remove, and the machine down-feeds in 0.00004″ (0.001 mm) steps and cross-feeds 0.002 – 0.79″ per stroke by itself. Installed and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: 17.7 × 35.4″ table, 15.7 × 31.5″ electromagnetic chuck, 882 lb table load, 3 – 21.7″ under the wheel centre
Mitsubishi NC with 10″ touchscreen: automatic down feed in 0.00004″ steps and cross feed 0.002 – 0.79″ per stroke
Direct-drive spindle 100 – 1,450 rpm, Ø13.8″ wheel; hydraulic table 16 – 82 ft/min on scraped V and flat ways
faq: What does the NC do on a surface grinder?

On a manual grinder the operator turns the handwheels for every pass. On the TGH-B 450 the cross and vertical axes are AC servo axes under the Mitsubishi NC: the operator enters the stock to remove, the down feed per pass and the cross feed, and the machine grinds the face — roughing, finishing and spark-out passes — while the hydraulic table runs back and forth. The handwheel stays for touching off and setup.
How large a part can it grind?

Faces up to 35.4 × 17.7″ (900 × 450 mm) on the 15.7 × 31.5″ (400 × 800 mm) electromagnetic chuck, parts up to 882 lb (400 kg), and up to 21.7″ (550 mm) from the table to the wheel centre — about 14.8″ of part height under a new Ø13.8″ wheel.
Which accessories are worth adding?

A magnetic sine plate and sine bar for angled faces, a precision toolmaker's vise for non-magnetic parts, a magnetic separator with the paper filter for long coolant life, a wheel-head diamond dresser and a profile dressing attachment for formed wheels, and a demagnetizer for finished parts. A second wheel flange makes wheel changes quick.
Do you deliver, install and train in Canada?

Yes. Machines ship from Kayseri to Mississauga, ON, Canada; NovoTech unloads, levels and commissions the machine, checks the geometry, trains your operators and programmers on the control and helps with the first parts. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, a 1-year warranty and parts and service from Mississauga. Ask for the foundation drawing and the power and air requirements before the machine ships.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Trumpf and Wila-style (New Standard) press brake tooling
pages.desc: Trumpf-style punches to 300 mm and dies V6 – V120, Wila-style (New Standard) punches and dies — safety buttons, made in Italy, DXF profiles.
pages.intro: EUROSTAMP tooling for press brakes with Trumpf and Wila (New Standard) clamping — Trumpf, Darley, Safan, RPC and the other makers that use this hydraulic clamping. Trumpf-style punches stand 140 to 300 mm (5.51 – 11.81″) tall for deep boxes, with dies from V6 to V120 in 100, 120 and 150 mm heights; Wila-style punches run from 135 to 237 mm and the dies are 55 or 100 mm high. Tools up to 13.5 kg (Trumpf style) and 12.5 kg (Wila style) come with safety buttons that stop a released tool from falling, so they load from the front. 42CrMo4 and C45 steel, induction-hardened, with a DXF profile of every tool.
points: Trumpf-style punches 5.51 – 11.81″ (140 – 300 mm) high, rated to 84 US t/ft (250 t/m); dies V .24 – 4.72″
Wila-style punches 5.31 – 9.33″ (135 – 237 mm); dies 55 and 100 mm (2.17 / 3.94″) high
Safety buttons standard on the lighter tools; 500 / 515 mm lengths and 550 mm sectioned sets
faq: Are Trumpf-style and Wila-style tools interchangeable?

They share the New Standard clamping idea — a vertical tang with safety buttons that the hydraulic clamp pulls up and seats — and EUROSTAMP lists Trumpf, Darley and Safan brakes for both. Check the tang and the heights of the tools you already run before mixing them, and send us the clamp model if you are unsure; we confirm before you order.
What do the safety buttons do?

The spring-loaded buttons in the tang catch the tool in the clamp while it is released, so it can be loaded and removed from the front without falling. EUROSTAMP fits them as standard on Trumpf-style tools up to 13.5 kg (30 lb) and Wila-style tools up to 12.5 kg (27.5 lb); heavier tools are loaded from the side.
Which height should I order?

Match the height of the tools already in the machine so the punch tips and die shoulders stay on the same line — mixing heights means re-setting the ram. Use the tall 220 – 300 mm punches only where the part needs the depth, as the load rating falls with height.
Can we get the tools as DXF files for our CNC?

Yes — every tool in these tables that has a DXF link can be downloaded straight from the page: the profile drawn in millimetres, ready to import into the tool library of a Delem, ESA or Cybelec control or into offline bending software. For the few tools without one, ask us and we get the drawing from EUROSTAMP.

pages.h1: Tube end deburring machine — pipe and tube ends, inside and out
pages.desc: Tube end deburring machine for cut pipe and tube: the Eurofintec 143 deburrs the end inside and outside in one cycle, Ø13/16″ to 4-3/4″, cut at 90° or 45°.
pages.intro: A tube end deburring machine (pipe end deburring machine) takes the burr off the cut end of a tube or pipe — inside and outside — after the saw, the tube cutter or the laser, so the end is safe to handle, slides cleanly into a fitting or a joint and takes paint or plating evenly. NovoTech sells the Eurofintec 143, built in Parma, Italy, by Gecam: the tube end goes into an adjustable central prism against a Ø9-13/16 × 3-15/16″ wire brush that turns while its own axis rotates, changing direction so every edge is deburred evenly — the inside and the outside of the end in one cycle, on stainless tube and profiles, round Ø13/16″ to Ø4-3/4″ and square 13/16″ to 4-3/4″, cut at 90° or 45°, and on bent parts too. Two brush speeds and two speeds of the brush-axis rotation. Supplied with a CSA-approved panel, installed and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Inside and outside of the tube end deburred in one cycle — ends cut at 90° or 45°, bent parts too
Round tube Ø13/16″ – 4-3/4″ and square tube 13/16″ – 4-3/4″, stainless tube and profiles
Wire brush Ø9-13/16 × 3-15/16″: two brush speeds, two speeds of brush-axis rotation, adjustable central prism
faq: What does a tube end deburring machine do?

It removes the burr that the saw, the tube cutter or the laser leaves on the cut end of a tube or pipe, on the inside and the outside edge, so the end is safe to handle, fits into a fitting or a joint and welds, paints and plates cleanly. On the 143 the end is pushed against a wire brush that turns while its own axis rotates, so both edges are deburred evenly in one cycle.
Which tube sizes and cuts does the 143 take?

Round tube from Ø13/16″ to Ø4-3/4″ (20 – 120 mm) and square tube from 13/16″ to 4-3/4″, with ends cut at 90° or 45°, and bent parts too. The adjustable central prism at the entry centres the tube at the brush.
How are cut tube ends deburred on the 143?

The tube end is pushed into a prism against a wire brush that turns while its own axis rotates and changes direction, deburring the inside and the outside of the end in one cycle. Two brush speeds and two speeds of the axis rotation set the action for the material and the burr.
Does it polish the tube as well?

No — the 143 works the cut end only. To clean, satin-finish or polish the length of the tube, see the pipe sanding and polishing machines: the BT 114-S, the 141 and 144 orbital sanders, the 128 centreless sanders and the 728 tube brushing machine.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Tube end forming machines — expanding, reducing, beading and flanging
pages.desc: Tube end formers from Ø3-1/2″ expander-reducers and six-station formers to Swiss CNC inner / outer machines for Ø23.6″: expand, reduce, bead, flare, groove.
pages.intro: A tube end former (pipe end forming machine) expands or reduces the end of a tube so two tubes slip together, and the production versions bead, flare, flange, calibrate and emboss the end as well — the machines behind exhaust systems, ventilation and chimney tube, shock absorbers, handrail and furniture connectors. Three ranges on this page, small to large. ISITAN's SFF single-station hydraulic end formers expand and reduce tube to Ø3-1/2″ × 14 ga with one tooling set, for the fabrication shop. CSM's EF end formers carry six forming stations on one ram for tube to Ø2″, the REF machines roll grooves and the ER 30-5 forms, chamfers and grooves in one cycle — the end-finishing stations of a bending cell. Wecotech's Swiss tube end forming machines cover series production: the Easy line of compact expanders, reducers, a straightening press and a punching unit; the Universal line of modular production machines — expanders, reducers, axial and servo rotary formers, a multi-station forming centre and an automatic beading machine to Ø39.4″; the Traditional line built for the C and IO tooling that is standard in the exhaust trade; the Weco line of CNC inner / outer formers with programmable tool rotation for tube to Ø23.6″ and a flanging cell for bellows; and the shearing cutters, tube shear and deburring machine that complete an end-forming cell. Siemens controls, Bosch Rexroth hydraulics or servo drives, CSA-approved panels and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: ISITAN SFF hydraulic end formers to Ø3-1/2″ × 14 ga · CSM EF six-station formers to Ø2″, REF grooving and ER 30-5 end-finishing machines
Wecotech compact expanders and reducers from Ø3/8″ to Ø23.6″, 21 – 26 US tons, 2 – 4 s cycles, touchscreen programming
Wecotech CNC inner / outer formers to Ø23.6″ with 8 – 24 radial pistons, Tubimatic machines for standard C and IO tools, beading, flanging, shearing and deburring
faq: Expanding or reducing — what does the end former do?

An expander opens a tube end so the next tube slips inside (exhaust slip joints, telescoping handrail, sleeves); a reducer collapses the end to fit into the next tube. The ISITAN SFF does both in one station with a hydraulic ram and interchangeable forming tools; the Wecotech Tubex and Tubex-U expand with a cone-driven segmented tool, the Tubin and Tubin-U reduce with collet-type top jaws, and the Tubimatic and Weco-line machines do both — and bead, flare and flange — with inner and outer tools.
What do the CSM EF, REF and ER machines do?

The CSM EF carries six forming stations on one hydraulic ram, so expanding, reducing, beading, flaring and flanging run in sequence without a tool change — the end former to put beside a bender for tube to Ø13/16″, Ø1-3/16″ or Ø2″, in a horizontal or vertical layout. The REF 30 and REF 40 roll a groove into the tube end for O-ring and clamp connections; the ER 30-5 forms, chamfers and grooves the end in one cycle on a trolley that moves between cells. With a CSM WB wire bender the EF50 makes complete exhaust hangers.
What is an inner / outer (IO) tube end former?

A machine with two tools that work on the tube end at the same time: an inner mandrel or expansion tool inside the tube and an outer tool — closing jaws or, on the Weco line, 8 to 24 radial pistons — around it. Between them the end is expanded, reduced, beaded, flared, flanged or embossed to a defined shape in one stroke, in any position on round or shaped tube. The Tubimatic IO machines take the commercially available IO-tools; the Tubex IO-S and Wecomatic run Wecotech's own tooling under CNC.
Which Wecotech line do I need?

The Easy line is for a shop that forms a few hundred ends a day beside a bender or saw: compact, foot-switch operated, 21 US tons. The Universal line is the modular production machine with touchscreen programming, 26 US tons and the options that a production cell needs — heat exchangers, remote maintenance, Profisafe, horizontal version. The Traditional line is the choice when you already own C or IO tooling. The Weco line is for complex, multi-step forming of exhaust, ventilation and chimney parts at 10 – 40 s a cycle, programmed on the machine.
What tube sizes and wall thickness can the SFF form?

The SFF 90-1 expands tube from Ø1-3/8″ to Ø3-1/2″ and reduces ends down to Ø5/16″, in mild steel up to 14 ga; the SFF 60-1 covers tube to Ø2-3/8″. Stainless and thicker walls are quoted case by case — send us the tube OD, wall and the finished end size you need.
Hydraulic or Electra?

Wecotech builds the Tubimatic IO, Tubax-Rotary, Tubax-Multi and Tubecut as Electra versions with Bosch Rexroth servo drives instead of a hydraulic power unit: no oil, no heat exchanger, lower energy use and quieter running, with the forming force and position under direct servo control. The hydraulic versions keep the higher force reserve (37 US tons on the IO 160) and the lower price.
How long does a tool change take?

A few minutes on every machine on this page: the SFF holds its forming set in a quick-change holder; the Wecotech machines have quick-change flanges for the basic tool and the mandrel and quick-change interfaces for the outer jaws, and the Tubimatic C 80 TRE carries three tool stations so three forming steps run without a change at all.
Can the end former do an exhaust slip joint?

Yes — that is the most common job: expand one end of the pipe so the next section slides in, or reduce it to slip into a muffler or flex pipe, then bead it for the clamp. The SFF does the expansion and reduction; a Tubimatic IO or Wecomatic adds the bead, flare and calibration in the same stroke.
Where are these machines made and how are they supported?

The SFF is built by ISITAN in Bursa, Turkey; the Wecotech machines by Wecotech AG in Switzerland, a 60-person company whose customers include 3M, ABB, Akrapovič and American Axle. NovoTech sells, installs and supports both in Canada from Mississauga, ON, Canada, with CSA-approved panels, remote maintenance on the Wecotech controls and tooling to your tube size.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Tube and profile laser cutting machines — Ø0.3″ to 25.2″, 1.5 to 40 kW
pages.desc: Tube laser cutting machines sold and supported in Canada, compared side by side: two-chuck, three-chuck zero-tail, bevel-cutting and heavy machines to Ø25.2″.
pages.intro: A tube laser cuts round, square, rectangular and open profiles to length and cuts the holes, copes, slots and notches in them in one pass — no saw, no drill, no notcher, no layout — straight from the 3D model. Every tube laser NovoTech sells in Canada is on this page, and the table below sets the series side by side: how many chucks, what tube, how long and heavy a bar, how fast, and how it is loaded. Two chucks hold the tube at both ends and leave a short tail on each bar — the Dener E-FTL made in Turkey, NovoTech's ULT, the Senfeng T series, the high-speed PLUS for small tube in volume and the GPLUS / GT that cut ±45° bevels. Three chucks cut the last part with zero tail and carry long, heavy tube: the Dener FTL to Ø25.2″, the ULT three-chuck, the Senfeng NT and the heavy ST to Ø25″ and 6,614 lb. Each machine can be loaded by hand or crane, or with a semi-automatic or fully automatic loader — explained below. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, chiller and tube nesting software, a 1-year warranty and installation, training and parts from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Premium E-FTL Ø0.3″ – 13.8″, 1 G, ±0.05 mm, and premium FTL Ø0.6″ – 25.2″ with three chucks and zero tail, bars to 40 ft
Value ULT Ø0.4″ – 14.2″ with two or three chucks; T series two-chuck Ø0.5″ – 14.1″; PLUS high-speed Ø0.4″ – 9.4″; GPLUS / GT ±45° bevel
Three-chuck NT zero-tail Ø0.7″ – 14.1″ and heavy-duty ST Ø1.9″ – 25.1″, bars to 40 ft and 6,614 lb
Loaded by hand, or with a semi-automatic or fully automatic loader — see the loading options
faq: Two or three chucks — which should I buy?

By what you cut and what the leftover costs you. Two chucks hold the tube at both ends; the rear chuck has to keep hold of the bar, so a short tail of every bar is scrap — fine for mild steel in short and medium runs, and the cheapest machine: the Dener E-FTL, the NovoTech ULT and the Senfeng T, PLUS and GPLUS / GT. A third chuck takes over the bar as it shortens, so the last part is cut with zero tail, and it supports long, heavy tube so it is cut straight: the Dener FTL, the ULT three-chuck, the Senfeng NT and, for pipe and structural tube to Ø25″, the Senfeng ST. On 20 to 40 ft bars of stainless, aluminum or heavy-wall tube the saved material pays for the third chuck.
Premium line or value line?

The premium Dener E-FTL and FTL are built in Turkey with servo-driven chucks (1 G on the E-FTL), a Maxphotonics fiber source, a BOCI autofocus head and ±0.05 mm repeatability, with parts stocked in Canada — for the shop that runs the tube laser all day. NovoTech's value-line ULT and the Senfeng T / PLUS / GT / NT / ST are built in China with pneumatic chucks, in a wider range of sizes and powers at a lower price; NovoTech stocks the parts and does the service. The premium machine is faster between parts and holds tighter tolerance at high duty.
E-FTL or FTL?

The E-FTL is the fast machine for the sizes most fabricators use — railings, frames, furniture, trailers, exhaust — Ø0.3″ to 13.8″, accelerating at 1 G and running 394 ft/min on the small chucks. The FTL is built for weight: structural tube and pipe to Ø25.2″ and 40 ft (12 m) bars of 5,732 lb (2,600 kg), with ±0.1 mm repeatability on the large chucks. Both take 3 to 20 kW sources. The E-FTL holds the bar in two chucks and leaves a tail of 1.4″ (35 mm) or more; the FTL's three chucks cut the last part with zero remnant. A fully automatic bundle loader is an option on the E-FTL, a semi-automatic loader on the FTL.
What can a tube laser cut?

Round, square, rectangular, oval and open profiles — angle, channel, flat bar — in mild steel, stainless, aluminum, copper and brass, from the chuck's minimum to its maximum size, in wall thicknesses to about 1/2″ (12 kW) or 3/4″ (20 kW). Holes, slots, copes for tube-to-tube joints, tabs and notches for folding, engraving — anything you can draw on the surface of the profile. A 5-axis or 45° bevel head adds weld preparations and mitred corners.
Do I need an automatic loader?

Not to start: every machine here is loaded by hand or crane as standard, and the loader can usually be added later. A semi-automatic loader is worth it once an operator spends more time lifting tube than watching the machine — the operator keeps a rack or chain filled and the loader feeds one tube at a time, open profiles and special shapes included. A fully automatic bundle loader takes a whole 3 t bundle from the crane and feeds round, square and rectangular tube with nobody at the machine — the choice for production runs and two shifts.
What is zero-tailing — the NT series?

A two-chuck machine cannot cut the last part of the bar because the rear chuck has to hold something, so a remnant of the chuck length is scrapped from every bar. The NT puts a third chuck in the middle that takes over the bar as it shortens, so the last part is cut and the tail is near zero — on 20 to 40 ft stock to Ø14″ that is several percent of material saved on every bundle.
Which chuck size?

The number is the largest round tube in millimetres: E-FTL 120 takes Ø0.3 – 4.7″, 180 to 7.1″, 250 to 9.8″ and 350 to 13.8″; FTL 250, 350, 500 and 640 take Ø0.6″ to 9.8, 13.8, 19.7 and 25.2″. Square and rectangular tube goes to the same size — 350 × 350 mm (13.8″) on the 350 chuck. Buy the chuck for the largest tube you cut regularly — a smaller chuck is faster and holds thin tube better — and the bar length — 23, 30 or 40 ft (7, 9 or 12 m) on the E-FTL, 20, 30 or 40 ft (6, 9 or 12 m) on the FTL — for the stock you buy.
Can it cut bevels and weld preparations?

Yes — the bevel (3D) head, standard on the 12 m FTL 12035, 12050 and 12064 and optional on the other FTL and E-FTL models, tilts the beam so mitred corners, chamfers and weld preparations are cut in the same pass as the holes and copes; the tube arrives at the welding table ready to fit. The seam detector orients welded tube so the seam sits where the drawing puts it.
What about software?

The CNC imports STEP / IGES solid models of the tube parts, unfolds them onto the profile, nests them along the bar to use the remnant and writes the program — with the cutting database for the material and seam detection to orient welded tube. Offline programming on a PC is standard on both lines.
Floor space and power?

A 23 ft (7 m) machine needs about 65 ft (20 m) of length including the loader and unloader; a 40 ft (12 m) machine about 100 ft (30 m). 600 V 3-phase with the supplied transformer or 480 V, a chiller (included), assist gas and a dust collector. We lay the machine out for your building before you order.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: NovoTech double-column band saws
pages.desc: Value-line twin-column band saws: semi-automatic TBK-4228, TGK and GZ gantry saws, automatic TBK-4228B and CNC BS-500G / 500GT / 850G. Specs in inches.
pages.intro: Twin-column saws at value-line prices: the bow travels vertically on two columns, so the cut stays square in solid bar, blocks and bundles. The TBK-4228 and the 45° miter (mitre) TBK-4228A are the semi-automatics, the TBK-4228B the automatic; the TGK-4235 and 4240 add gear drive and hydraulic blade tension; the BS-500G, 500GT and 850G are CNC production saws with servo feeding and stepless blade speed; the GZ4250/70 and GZ4260/120 are gantry saws for plate up to 47-1/4″ wide. Known as double column, twin-column or dual column metal bandsaws, these horizontal band saw machines are the industrial choice for heavy solids, bundles and plate.
points: Twin-column guidance for square cuts in heavy stock
Semi-automatic and fully automatic models listed separately, smallest to largest
Round capacities from Ø11″ (280 mm) to Ø23-5/8″ (600 mm)
faq: Why choose a double-column saw over a pivot saw?

Rigidity and capacity. The bow is guided on two columns, so there is no side load on the blade — cuts stay square in large solids and the blade lasts longer. The GZ4250/70 and GZ4260/120 gantry saws also take plate and bundles a pivot bow cannot.
Which value-line double-column saws are automatic?

The TBK-4228B feeds and cuts automatically with a shuttle vise, stepless blade speed and a chip conveyor; the BS-500G, BS-500GT and BS-850G are CNC production saws with servo feeding, hydraulic vises and stepless blade speed. The TBK-4228, TBK-4228A, TGK-4235, TGK-4240, GZ4250/70 and GZ4260/120 are hydraulic semi-automatics with manual material feed.
Can a value-line double-column saw cut miters?

The TBK-4228A swivels for cuts at 30° and 45° (Ø10-1/4″ and Ø6-3/4″), and the CNC BS-500G and BS-500GT have an automatic rotary bow to 45°. The other value-line double-column models are straight-cut saws.
What voltage do these saws run on?
Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V with a CSA-approved electrical panel; 208 V, 240 V or 480 V 3-phase are available on request.

pages.h1: CNC V-grooving machines — horizontal to 20 ft, vertical to 1/4″ plate
pages.desc: CNC V-grooving machines sold in Canada: horizontal 10.5–20 ft tables for sheet to 5/32″, vertical to 13 ft for plate to 1/4″ — sharp zero-radius bends.
pages.intro: A V-grooving machine (sheet grooving or slotting machine) planes a V-shaped channel along the bend line of a sheet, leaving a thin web; the sheet then folds to a sharp, zero-radius outside corner with no springback and no cracking or orange-peel of the finish — the way stainless elevator and door panels, column cladding, signage, appliance fronts and architectural trim are made, and the way thick sheet is bent on a small press brake. NovoTech sells its own value-line CNC V-grooving machines in Canada: the horizontal machines lay the sheet flat on a 10.5 to 20 ft table, the vertical machines stand it against a fixed beam in half the floor space and groove plate to 1/4″. Four-tool servo heads on ball screws, ± 0.01 mm, Taiwan CNC and servos, hydraulic clamping that does not mark the sheet. Installed and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada, with a CSA-approved panel.
points: Horizontal: 7 sizes, 10.5 – 20 ft × 49 – 59″, sheet 0.016″ – 5/32″, four-tool head at 295 ft/min
Vertical: 4 sizes, 10.5 – 13 ft × 49 – 59″, plate to 1/4″, rear feeding, half the footprint
± 0.01 mm positioning, 0.001 mm resolution; hydraulic blank holder; CNC with touchscreen
faq: What is V-grooving for?

Three things. Sharp corners: a press brake leaves an inside radius about equal to the thickness, a grooved sheet folds to a radius near zero, which is what architects, elevator and furniture makers want in stainless and aluminum. Finish: the groove removes most of the thickness so the outer skin bends without stretching — no cracking, no orange peel, no marking of brushed or mirror stainless and pre-painted sheet. Force: a grooved 1/4″ plate bends on a 40-ton (36 t) brake, and long panels bend by hand on a folder.
Horizontal or vertical machine?

The horizontal machine lays the sheet on a table with pneumatic clamps along the edge and the head travels the length — the machine for long panels (to 20 ft), thin sheet and the highest speed, and the one most sign and cladding shops buy. The vertical machine clamps the sheet upright against a fixed beam and feeds it from the rear: the bed cannot deflect, it grooves plate to 1/4″ and it takes half the floor space, at the cost of the 13 ft maximum length.
What sheet can it groove?

Stainless, mild steel, aluminum, copper and brass from 0.016″ to 5/32″ on the horizontal machines and to 1/4″ on the vertical; sheet widths of 49 or 59″ and lengths of 10.5, 13, 16 and 20 ft. The groove depth is programmed in the control — typically 60 – 70 % of the thickness for a 90° bend — with the first groove no closer than 5/16″ to the edge.
How is it programmed?

On the touchscreen CNC: enter the sheet thickness, the groove positions (or a pitch and count), the depth and the number of passes, and the machine runs the sheet automatically; the four-tool head takes the groove in several light cuts for a clean V. Programs are stored and recalled; the control runs in inches or millimetres.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Bekamak vertical band saws
pages.desc: Bekamak vertical band saws for metal: the tilting-frame BMSY 460VG, the BMSY 613VT and VB 0814-8 block saws and the fully automatic CROSS 0626VT plate saw.
pages.intro: A vertical band saw for metal cutting runs the blade vertically through the workpiece instead of swinging a bow down onto it, so plates, blocks and billets can be sliced along their length or cross-cut flat on a table. Bekamak builds four: the BMSY 460VG, a semi-automatic saw whose frame tilts 60° both ways for miter cuts in Ø18″ stock; the BMSY 613VT, which slices 23-5/8″ × 23-5/8″ sections up to 51″ long from blocks and plates on a servo cutting feed; the VB 0814-8 block-cutting machine for 32″ × 55″ blocks of 40,000 kg over a 26 ft cut; and the fully automatic CROSS 0626VT, which feeds and cuts plates up to 23-5/8″ × 102″ in tool steel, titanium and Inconel. CSA-approved panels, parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada. If you are looking for a vertical band saw for metal cutting or a vertical bandsaw for plate, blocks and contour work, these are the machines NovoTech sells and supports in Canada.
points: Semi-automatic: BMSY 460VG tilting-frame miter saw, BMSY 613VT and VB 0814-8 block saws
Fully automatic: CROSS 0626VT plate saw with automatic feed, 23-5/8″ × 102″
Sections from Ø18″ (460 mm) to 32″ × 55″ blocks and 102″ wide plate
faq: When is a vertical band saw better than a horizontal one?

When the workpiece is a plate, slab or block rather than a bar: a horizontal saw clamps a bar and drops the bow through it, while a vertical saw passes the blade along a workpiece lying flat on a table — slicing a block into plates, trimming a slab or cutting a long plate to width. Tool steel, titanium and nickel alloys are usually cut this way.
What does the BMSY 460VG cut?

Round, square and rectangular stock up to Ø18″ / 28″ × 18″ (460 / 710 × 460 mm), straight or at a miter: the whole frame tilts up to 60° to either side under power, with the hydraulic vise and automatic return of a semi-automatic saw.
How long a cut can the block saws make?
The BMSY 613VT travels 51″ (1300 mm) along a 23-5/8″ × 23-5/8″ block; the VB 0814-8 has 26 ft (8 m) of cutting travel on a table rated 40,000 kg for blocks up to 32″ × 55″ (820 × 1400 mm).
What is automatic on the CROSS 0626VT?

Feeding and cutting: a feeder and servo positioning move the plate to the programmed length for each cut, the vises clamp across the full 102″ (2600 mm) width and the blade cuts, piece after piece, down to a minimum cut of 1-3/16″ (30 mm) in automatic mode.
What voltage do these saws run on?
Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V with a CSA-approved electrical panel; 208 V, 240 V or 480 V 3-phase are available on request.

pages.h1: CNC machining centers — vertical (VMC) and double-column, BBT40/50
pages.desc: Vertical machining centers (VMC) for sale in Canada: Dener TMC, BBT40, 10,000 rpm, 24 tools, X 33.5 – 63″, and TDC double-column machining centers with BBT50.
pages.intro: A machining centre mills, drills, bores and taps prismatic parts under CNC and changes its own tools from a magazine, so a part that once went from the mill to the drill press to the tapping arm is finished in one setup. NovoTech sells Dener's machining centres in Canada, built in Kayseri, Turkey: the TMC vertical machining centres (VMC) in five sizes, from the TMC 850 with 33.5 × 20.1 × 22″ (850 × 510 × 560 mm) travels to the TMC 1600 with 63 × 27.6 × 27.6″ (1,600 × 700 × 700 mm), all with a direct-drive BBT40 spindle at 10,000 rpm, a 24-tool arm changer and rapids of 1,417 in/min (36 m/min); and the TDC double-column (gantry) machining centres for long, wide and heavy parts — 82.7 to 161.4″ (2,100 – 4,100 mm) of X travel, 55 to 82.7″ between the columns, tables to 157.5 × 70.9″ for 26,455 lb (12,000 kg) and a BBT50 spindle with through-spindle coolant. Mitsubishi M80A control with Navi-Mill conversational programming as standard, Fanuc to order. Installed and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: TDC 2112 – 4120: X 82.7 – 161.4″, 55 – 82.7″ between the columns, tables to 157.5 × 70.9″ and 26,455 lb, BBT50, 24 or 40 tools
Mitsubishi M80A with Navi-Mill (Fanuc optional); C3 ballscrews, roller guides, ±0.00016″ positioning on the TMC
faq: Vertical or double-column machining centre?

A vertical machining centre carries the part on a table that moves in X and Y under a spindle on a single column — the standard machine for brackets, housings, plates and moulds up to the size of its table — 39 × 20″ to 69 × 28″ on the TMC. A double-column machine puts the spindle on a cross rail between two columns over a long table: it takes parts far wider and heavier than a vertical's single column could, keeps its rigidity over the whole width, and machines machine bases, plates, frames and large moulds. The TMC runs to 63 × 27.6″ of travel and 2,646 lb on the table; the TDC starts at 82.7 × 48″ and carries up to 26,455 lb.
BBT40, BBT50 — will my CAT40 holders fit?

BBT is BT with the BIG-PLUS dual-contact face: the holder seats on the taper and on the spindle face at once, which stiffens the tool. Standard BT holders fit a BBT spindle too. CAT40 holders do not: the taper is the same 7/24 but the flange and the pull stud are different, so plan for BT or BBT holders — we quote a starter set with the machine. BBT50 carries larger face mills and boring bars and takes heavier cuts than BBT40.
How accurate are they?

Dener specifies ±0.004 mm (±0.00016″) positioning and ±0.002 mm repeatability per 300 mm on the TMC (±0.005 mm on the TMC 1600), and ±0.008 / ±0.004 mm on the TDC. Double-nut C3 ballscrews coupled directly to the servo motors, roller linear guides, spindle cooling and stress-relieved Meehanite castings keep it there; linear scales are an option for closed-loop positioning.
Which control, and how are they programmed?

The Mitsubishi M80A with a 15″ touchscreen is standard, with Navi-Mill conversational programming for simple parts at the machine; Fanuc 0i-MF is an option. Both run ISO G-code from any CAM system, with rigid tapping, canned cycles and 4th-axis control for the optional rotary table.
Which options are worth it?

Through-spindle coolant at 435 psi (30 bar) for deep drilling and pocketing (standard on the TDC); a 12,000 or 15,000 rpm spindle if you cut mostly aluminum; a tool setter and workpiece probe to cut setup time; a CNC rotary table for four-sided work; and linear scales for the tightest work. The chip conveyor, chip wash-down, oil skimmer and spindle cooling are standard.
What foundation, power and air do they need?

The TMC machines need 32 kVA (43 kVA for the 1300 and 1600), 73 – 87 psi of shop air and a level reinforced-concrete floor; the TDC machines, at 21 to 40 tonnes, sit on a foundation built to Dener's drawing. We send the drawings and the floor-space plan with the quote.
Do you deliver, install and train in Canada?

Yes. Machines ship from Kayseri to Mississauga, ON, Canada; NovoTech unloads, levels and commissions the machine, checks the geometry, trains your operators and programmers on the control and helps with the first parts. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, a 1-year warranty and parts and service from Mississauga. Ask for the foundation drawing and the power and air requirements before the machine ships.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: NovoTech vertical metal band saws
pages.desc: Value-line vertical metal band saws VS-300 to VS-585: 12″ to 23″ throat, tilting table, inverter blade speed and a built-in blade welder for contour cuts.
pages.intro: Vertical band saws for the tool room, fabrication and maintenance shop: the blade runs vertically and the workpiece — sheet, plate, bar, profiles, plastics or wood — is pushed across the table, so the saw cuts contours, radii, slots and straight lines that a horizontal saw cannot. The VS series has four sizes from a 12-1/4″ to a 23″ throat, a table that tilts 45° right (30° on the two larger saws) and 15° left, stepless blade speed from an inverter, and a blade welder with annealer and grinder on the column: cut the blade, thread it through a drilled hole, weld it and saw an internal cut-out. For slicing blocks and plate on a production line see the premium vertical saws. If you are looking for a vertical band saw for metal cutting or a vertical bandsaw for plate, blocks and contour work, these are the machines NovoTech sells and supports in Canada.
points: Built-in blade welder, annealer and grinder for internal cut-outs
Tilting table, inverter blade speed to 1,076 ft/min, table gauge and work light
faq: What is the throat of a vertical band saw?

The width from the blade to the column (how wide a part can pass beside the blade) and the height under the upper blade guide (how thick a part can be). The VS-300 takes 12-1/4″ × 7-1/4″ (310 × 185 mm), the VS-400 15-3/4″ × 11-1/4″, the VS-500 19-3/4″ × 12-1/4″ and the VS-585 23″ × 13-1/4″ (585 × 336 mm).
What is the blade welder for?

Internal cut-outs and blade repair. Drill a hole in the part, cut the blade, thread it through the hole and weld it on the saw's own butt welder, anneal the weld and grind it flush with the built-in grinder — then saw the inside contour. The same welder makes blades from coil stock and repairs a broken blade in a few minutes.
Can these saws cut steel?

Yes — mild steel, stainless, tool steel in thin sections, aluminum, copper and brass, as well as plastics and wood: the inverter sets the blade speed from about 33 – 49 ft/min for steel to 590 – 1,076 ft/min for aluminum and non-metals. The chart on the saw gives the speed and tooth pitch for each material and thickness.
Vertical band saw or horizontal band saw?

A horizontal saw clamps a bar and cuts it to length, unattended; a vertical saw is a hand-fed machine for shapes — curves, slots, angles, notches and internal cut-outs in sheet and plate. Most shops that cut both have one of each.
What voltage do these saws run on?
Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V with a CSA-approved electrical panel; 208 V, 240 V or 480 V 3-phase are available on request.

pages.h1: Welding automation — positioners, turning rolls, manipulators, tables
pages.desc: Welding automation sold, installed and supported in Canada: welding positioners 22 – 44,092 lb, turning rolls to 220,462 lb, column and boom, tables.
pages.intro: Welding automation moves the work, not the welder: the part turns under a fixed torch at the welding speed, so round and long welds are laid in one continuous pass in the flat position, by hand or with an automatic welding head. NovoTech sells four kinds in Canada, each on its own page: welding positioners — tilting turntables, rotary tables, lift positioners and headstock and tailstock positioners from 22 to 44,092 lb; welding turning rolls — light, adjustable and self-aligning rolls for pipe, tanks and vessels from Ø0.8 to 216.5″ and 2,205 to 220,462 lb per set, with pipe and fit-up rotators and pipe stands; column and boom manipulators that carry the welding head over the seam, 31.5 to 275.6″ of lift; and welding tables and downdraft tables. The premium-line WP positioners are built in Turkey, the value line in China. Below, the four kinds compared, every family by line, the buying guide and the questions we get asked; every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Welding positioners: light, premium-line WP, heavy, rotary-table and lift positioners, 22 – 44,092 lb
Welding turning rolls: self-aligning and adjustable rolls to 220,462 lb per set, pipe and fit-up rotators, pipe stands
Column and boom manipulators 31.5 – 275.6″ lift · welding and downdraft tables
faq: Which welding automation do I need?

By the part. Round parts that fit on a table — flanges, hubs, pipe spools, tank heads — go on a positioner, tilted to bring the joint flat. Long round parts — pipe, tank shells, pressure vessels — turn on turning rolls. Long seams and circumferential seams welded by an automatic head need a column and boom over the part, usually with turning rolls under it. Fit-up, tacking and small parts go on a welding table. Send us the part and the welds and we size the set.
Positioner or turning rolls?

A positioner holds the part on a turntable or in a chuck and turns it about its own axis, tilted to bring the joint to the flat position: the machine for flanges, short pipe spools, hubs and parts up to about the size of the table. Turning rolls carry a long round part — pipe, a tank shell, a pressure vessel — on wheels and turn it under the torch: the machine for long and heavy work. Long pipe in a positioner chuck needs an outboard support stand at the far end.
What does a column and boom do?

It holds the welding head on a boom that moves up and down the column and in and out over the part, and feeds it along the seam at the welding speed: longitudinal seams of tanks and pipe and, with turning rolls under the part, circumferential seams inside and outside. The column turns ±180° and, on the travelling versions, the carriage runs on rails along the work.
How do I size a positioner for my part?

By the weight and where its centre of gravity sits. The rating is for the centre of gravity close to the table centre and face: the further it is from the axis (an off-centre bracket) or from the table (a tall part), the more torque the drive and the tilt need. The tables give the limits — the HB positioners up to 3.9 – 9.8″ off the axis and 5.9 – 23.6″ above the table, the heavy WP positioners 12″ and 12″. For off-centre or tall parts choose the next size up, and send us a sketch with the weight.
Premium-line or value-line?

The WP 100 and WP 300 tilting positioners are built in Turkey for NovoTech's premium line and run on single-phase 220 V with a foot pedal. The other positioners, the turning rolls, the column and boom manipulators, the pipe stands and the tables are NovoTech's value line, built in China to NovoTech's specification — with the same CSA-approved panel, 1-year warranty and parts and support in Canada.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Welding positioners — tilting, rotary and lift, 22 to 44,092 lb
pages.desc: Welding positioners from 22 to 44,092 lb sold and supported in Canada: benchtop, tilting, heavy, rotary-table, lift and headstock positioners.
pages.intro: A welding positioner holds the part on a turntable and turns it under the torch at a steady, adjustable speed, so a round weld on a flange, pipe-to-plate joint, hub, tank head or wheel is laid in one continuous pass in the flat position — no stopping, repositioning and restarting around the part, and a more even bead whether the torch is held by hand or clamped in a holder. Tilting the table brings the joint to the best angle for the torch. NovoTech has positioners for every size of part, all on this page, small to large: light and benchtop positioners from 22 to 247 lb, with chucks, hollow bores and foot pedals; the premium-line WP 100 and WP 300 tilting positioners, built in Turkey, 220 and 661 lb on single-phase power; value-line tilting positioners from 485 to 2,646 lb; HBT rotary welding tables and HBJ lift positioners that also adjust in height, to 44,092 lb; heavy tilting positioners from 3,307 to 44,092 lb with motorized tilt; headstock and tailstock, L-type and hydraulic positioners built to order; and the chucks and torch holders that go on them. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. Parts, installation and service from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Light and benchtop positioners 22 – 247 lb · premium-line WP 100 and WP 300 tilting positioners, 220 and 661 lb, single-phase
Tilting positioners to 2,646 lb · heavy HB and WP positioners to 44,092 lb with motorized tilt
HBT rotary welding tables and HBJ lift positioners to 44,092 lb · headstock and tailstock positioners built to order
faq: What does a welding positioner do?

It turns the part under a stationary torch at a set speed, so a circumferential weld is made in one pass in the flat position — the easiest position to weld and the one that gives the most even bead. The welder no longer walks around the part or stops to reposition it; with the torch in a holder the travel speed is as steady as the table, which makes repeat parts faster and more uniform.
How do I size a positioner for my part?

By the weight and where its centre of gravity sits. The rating is for the centre of gravity close to the table centre and face: the further it is from the axis (an off-centre bracket) or from the table (a tall part), the more torque the drive and the tilt need. The tables give the limits — the HB positioners up to 3.9 – 9.8″ off the axis and 5.9 – 23.6″ above the table, the heavy WP positioners 12″ and 12″. For off-centre or tall parts choose the next size up, and send us a sketch with the weight.
How fast should the table turn?

Table speed (rpm) = travel speed ÷ (π × weld diameter). A MIG weld at 20 in/min around a Ø6″ flange needs about 1.1 rpm; a submerged-arc weld at 20 in/min on a Ø60″ tank head about 0.1 rpm. Check that the positioner's speed range covers your smallest and largest weld diameters: the light positioners turn up to 8 – 18 rpm, the heavy ones as slowly as 0.03 rpm.
Tilting positioner, rotary table, lift or headstock positioner?

A tilting positioner turns and tilts the part on a table — the most versatile. A rotary welding table (HBT) only turns, for parts that stand upright: tanks, drums, rings and hubs. A lift positioner (HBJ) also adjusts the table height, so the work comes to the welder or the welding head. Headstock and tailstock positioners turn long parts — beams, columns, frames and shafts — about their own length.
What can be mounted on the turntable?

The tables are T-slotted for clamps, angle plates and fixtures. A self-centring 3-jaw welding chuck holds pipe, shafts and round parts on centre — the WPC chucks on this page grip from Ø0.4″ inside to Ø15″ outside — and a torch holder on an adjustable arm keeps the torch in one place while the part turns.
Premium-line or value-line?

The WP 100 and WP 300 tilting positioners are built in Turkey for NovoTech's premium line and run on single-phase 220 V with a foot pedal. The other positioners, the turning rolls, the column and boom manipulators, the pipe stands and the tables are NovoTech's value line, built in China to NovoTech's specification — with the same CSA-approved panel, 1-year warranty and parts and support in Canada.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Welding tables and downdraft tables — fixture and grinding tables
pages.desc: Welding tables and downdraft tables sold in Canada: a mobile 36 × 24″ fixture table with a 2″ hole grid, and MDT downdraft tables drawing 1,350 – 3,700 CFM.
pages.intro: A welding table holds the parts square and flat for fit-up, tacking and welding; a downdraft table draws grinding dust, sanding dust and welding fumes down through its perforated top before they reach the operator. NovoTech's value line, built in China, has both on this page: the WT-36X24 mobile fixture table — a 36 × 24 × 5/8″ top flat to 0.006″ with 216 holes of 5/8″ on a 2″ grid for clamps and fixtures, reversible and nitrided against spatter, on casters with a tube and pipe notcher — and the MDT downdraft tables: the MDT-4840 and MDT-6137 drawing 1,350 CFM through three filter stages to HEPA, and the MDT-6022 grinding table moving 3,700 CFM through four panel filters. Each has its full specification table and photos. Parts and service from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: WT-36X24 fixture table: 36 × 24 × 5/8″, flat to 0.006″, 216 holes of 5/8″ on a 2″ grid, 1,500 lb
MDT-4840 and MDT-6137 downdraft tables: 1,350 CFM, three-stage filtration to HEPA H13
MDT-6022 grinding table: 61 × 20″, 3,700 CFM through four panel filters
faq: What is a downdraft table for?

Grinding, sanding and welding small parts without the dust and fumes rising past the operator's face: a fan under the perforated top pulls the air down through the filters. The MDT-4840 and MDT-6137 filter it in three stages to HEPA H13, the MDT-4840 with compressed-air cleaning of its cartridges; the MDT-6022 moves 3,700 CFM for heavy grinding.
Why a fixture table with a hole grid?

The 5/8″ holes on a 2″ grid take standard clamps, stops and squares, so a part is set up square and repeatable in minutes and the setup can be rebuilt for the next batch. The top is flat to 0.006″, reversible and nitrided, so spatter does not stick and the surface stays true.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Welding turning rolls — welding and pipe rotators, 2,205 to 220,462 lb
pages.desc: Welding turning rolls from 2,205 to 220,462 lb per set, sold in Canada: light, adjustable and self-aligning rotators, fit-up rotators and pipe stands.
pages.intro: Welding turning rolls (welding rotators, tank turning rolls) carry a long round part — pipe, a tank shell, a pressure vessel — on two sets of wheels and turn it under a fixed torch at the welding speed: one section has the motor and the control, the other is an idler placed to suit the length of the part. NovoTech has them all on this page, small to large: light turning rolls from 2,205 lb per set for pipe and small vessels; DKG bolt-adjustable and DSK lead-screw adjustable rolls from 4,409 to 220,462 lb, whose wheel spacing is set to the diameter; DZG self-aligning rolls from 11,023 to 220,462 lb, whose wheel pairs swing to the vessel by themselves; GGLJ pinch-type pipe rotators for pipe segments and flanges and hydraulic fit-up rotators that line up two shell sections for the joint; and pipe stands and supports for fit-up and outboard support. Polyurethane wheels; surface speeds of 3.9 – 39.4 in/min set by VFD on the larger rolls. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. Parts, installation and service from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Light DZG and TRS turning rolls, 2,205 – 11,023 lb per set, work from Ø0.8″
DKG bolt-adjustable and DSK lead-screw rolls 4,409 – 220,462 lb · DZG self-aligning rolls 11,023 – 220,462 lb, work to Ø216.5″
GGLJ pinch-type pipe rotators, hydraulic fit-up rotators and pipe stands to 19,800 lb
faq: Self-aligning or adjustable turning rolls?

Self-aligning rolls (DZG) swing their wheel pairs to the diameter by themselves, so vessels of different diameters go on without resetting — the choice when diameters change often. Adjustable (conventional) rolls hold their wheels at a set spacing: the DKG moves the wheel blocks to bolt positions, the DSK sets them with a lead screw and hand wheel. They cost less and suit work that stays in one diameter range for a while.
How are turning rolls rated?

By the weight per set — one drive and one idler section — and by the diameter range the wheels carry. Add the weight of the part and any fixtures, and leave a margin for out-of-round shells and off-centre nozzles; very long work can rest on two idler sections beside the drive.
How fast do the rolls turn the work?

Turning rolls are set by the surface speed of the work, which is the travel speed of the weld: the adjustable and self-aligning rolls run 3.9 – 39.4 in/min (6 – 60 m/h) by VFD, for manual welding and submerged-arc heads; the light DZG rolls reach 43 – 75 in/min and the TRS rolls 56 – 143 in/min.
What does a fit-up rotator do?

It brings two shell sections into line before they are welded: two hydraulic swing-arm lifting rollers raise, lower and shift each section slightly until the edges meet evenly, then the drive roller turns both for welding. The rollers move on rails to suit the diameter.
Positioner or turning rolls?

A positioner holds the part on a turntable or in a chuck and turns it about its own axis, tilted to bring the joint to the flat position: the machine for flanges, short pipe spools, hubs and parts up to about the size of the table. Turning rolls carry a long round part — pipe, a tank shell, a pressure vessel — on wheels and turn it under the torch: the machine for long and heavy work. Long pipe in a positioner chuck needs an outboard support stand at the far end.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Window assembly machines — corner crimpers, screwing and conveyors
pages.desc: A hydraulic corner crimper for aluminum frames, pneumatic screwing and sash assembly machines, portable notching and copy milling machines and conveyors.
pages.intro: Once the profiles are cut and machined, the frames are put together: aluminum corners are crimped over cleats, reinforcements and hardware are screwed in, and the sashes are fitted with their hardware. NovoTech supplies the machines for that from Plastmak, built in Bursa, Turkey: the SC 902 hydraulic corner crimper with 4 + 4 knives; single and double-head pneumatic screwing machines and a sash assembly machine that fits a double-opening sash's hardware in 3.5 minutes; the SC 221 and SC 551 portable notching and copy milling machines; and the SC 1000 digital measuring conveyor with the SC 1001 – 1003 conveyors that carry profiles to and from every machine. Supplied with a CSA-approved panel, installed and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: SC 902 hydraulic corner crimper: 4 + 4 knives, aluminum profiles to 5-1/8″ high
Single and double-head screwing machines · sash assembly machine, double sash in 3.5 min
SC 221 · SC 551 portable machines · SC 1000 measuring conveyor 9′ 10″, ±.020″
faq: How is an aluminum frame joined?

Aluminum profiles are not welded: a cleat (corner bracket) is pushed into the mitred ends, and the crimper drives knives into the profile walls over the cleat so they lock onto it. The SC 902 does it hydraulically with four knives a side, set to the profile with millimetre scales, while a pneumatic miter wedge holds the corner square.
What does the sash assembly machine do?

It fits the hardware of single and double-opening sashes without moulds or templates: it measures the sash, drills with a three-arm unit, mills the espagnolette groove and screws the hardware in, aligned by laser — 3.5 minutes on average for a double-opening window.
Why a digital measuring conveyor?

It sets the saw's length stop for you: type the length on the SC 1000's touch screen and the stop moves there to ±.020″ (±0.5 mm), then retracts at one push so the cut piece comes out. No tape and no reading errors, and it fits any of the saws.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Window production lines — 40 to 220 PVC or aluminum windows a shift
pages.desc: Matched PVC and aluminum window production groups — single-head, double-head and aluminum sets and a full PVC workshop — with power, air and weight.
pages.intro: A window shop is a flow of machines, and its output is set by the slowest of them. Plastmak plans production groups in which every step keeps pace with the others, and NovoTech supplies four of them: a PVC single-head group (six machines, 40 – 60 windows in an 8-hour shift), a PVC double-head group (six machines, 80 – 120 windows), an aluminum double-head group (four machines, 80 – 120 windows) and a complete PVC workshop laid out as a loop (seven machines, 200 – 220 windows). Each table lists the machines with their capacity, power, air and weight, and the totals for the group. Machines can be swapped or added to suit your profiles and output; we plan the layout, install the line and train your team from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: PVC single-head group: 6 machines, 40 – 60 windows a shift
PVC double-head and aluminum double-head groups: 80 – 120 windows a shift
Complete PVC workshop with compressor: 7 machines, 200 – 220 windows a shift
faq: How many windows will a group make?

Plastmak's figures for an 8-hour shift are 40 – 60 windows for the PVC single-head group, 80 – 120 for the PVC and aluminum double-head groups and 200 – 220 for the complete workshop. The real number depends on window sizes and types, the profile system and how many people run the line — tell us your mix and we will estimate it.
Can I start small and grow?

Yes. The groups share machines: the copy router, end mill, bead saw and corner cleaner of the single-head group stay when a double-head saw and welder are added, and a CNC corner cleaner, a 3-axis CNC or a 4-corner welder can follow later.
What do I need on site?

Three-phase power for the installed load in each table, compressed air at 87 – 116 psi (6 – 8 bar) for the consumption listed — the workshop group includes a 130 gal (500 l) compressor — and floor space for the machines in a loop, with room for 21-ft profiles. We provide a layout before delivery.

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. pages.h1: CNC wire bending machines — 3D wire benders from the coil, to Ø9/16″
pages.desc: 3D CNC wire benders fed from the coil, sold in Canada: decoiler, straightener, servo feed and a 1,000°/s bending head — baskets, racks, frames, hooks.
pages.intro: A CNC wire bending machine turns wire from the coil into a finished part in one pass: the decoiler pays off the wire, the straightener takes out the coil set, a servo feeder pushes the programmed length through the bending head, the head bends, rotates to the next plane and bends again, and a cutter drops the part — baskets, display racks, shelf supports, chair and furniture frames, handles, hooks, springs and exhaust hangers, with no jigs and no bending by hand. NovoTech sells the CSM WB 10-A and WB 14-A, built in Tainan, Taiwan, by the tube-bender maker CSM: 3D benders for Ø5/32″ to Ø3/8″ and Ø1/4″ to Ø9/16″ wire, bending at up to 1,000°/s with ±0.01° repeatability, an IPC control with a 15″ touch-screen that simulates the part in 3D before the first bend, and a concentric tool design and customised work-head that keep complex shapes free of interference. With a CSM EF end former they make a complete exhaust-hanger line. Installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada, with a CSA-approved panel.
points: WB 10-A: Ø5/32″ – 3/8″ wire at 1,000°/s · WB 14-A: Ø1/4″ – 9/16″ wire at 600°/s — ±0.01° bending repeatability
From the coil: AC-driven decoiler, hydraulic straightener, servo feed at 164 ft/min (±0.004″), hydraulic cutter
3D: servo work-head rotation at 440°/s, servo tool shift, concentric tools; IPC control with 15″ touch-screen and 3D simulation
faq: What can a CNC wire bender make?

Any part bent from round wire or rod in the capacity range: wire baskets and racks, display and shelf hardware, chair, sofa and bed frames, handles and hooks, springs and clips, automotive seat and exhaust-hanger wire, fencing and agricultural parts. The machine bends in three dimensions, so a part with bends in several planes comes off finished and cut to length.
WB 10-A or WB 14-A?

By the wire. The WB 10-A bends Ø5/32″ to Ø3/8″ (4 – 10 mm) at 1,000°/s — the faster machine for furniture, display and basket wire. The WB 14-A takes Ø1/4″ to Ø9/16″ (6 – 14 mm) at 600°/s — heavier frames, rod, seat and exhaust-hanger wire. Both feed at 164 ft/min, rotate the head at 440°/s and repeat to ±0.01°; base, power and footprint are the same.
2D or 3D — what does the rotating work-head do?

A 2D bender bends in one plane only. On the WB the work-head itself rotates around the wire under servo control, so after one bend the next can be made in any other plane — the wire never has to be turned by hand, and three-dimensional parts come off in one cycle. The concentric tool design and the customised work-head keep the head clear of the part as it grows.
How is a new part programmed?

On the IPC control with its 15″ touch-screen: enter the lengths, bend angles and rotation angles of the part, and the control shows it in 3D, checks the sequence for interference and runs it. Programs are stored and reloaded for the next batch; no jigs or fixtures have to be built for a new part.
Can it work with an end former?

Yes — the WB 14-A with a CSM EF50 end former makes complete exhaust hangers: the wire is bent and cut and the ends are formed in one line. The videos below show the line in production; the EF end formers are on our tube end forming page.
What voltage do these machines run on?

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.

pages.h1: Woodworking machinery — jointers, planers, table saws and band saws
pages.desc: Woodworking machines in Canada: jointers, thickness planers, jointer-planers, 10″ table saws, band saws, slot boring machines, a lathe and a dust collector.
pages.intro: Woodworking machines for the cabinet shop, the joinery, the school shop and the serious home workshop. NovoTech's value-line woodworking machinery is built in China to our specification: 6″ and 8″ jointers and 15″ and 20″ thickness planers with spiral carbide cutterheads, and jointer-planers to 16″; 10″ cabinet table saws with 30″ and 52″ of rip, with touch-screen blade height and angle on the S models; 14″ and 18″ band saws for resawing; slot boring and horizontal boring machines; a 12 × 16″ wood lathe; and a dust collector — 20 models, with parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.
points: Jointers 6 – 8″ and thickness planers 15 – 20″ with spiral carbide cutterheads; jointer-planers 10 – 16″
WTS10 10″ cabinet table saws, 30″ and 52″ rip, touch-screen S models; TBS 14″ and 18″ band saws
MGX slot boring machines, WM-01 horizontal boring machine, TL-406 lathe, DC900 dust collector
faq: Jointer, thickness planer or jointer-planer — what do I need?

A jointer flattens one face of a rough board and squares an edge to it; a thickness planer then makes the other face parallel and brings the board to thickness. You need both to mill rough lumber. A jointer-planer (TDM) does both jobs with one cutterblock in the space of one machine — the tables lift for thicknessing — at the cost of a changeover between the two; separate machines are faster when both run all day.
Spiral carbide cutterhead or straight knives?

A spiral (helical) cutterhead has many small carbide inserts set in a spiral: it cuts with a shearing action, so it is quieter, leaves a cleaner surface on figured and interlocked grain and tears out less, and a chipped insert is turned to a fresh edge in a minute instead of a set of knives reground and reset. Straight knives cost less to buy and are fine for softwood and general work. The WJ jointers and WJP planers have spiral carbide heads; the WJ10X40 has straight knives.
Which table saw — 30″ or 52″ rip, hand wheels or touch screen?

The rip capacity is the widest cut to the right of the blade: 30″ is enough for solid wood and for cutting a sheet of plywood to 30″ parts; 52″ cuts a 4 × 8 sheet to any width, which a cabinet shop needs. All WTS10 saws take a 10″ blade with 3-3/8″ of cut at 90°; on the S models the blade height and angle are typed on a touch screen and shown digitally — faster and repeatable set-ups for production.
Do I need a dust collector?

Yes for every planer, jointer and table saw: they make chips faster than a shop vacuum can take them, and fine dust is a health risk. A single-stage collector like the DC900 — 940 CFM, two 4″ inlets — serves one or two machines at a time; keep the hose runs short and connect the machine that is running.

Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
